children.title: Theory-Relative Satisfiability
children.top_down_role: Semantic problem classes distinguished by background theory, quantification, and permitted solver outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: SMT Background Theories
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a background theory semantically as a signature together with an admissible class of structures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SMT background theory is a pair \(T=(\Sigma,\mathcal K_T)\), where \(\Sigma\) is a many-sorted first-order signature and \(\mathcal K_T\) is a class of \(\Sigma\)-structures, equivalently the models of a set of \(\Sigma\)-sentences. For any \(\Sigma\)-formula \(\varphi\) with free variables \(\bar x\), \(\varphi\) is satisfiable modulo \(T\) precisely when there exist \(M\in\mathcal K_T\) and an assignment \(\nu\) to \(\bar x\) such that \(M,\nu\models\varphi\). Logical symbols retain first-order semantics; symbols from \(\Sigma\) receive their interpretations from \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A background theory fixes the allowed structures interpreting nonlogical symbols; an SMT formula is satisfiable when some allowed structure and variable assignment satisfy it.
assumptions_latex: \(\Sigma\) is a many-sorted first-order signature.
\(\mathcal K_T\neq\varnothing\) is a specified class of \(\Sigma\)-structures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sat}_T(\varphi)\iff\exists M\in\mathcal K_T\;\exists\nu\;(M,\nu\models\varphi)\).

notation.meaning: Class of structures admitted by the theory.
Formula satisfaction in structure M under assignment ν.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No cited source is supplied. Also, an arbitrary class of Σ-structures is not necessarily the model class of any set of Σ-sentences, so the claimed equivalence requires an elementary-class assumption; requiring the class to be nonempty also excludes inconsistent theories.

children.title: Ground SMT Instances
children.top_down_role: Closed SMT instances whose theory terms contain no variables requiring quantification.

knowledge_statements.title: Ground SMT Instances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the standard syntactic meaning of ground: no free or bound variables occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a background theory over signature \(\Sigma\). A ground SMT instance is a quantifier-free \(\Sigma\)-formula \(\varphi\) in which no variable occurs; constant symbols, including fresh constants, may occur. Its decision problem asks whether \(\operatorname{Sat}_T(\varphi)\) holds. Because \(\varphi\) has no free variables, satisfaction requires only a theory model: \(\operatorname{Sat}_T(\varphi)\) holds exactly when some \(M\in\mathcal K_T\) satisfies \(\varphi\). A finite Boolean combination of ground theory atoms is therefore a ground SMT instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A ground SMT instance is a variable-free, quantifier-free Boolean combination of theory atoms, tested for satisfaction in some background-theory model.
assumptions_latex: \(T=(\Sigma,\mathcal K_T)\) is a fixed background theory.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varphi\text{ is ground SMT}\implies\bigl(\operatorname{Sat}_T(\varphi)\iff\exists M\in\mathcal K_T\;(M\models\varphi)\bigr)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is standard and fits the leaf, but no citation or inspectable locator supports it.

children.title: Quantifier-Free SMT Fragments
children.top_down_role: SMT fragments excluding explicit quantifiers while retaining theory-relative satisfiability.

knowledge_statements.title: Quantifier-Free SMT Fragments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies SMT inputs by forbidding quantifiers while permitting free variables or constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a background theory \(T\) over signature \(\Sigma\), the quantifier-free SMT fragment \(\mathrm{QF}(T)\) is the set of finite \(\Sigma\)-formulas constructed from theory atoms using Boolean connectives, with no occurrence of \(\forall\) or \(\exists\). Free variables may occur and are interpreted by an assignment. Thus, for \(\varphi(\bar x)\in\mathrm{QF}(T)\), satisfiability means that some \(T\)-model and some assignment to \(\bar x\) satisfy the formula. Ground SMT instances form the variable-free subclass of \(\mathrm{QF}(T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quantifier-free fragment contains Boolean combinations of theory atoms without quantifiers; free variables are existentially chosen for satisfiability.
assumptions_latex: \(T=(\Sigma,\mathcal K_T)\) is a fixed background theory.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varphi(\bar x)\in\mathrm{QF}(T)\implies\bigl(\operatorname{Sat}_T(\varphi)\iff\exists M\in\mathcal K_T\;\exists\nu\;(M,\nu\models\varphi)\bigr)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement is mathematically plausible and fits the leaf, but the proposed notation and free-variable satisfiability convention require an authoritative SMT source with a specific locator.

children.title: Free-Constant Closure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Treatment of free constants when relating ground instances to quantifier-free input.

knowledge_statements.title: Free-Constant Closure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates free-variable, fresh-constant, and existential-closure presentations of quantifier-free satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi(\bar x)\) be quantifier-free over \(\Sigma\), and let \(\bar c\) be fresh constants of the corresponding sorts. Under satisfiability semantics, free variables are existentially assigned, so the three presentations are equivalent: \[\operatorname{Sat}_T(\varphi(\bar x))\iff\operatorname{Sat}_T(\exists\bar x\,\varphi(\bar x))\iff\operatorname{Sat}_{T^{\bar c}}(\varphi(\bar c)).\] Here \(T^{\bar c}\) conservatively extends the signature with unconstrained constants \(\bar c\). This equivalence concerns satisfiability, not validity; universal closure generally yields a different problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For satisfiability, free variables may equivalently be existentially closed or replaced by fresh unconstrained constants; universal closure is not equivalent.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi(\bar x)\) is quantifier-free over the signature of \(T\).
\(\bar c\) consists of fresh, correctly sorted constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sat}_T(\varphi(\bar x))\iff\operatorname{Sat}_T(\exists\bar x\,\varphi)\iff\operatorname{Sat}_{T^{\bar c}}(\varphi(\bar c))\).

notation.meaning: Conservative signature extension of T by fresh constants.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited. The fresh-constant equivalence is standard, but the models and satisfiability semantics of the signature extension T^{\bar c} must be defined precisely and sourced.

knowledge_statements.title: Quantified SMT Problem Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies theory-relative formulas by quantifier prefix and quantifier-free matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a background theory over a many-sorted signature. A quantified SMT instance is a first-order formula whose matrix is a Boolean combination of theory atoms and whose variables may be bound by \(\forall\) or \(\exists\). In prenex form it has the shape \(Q_1\bar x_1\cdots Q_k\bar x_k\,\psi\), where each \(Q_i\in\{\forall,\exists\}\) and \(\psi\) is quantifier-free. Problem classes are distinguished by the number and order of quantifier blocks, the background theory, and whether remaining free variables are existentially assigned for satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quantified SMT classes consist of theory formulas with quantified variable blocks and a quantifier-free matrix, classified by prefix structure and background theory.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) supplies the admissible structures and interpretations of theory symbols.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi=Q_1\bar x_1\cdots Q_k\bar x_k\,\psi\), with \(Q_i\in\{\forall,\exists\}\) and \(\psi\in\mathrm{QF}(T)\).

notation.meaning: Universal or existential quantifier for block i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this proposed classification. An authoritative reference is needed for treating all quantified theory formulas in prenex form and classifying them by quantifier blocks under the stated free-variable convention.

children.title: Satisfiable Result Regime
children.top_down_role: Successful satisfiability outcomes, including the associated model-facing expectations.

knowledge_statements.title: Satisfiable Result Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the semantic meaning and model certificate associated with an SMT sat result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an SMT input \(\varphi( ar x)\) relative to background theory \(T=(\Sigma,\mathcal K_T)\), the result \(\mathsf{sat}\) is semantically correct exactly when there exist a structure \(M\in\mathcal K_T\) and an assignment \(
u\) to the free variables such that \(M,
u\models\varphi\). The pair \((M,
u)\), or a finite representation sufficient to reconstruct its interpretations on relevant terms, is a satisfiability witness. For a closed formula, the assignment component is unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sat result asserts that an admissible theory model and assignment satisfy the input; such a model-assignment pair is its semantic witness.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\) is well-sorted over the signature of \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathsf{result}_T(\varphi)=\mathsf{sat}\implies\exists M\in\mathcal K_T\;\exists\nu\;(M,\nu\models\varphi)\).

notation.meaning: Solver result claiming satisfiability modulo T.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The semantic characterization of sat is standard, but no source is supplied. The leaf is a result regime, whereas content_kind certificate and the finite-representation claim blend the result semantics with a solver-dependent certificate notion.

children.title: Unsatisfiable Result Regime
children.top_down_role: Successful refutation outcomes, including the associated certificate-facing expectations.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsatisfiable Result Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes an SMT unsat result and the role of a checkable refutation certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an SMT input \(\varphi( ar x)\) relative to \(T=(\Sigma,\mathcal K_T)\), the result \(\mathsf{unsat}\) is semantically correct exactly when no admissible structure and assignment satisfy the input: \[ orall M\in\mathcal K_T\; orall
u\; M,
u
ot\models\varphi.\] Equivalently, the existential closure of \(\varphi\) is inconsistent with \(T\). A proof object is an unsatisfiability certificate when a sound checker can verify that its Boolean and theory inferences derive contradiction from \(T\) together with \(\varphi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unsat result asserts that no background-theory model and assignment satisfy the input; a soundly checkable refutation can certify this claim.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\) is well-sorted over the signature of \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(\mathsf{result}_T(\varphi)=\mathsf{unsat}\implies
eg\exists M\in\mathcal K_T\;\exists
u\;(M,
u\models\varphi)\).

notation.meaning: Solver result claiming unsatisfiability modulo T.
Assignment to the free variables of the input.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The semantic characterization of unsat is standard, but no source is supplied. The result-regime leaf is classified as a certificate and combines semantic unsatisfiability with a solver- and proof-system-dependent certificate claim.

children.title: Unknown Result Regime
children.top_down_role: Inconclusive outcomes caused by unsupported, incomplete, interrupted, or resource-limited reasoning.

knowledge_statements.title: Unknown Result Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Treats unknown as an operational outcome distinct from either semantic truth value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an SMT input \(\varphi\), the result \(\mathsf{unknown}\) means that the solver returns neither a justified \(\mathsf{sat}\) claim nor a justified \(\mathsf{unsat}\) claim. It does not define a third semantic truth value: exactly one of \(\operatorname{Sat}_T(\varphi)\) and \(\neg\operatorname{Sat}_T(\varphi)\) holds under classical semantics. The outcome may arise from incompleteness, unsupported theory features, quantified reasoning, resource limits, or an interrupted search; therefore no satisfiability conclusion follows from \(\mathsf{unknown}\) alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unknown is an operational failure to decide, not a third truth value, and by itself implies neither satisfiability nor unsatisfiability.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\) has ordinary two-valued first-order semantics relative to \(T\).

notation.meaning: Solver outcome making no semantic decision.
Semantic satisfiability of φ modulo T.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between unknown and a semantic truth value fits the leaf and failure-boundary kind, but the standard behavior and listed operational causes require an authoritative SMT standard or solver-interface source with a specific locator.

children.title: Theory-Boolean Abstraction Interface
children.top_down_role: The interface between theory syntax and propositional search.

children.title: Theory Atoms
children.top_down_role: Atomic theory constraints exposed to the Boolean reasoning layer.

knowledge_statements.title: Theory Atoms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines atoms at the interface between theory semantics and Boolean abstraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a first-order signature \(\Sigma\). A theory atom is an atomic \(\Sigma\)-formula, hence either an equality \(t_1=t_2\) between same-sorted terms or an application \(P(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\) of a predicate symbol to correctly sorted terms. It contains no Boolean connective or quantifier as an outer constructor. Relative to a theory model and variable assignment, the atom has a Boolean truth value; Boolean abstraction may therefore associate it with a propositional variable while retaining its theory interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A theory atom is a well-sorted atomic equality or predicate application that can be represented by one propositional variable during Boolean abstraction.
assumptions_latex: \(t_1,\ldots,t_n\) are well-sorted \(\Sigma\)-terms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a\in\operatorname{Atom}(\Sigma)\iff a=(t_1=t_2)\ \text{or}\ a=P(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\).

notation.meaning: Set of atomic formulas over Σ.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and is standard for first-order signatures with equality, but no source or locator is provided.

children.title: Positive Theory Literals
children.top_down_role: Unnegated occurrences of theory atoms in solver-facing representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive Theory Literals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the unnegated polarity of a theory atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a\) be a theory atom. The positive theory literal generated by \(a\) is the literal \(a\) itself, with polarity \(+1\). For every theory model \(M\) and assignment \(
u\), its satisfaction condition is unchanged from that of the underlying atom: \[M,
u\models a\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a^{M,
u}=\mathsf{true}.\] Under a Boolean abstraction \( eta\) assigning a propositional variable \(p_a\) to \(a\), the positive literal is represented by \(p_a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive literal of an atom is the unnegated atom; it is true exactly when that atom is true and maps to a positive Boolean variable.
assumptions_latex: \(a\) is a well-sorted theory atom.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{lit}^{+}(a)=a\quad\text{and}\quad\beta(\operatorname{lit}^{+}(a))=p_a\).

notation.meaning: Positive theory literal generated by a.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polarity definition fits the leaf, but no source supports either the terminology or the stated Boolean-abstraction convention.

children.title: Negative Theory Literals
children.top_down_role: Negated occurrences of theory atoms in solver-facing representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative Theory Literals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the negated polarity of a theory atom under classical semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a\) be a theory atom. The negative theory literal generated by \(a\) is \(
eg a\), with polarity \(-1\). For every theory model \(M\) and assignment \(
u\), \[M,
u\models
eg a\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad M,
u
ot\models a.\] Under a Boolean abstraction \( eta\) assigning propositional variable \(p_a\) to \(a\), the negative theory literal is represented by \(
eg p_a\). The negation changes polarity but does not introduce a distinct underlying theory atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative literal of an atom is its logical negation; it maps to the negation of the same Boolean abstraction variable.
assumptions_latex: \(a\) is a well-sorted theory atom.
The logic uses classical negation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{lit}^{-}(a)=\neg a\quad\text{and}\quad\beta(\operatorname{lit}^{-}(a))=\neg p_a\).

notation.meaning: Negative theory literal generated by a.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The classical negative-literal definition fits the leaf, but no source supports the terminology and Boolean-abstraction convention.

children.title: Atom-Literal Polarity Mapping
children.top_down_role: The representational correspondence between an atom and its positive or negative literal occurrences.

knowledge_statements.title: Atom-Literal Polarity Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the two-polarity representation shared by theory literals and their Boolean abstractions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be a set of theory atoms and let \(\beta:A\to P\) be an injective map to propositional variables. Every theory literal has a unique representation \((a,s)\in A\times\{+1,-1\}\), with decoding \(\delta(a,+1)=a\) and \(\delta(a,-1)=\neg a\). Extend the abstraction by \(\widehat\beta(a,+1)=\beta(a)\) and \(\widehat\beta(a,-1)=\neg\beta(a)\). Then abstraction preserves atom identity and polarity, and complementation acts by \((a,s)\mapsto(a,-s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each theory literal is uniquely an atom plus a polarity; Boolean abstraction preserves both, and negation flips only the polarity.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a set of theory atoms.
\(\beta:A\to P\) is injective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta(a,s)=\begin{cases}a,&s=+1,\\ \neg a,&s=-1,\end{cases}\quad\widehat\beta(a,s)=\begin{cases}\beta(a),&s=+1,\\ \neg\beta(a),&s=-1.\end{cases}\)

notation.meaning: Atom-polarity representation of a theory literal.
Injective Boolean abstraction of theory atoms.
Decoding from atom-polarity pairs to theory literals.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The atom-polarity representation is internally coherent and fits the representation leaf, but it is a chosen formal convention with no cited source or inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Propositional Skeletons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean skeleton of a quantifier-free SMT formula under atom abstraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a quantifier-free formula whose maximal theory atoms form the finite set \(\operatorname{At}(F)\). Choose an injective map \(\alpha:\operatorname{At}(F)\to P\) into propositional variables, and extend \(\alpha\) homomorphically over \(\neg,\wedge,\vee,\rightarrow\), and \(\leftrightarrow\). The propositional skeleton of \(F\) is the propositional formula \(\operatorname{skel}(F)=\alpha(F)\). It retains the Boolean connective structure of \(F\) while treating each distinct theory atom as an indivisible Boolean variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace every distinct theory atom by a unique propositional variable while retaining all Boolean connectives; the resulting formula is the propositional skeleton.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is quantifier-free.
Syntactically identical theory atoms receive the same propositional variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{skel}(F)=\alpha(F)\) is a propositional abstraction of \(F\).

notation.meaning: Set of maximal theory atoms occurring in the formula.
Injective atom-to-variable abstraction extended over Boolean connectives.
Propositional skeleton of the SMT formula.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Propositional Skeletons container and is mathematically plausible, but the record cites no inspectable source or specific locator. Authoritative SMT abstraction support is required before the statement can be reviewed as candidate knowledge.

children.title: Boolean Abstraction Interface
children.top_down_role: The solver-visible boundary that maps theory constraints into propositional search.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Abstraction Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bidirectional correspondence between theory atoms and SAT literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a quantifier-free theory formula \(F\), a Boolean abstraction interface consists of an injective map \(\alpha:\operatorname{At}(F)\to P\) and the partial inverse \(\gamma\) on literals, defined by \(\gamma(\alpha(A))=A\) and \(\gamma(\neg\alpha(A))=\neg A\). Extending \(\alpha\) homomorphically gives a propositional formula \(B=\alpha(F)\). A total Boolean assignment \(\mu\) to \(P\) induces the theory-literal set \(L_\mu=\{\gamma(l):l\text{ is selected by }\mu\}\), which is passed to the theory solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface maps theory atoms to SAT variables and maps assigned SAT literals back to signed theory atoms for consistency checking.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is quantifier-free with finitely many theory atoms.
\(\alpha\) is injective on distinct atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B=\alpha(F)\) and \(L_\mu\) provide the Boolean-to-theory communication representation.

notation.meaning: Concretization map from Boolean literals to signed theory atoms.
Theory literals selected by the Boolean assignment.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the Boolean Abstraction Interface container, and the atom/literal correspondence is plausible. No cited source supports the precise interface, concretization map, or assignment-induced literal set.

children.title: Theory Refinement Interface
children.top_down_role: The boundary through which theory reasoning restricts or redirects propositional search.

knowledge_statements.title: Theory Refinement Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lazy SMT refinement by theory-conflict clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a propositional abstraction \(B=\alpha(F)\). Repeatedly obtain from the SAT solver an assignment \(\mu\models B\), form its concretized theory literals \(L_\mu\), and ask the theory solver whether \(L_\mu\) is \(T\)-satisfiable. If it is, return \(T\)-SAT with \(\mu\) and a compatible theory model. Otherwise obtain a finite \(T\)-inconsistent subset \(C\subseteq L_\mu\), add the refinement clause \(\bigvee_{l\in C}\neg\alpha(l)\) to \(B\), and continue. If the Boolean problem becomes unsatisfiable, return \(T\)-UNSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A SAT assignment is theory-checked; an inconsistent theory core generates a blocking clause, and refinement repeats until a model or Boolean refutation is found.
assumptions_latex: The theory solver decides finite conjunctions of \(T\)-literals.
Every reported conflict set \(C\) is \(T\)-inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a \(T\)-model of \(F\) or exhausts the Boolean search with a sound refutation.

notation.meaning: Theory-inconsistent subset of the current assignment.
Boolean literal corresponding to signed theory literal l.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind correctly captures a lazy SMT theory-refinement interface. A source with a specific DPLL(T) or lazy-SMT algorithm locator is required to validate the stated termination outcome, conflict-clause construction, and solver assumptions.

children.title: Abstraction Fidelity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where propositional candidates fail to represent theory-consistent assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: Abstraction Fidelity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit of satisfiability preservation by an unrefined Boolean skeleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every quantifier-free theory formula \(F\), \(T\)-satisfiability implies propositional satisfiability of \(\alpha(F)\), but the converse can fail. For example, over linear arithmetic, \(F=(x<0)\wedge(x>1)\) has skeleton \(p\wedge q\), which is propositionally satisfiable although \(F\) is theory-inconsistent. For a Boolean assignment \(\mu\models\alpha(F)\), lifting is valid exactly when its selected literal set \(L_\mu\) is \(T\)-satisfiable. Thus Boolean abstraction alone is exact only when every satisfying Boolean assignment under consideration admits such a theory model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boolean satisfiability is only a necessary condition for SMT satisfiability; a Boolean assignment is genuine precisely when its theory literals are jointly consistent.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is quantifier-free.
\(\alpha\) preserves Boolean structure and abstracts theory atoms injectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is }T\text{-satisfiable}\Rightarrow\alpha(F)\text{ is propositionally satisfiable}\), while the reverse implication is not generally valid.

notation.meaning: Theory literals selected by Boolean assignment mu.
Boolean abstractions of the two arithmetic atoms in the example.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the container, and the arithmetic counterexample correctly illustrates loss of fidelity in an unrefined Boolean abstraction. The record nevertheless has no source or locator supporting the exact lifting criterion and boundary statement.

children.title: Signature-Aware Normalization Calculus
children.top_down_role: Representational preprocessing used before individual-theory solving and modular combination.

children.title: Term Flattening
children.top_down_role: Structural reduction of nested theory terms into flatter constraint representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Term Flattening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equisatisfiable flattening of nested ground terms by definitional equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a quantifier-free ground formula \(F\). Process its nonconstant compound subterms bottom-up. For each selected occurrence of \(t=f(t_1,\ldots,t_k)\), introduce a fresh constant \(c_t\), replace that occurrence by \(c_t\), and conjoin the defining equality \(c_t=f(c_{t_1},\ldots,c_{t_k})\), using original constants where no name was introduced. Continue until every theory atom has the required flat form. Output \(F^{\flat}\), the transformed formula conjoined with all definitions. Models of \(F\) extend to models of \(F^{\flat}\), and restricting any model of \(F^{\flat}\) to the original signature yields a model of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested ground terms are named bottom-up and linked by defining equalities, producing a flat formula equisatisfiable with the original over its original signature.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is quantifier-free and ground.
Every introduced constant is fresh and has the sort of its named term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is satisfiable if and only if \(F^{\flat}\) is satisfiable.

notation.meaning: Fresh constant naming compound term t.
Flattened formula together with defining equalities.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Term Flattening, and the bottom-up definitional transformation is plausible for quantifier-free ground formulas. An authoritative locator is needed for the precise model-extension and reduct claims.

children.title: Fresh Term Names
children.top_down_role: Introduced symbols used to reference extracted subterms across normalized constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Fresh Term Names
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Freshness and typing conditions for definitional term names.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) have signature \(\Sigma\), and let \(S\) be a finite set of terms selected for naming. A family \((c_t)_{t\in S}\) is a valid family of fresh term names when \(c_t
otin\Sigma\) for every \(t\in S\), \(c_t
eq c_u\) whenever \(t
eq u\), and \(c_t\) has the same sort as \(t\). Each name is introduced only through its defining constraint \(c_t=t\), with already named proper subterms substituted consistently. Under these conditions, every model of \(F\) has a unique expansion interpreting each \(c_t\) as the value of \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid term name is a new, sort-correct symbol, distinct from every other name, and constrained to equal exactly the term it names.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is interpreted over a many-sorted first-order signature \(\Sigma\).
\(S\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraints \(c_t=t\) define a conservative expansion of every model of \(F\).

notation.meaning: Fresh constant assigned to term t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits Fresh Term Names, and freshness, distinctness, and sort correctness are appropriate conditions. No source is supplied for the stronger unique-expansion and conservative-extension assertions.

children.title: Naming Correspondence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: The semantic correspondence expected between introduced names and their source terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Naming Correspondence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative-extension boundary of flattening by fresh names.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F^{\flat}(\bar c)\) be obtained from \(F\) using fresh names and complete defining equalities. Then, over the original signature, \(F\) is equivalent to \(\exists\bar c\,F^{\flat}(\bar c)\), not generally to the open expanded-signature formula \(F^{\flat}(\bar c)\) without existential interpretation. The correspondence can fail if a name is not fresh, has the wrong sort, or lacks a defining equality. For example, replacing \(f(a)\) by an unconstrained fresh \(c\) in \(f(a)=a\) yields \(c=a\), whose satisfiability need not constrain \(f(a)\) at all.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flattening is conservative only with fresh, sort-correct, fully defined names; its precise equivalence existentially hides the added symbols.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is quantifier-free.
\(\bar c\) lists all introduced names.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\equiv\exists\bar c\,F^{\flat}(\bar c)\) holds under valid naming, and may fail when a naming condition is removed.

notation.meaning: Tuple of all fresh term names.
Flattened formula over the expanded signature.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the container, and existentially hiding added names is the relevant conservative-extension boundary. A specific source is needed to validate the exact equivalence convention for introduced names and the stated failure modes.

knowledge_statements.title: Purification by Theory Signature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Signature-based separation of mixed ground constraints for theory combination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) have disjoint nonlogical signatures \(\Sigma_1\) and \(\Sigma_2\), with equality shared. Given a quantifier-free ground formula, first flatten it. Whenever a \(\Sigma_i\)-term occurs as a proper subterm of a \(\Sigma_j\)-term with \(i\neq j\), replace the alien subterm \(t\) by a fresh variable or constant \(v_t\) of the same sort and add \(v_t=t\) to the component owning \(t\). Repeat until each resulting atom is pure in one signature. Output the pure component constraints together with their shared interface names.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed ground terms are named at signature boundaries until every atom belongs to one component theory, with shared names linking the purified components.
assumptions_latex: \(\Sigma_1\cap\Sigma_2\) contains no nonlogical symbol other than designated shared symbols.
The input is quantifier-free and ground.
Replacement names are fresh and sort-correct.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conjunction of purified components is equisatisfiable with the original formula.

notation.meaning: Nonlogical signature of component theory i.
Fresh interface name replacing alien term t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Purification by Theory Signature. The exact treatment of shared equality, variables versus constants, designated shared symbols, component ownership, and equisatisfiability depends on theory-combination conventions that are not supported by any cited source.

children.title: Clausal Encodings
children.top_down_role: Encodings that expose normalized clause structure to the Boolean reasoning layer.

knowledge_statements.title: Clausal Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitional CNF encoding of Boolean structure in an SMT formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B\) be a propositional formula represented as a directed acyclic syntax graph. Assign a fresh variable \(p_G\) to every nonliteral subformula \(G\). For each connective node, add constant-size CNF clauses expressing \(p_G\leftrightarrow\operatorname{op}(p_{G_1},\ldots,p_{G_k})\); for example, \(p_G\leftrightarrow(p_H\wedge p_K)\) is encoded by \((
eg p_G\vee p_H)\wedge(
eg p_G\vee p_K)\wedge(p_G\vee
eg p_H\vee
eg p_K)\). Conjoin these clauses with the unit clause \(p_B\). The resulting CNF \(C_B\) satisfies \(B\equiv\exists P_{\mathrm{aux}}\,C_B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Tseitin-style encoding names each Boolean subformula and adds local CNF definitions, yielding an existentially equivalent clausal formula.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a finite propositional formula.
All auxiliary variables are fresh.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\equiv\exists P_{\mathrm{aux}}\,C_B\), hence \(B\) and \(C_B\) are equisatisfiable.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits Clausal Encodings, and the displayed conjunction encoding is consistent with a Tseitin-style definitional CNF. No authoritative source or precise locator supports the general encoding and existential-equivalence statement.

children.title: Structure-Preserving Encodings
children.top_down_role: Encodings that retain selected relationships from the source formula structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Preserving Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local definitional encoding that retains the Boolean syntax graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be represented by a Boolean syntax DAG, and introduce one fresh representative \(p_G\) for each distinct nonliteral node \(G\). A structure-preserving encoding is the conjunction of local constraints \(D_G\) satisfying \(D_G\models p_G\leftrightarrow\operatorname{op}(p_{G_1},\ldots,p_{G_k})\), together with the assertion \(p_B\). Every syntax-DAG edge becomes a dependency between representatives, shared subformulas retain a single representative, and any model of \(B\) extends to a model of the encoding by assigning each \(p_G\) the truth value of \(G\). Conversely, every encoding model restricted to original variables satisfies \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each syntax-DAG node receives one representative and a local connective constraint, preserving sharing and allowing models to transfer in both directions.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a finite propositional formula represented as a DAG.
Representative variables are fresh and unique per distinct DAG node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\equiv\exists P_{\mathrm{aux}}\,(p_B\wedge\bigwedge_G D_G)\).

notation.meaning: Local defining constraint for syntax node G.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind is suitable for Structure-Preserving Encodings. A source is required to establish the precise conditions on the local constraints needed for both model extension and projection; mere entailment of each displayed equivalence must be reconciled with those model-transfer claims.

children.title: Encoding Size-Fidelity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Navigation across representation growth, retained structure, solver visibility, plus artifact traceability.

knowledge_statements.title: Encoding Size-Fidelity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear definitional CNF versus potentially exponential equivalent CNF.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Measure input size by the number \(n\) of nodes and edges in a Boolean syntax DAG. A bounded-arity definitional CNF introduces at most one auxiliary variable and a constant number of clauses per connective node, so its size is \(O(n)\); its guarantee is \(B\equiv\exists P_{\mathrm{aux}}\,C_B\), rather than equivalence over the expanded signature without hiding auxiliaries. By contrast, eliminating connectives solely through distributivity can produce an equivalent CNF over only the original variables with exponentially many clauses: \(\bigvee_{i=1}^{m}(x_i\wedge y_i)\) has \(2^m\) clauses in its direct distributed CNF.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Definitional CNF is linear-size but uses existential auxiliary variables; requiring an equivalent CNF over original variables alone can cause exponential growth.
assumptions_latex: Boolean connectives have bounded arity.
Size counts syntax-DAG nodes, edges, literal occurrences, and clauses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Definitional encoding has size \(O(n)\), whereas original-variable equivalent CNF may require \(2^{\Omega(n)}\) size.

notation.meaning: Size of the input Boolean syntax DAG.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind correctly fits the size-fidelity tradeoff container. The linear definitional-CNF bound and especially the claimed exponential lower bound for original-variable equivalent CNF require an authoritative complexity or knowledge-compilation locator; the supplied inventory contains no relevant source.

children.title: Standardized SMT Logic Fragments
children.top_down_role: SMT-LIB-style classifications by quantification, background vocabulary, arithmetic domain, and theory combination.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Logics

knowledge_statements.title: Quantifier-Free Single-Theory Logics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard SMT-LIB-style fragment using one background theory without quantifiers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a many-sorted first-order signature \(\Sigma_T\) and background theory \(T\). A quantifier-free single-theory formula is built from well-sorted \(\Sigma_T\)-terms and atomic predicates or equalities using Boolean connectives, with no occurrence of \(\forall\) or \(\exists\), and with every nonlogical symbol governed by \(T\) or declared as an allowed free symbol of the fragment. Its satisfiability problem asks whether there exists a \(T\)-model and an interpretation of the free constants and functions in which the formula is true. A standardized logic additionally fixes the permitted sorts, symbols, and syntactic restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This fragment contains quantifier-free formulas interpreted in one background theory; a standardized logic fixes its sorts, symbols, and syntax.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a fixed many-sorted first-order theory with signature \(\Sigma_T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fragment consists exactly of well-sorted quantifier-free formulas interpreted modulo \(T\).

notation.meaning: Signature governed by the background theory.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits Quantifier-Free Single-Theory Logics, but the statement blends a general semantic fragment with standardized SMT-LIB logic conventions. A specific SMT-LIB standard section or authoritative SMT reference is required to validate the allowed free symbols and standardized syntax claims.

assumptions_latex: The input uses a many-sorted first-order SMT language with equality.
Each theory signature and its intended class of models are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A sentence belongs to the combined quantifier-free fragment exactly when it is quantifier-free and every nonlogical symbol belongs to the declared union signature.

notation.meaning: quantifier-free formulas over the combined signature

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Version-independent characterization of standardized quantifier-free logics combining multiple background theories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_k\) be theory signatures with compatible shared sorts and symbols, and let \(\Sigma=\bigcup_{i=1}^k\Sigma_i\). The associated quantifier-free combined-theory fragment is \[\mathrm{QF}(\Sigma)=\{\varphi:\varphi\text{ is a well-sorted }\Sigma\text{-formula containing no quantifiers}\}.\] Satisfiability is interpreted in structures satisfying every selected component theory and agreeing on shared symbols. Thus Boolean combinations may contain atoms from several theories, while explicit occurrences of \(\forall\) and \(\exists\) are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quantifier-free combined-theory logic permits Boolean combinations of atoms from several compatible theories, interpreted simultaneously, but contains no explicit quantifiers.
knowledge_statements.title: Quantifier-Free Combined-Theory Logics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and its content kind, and the plain and LaTeX statements agree. However, no citation supports the claimed standardized, version-independent characterization. A specific SMT-LIB logic-catalog locator is required, particularly because compatibility and agreement conditions for overlapping component signatures are not fully formalized.

assumptions_latex: The language is many-sorted first-order logic with equality.
The selected standardized logic fixes a signature and background theory.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A well-sorted sentence is in the quantified logic precisely when its signature, operators, and quantifier structure satisfy that logic's declared restrictions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General semantic characterization; individual named logics may impose additional syntactic restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a standardized logic \(L\), let \(\Sigma_L\) be its permitted signature and \(T_L\) its background theory. Its quantified fragment \(\mathrm{Form}(L)\) consists of the well-sorted \(\Sigma_L\)-formulas admitted by the logic declaration, including formulas formed with \(\forall\) or \(\exists\) when permitted. A closed formula \(\varphi\in\mathrm{Form}(L)\) is satisfiable exactly when \[\text{there exists }\mathcal M\in\mathrm{Mod}(T_L)\text{ such that }\mathcal M\models\varphi.\] Any logic-specific restrictions on alternation, sorts, or operators remain part of membership in \(\mathrm{Form}(L)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quantified standard logic fixes a theory and signature while admitting specified uses of universal or existential quantification, possibly subject to additional restrictions.
knowledge_statements.title: Quantified Standard Logics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is locally appropriate and explicitly delegates syntax restrictions to the selected named logic. No source is cited, however, and quantified SMT-LIB logics differ materially in permitted signatures, quantifiers, and other restrictions. A specific authoritative catalog entry or standard section is needed to support this general characterization.

children.title: Nonstandard Logic Signatures
children.top_down_role: Logic signatures outside the standardized SMT fragment catalog.

assumptions_latex: A reference standardized signature \(\Sigma_L\) is fixed for logic \(L\).
An implementation accepts a possibly larger signature \(\Sigma_S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Use of a symbol in \(\Sigma_S\setminus\Sigma_L\) makes the input nonstandard relative to \(L\), even when the implementation assigns it a semantics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonstandard means outside the selected standardized logic, not semantically meaningless.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a standardized logic \(L\) with signature \(\Sigma_L\), and let solver \(S\) accept signature \(\Sigma_S\). The nonstandard portion of the accepted signature is \[\Delta_S=\Sigma_S\setminus\Sigma_L.\] An input has a nonstandard logic signature relative to \(L\) when some declared or applied nonlogical symbol belongs to \(\Delta_S\), or when a standard symbol is assigned a sort profile not admitted by \(\Sigma_L\). Such an input may have a solver-defined semantics, but it is not a sentence of the standardized logic \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A signature is nonstandard relative to a selected logic when it introduces symbols or sort profiles outside that logic's standardized signature.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonstandard Logic Signatures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits the definition leaf and correctly treats nonstandardness as relative to a selected logic. Its conclusion depends on an authoritative specification of the standardized signature and admitted sort profiles, but no source or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Solver-Extended Operators
children.top_down_role: Implementation-specific operators or constructs exposed beyond standardized language features.

assumptions_latex: Logic \(L\) has standardized term language \(\mathrm{Term}(L)\).
Solver \(S\) accepts an additional operator \(o\) with a documented sort profile.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An occurrence of \(o\) is portable as standard syntax only if it can be eliminated into an equivalent term of \(\mathrm{Term}(L)\) under the declared semantics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes semantic eliminability of solver extensions, not their performance after translation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A solver-extended operator \(o\) is an operator accepted by solver \(S\) but absent from \(\mathrm{Term}(L)\), the standardized term language of the selected logic. It is conservatively eliminable when there exists a translation \(\tau\) such that, for every well-sorted argument tuple \(\bar t\) and every standard model \(\mathcal M\), \[\mathcal M\models o(\bar t)=\tau(o(\bar t)).\] If no such standard translation is specified, formulas containing \(o\) depend on solver-specific syntax or semantics and are not standard-language portable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver-extended operator is standard-language portable only when a semantics-preserving translation eliminates it using operators of the selected standard logic.
knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Extended Operators

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the solver-extension leaf, but the eliminability equation evaluates the nonstandard operator in a 'standard model' without specifying an expansion that interprets that operator. The intended portability criterion is plausible, yet both the extension semantics and the exact model correspondence require an authoritative, inspectable source before the mathematical formulation can be trusted.

children.title: Cross-Solver Portability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Interchange limitations created by nonstandard signatures, commands, or semantic conventions.

assumptions_latex: Solvers \(S_1\) and \(S_2\) expose accepted input languages \(L_1\) and \(L_2\).
Both solvers use compatible semantics on their common standardized fragment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Direct semantic portability is guaranteed only on \(L_1\cap L_2\); outside it, portability requires an explicit semantics-preserving translation.

notation.meaning: input languages accepted by two solvers

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates direct portability from portability obtained through a verified translation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For solvers \(S_1\) and \(S_2\) with accepted input languages \(L_1\) and \(L_2\), the direct portability region is \[L_{\cap}=L_1\cap L_2,\] restricted to inputs on which both solvers assign the same semantics. If \(F\in L_1\setminus L_2\), direct portability fails syntactically. Portability can be recovered only by a translation \(\tau(F)\in L_2\) satisfying, for every relevant interpretation \(\mathcal M\), \(\mathcal M\models F\) if and only if \(\mathcal M\models\tau(F)\). Acceptance alone does not establish semantic portability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two solvers directly share only their common, semantically compatible input fragment; inputs outside it require an explicit satisfiability-preserving translation.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Solver Portability Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind matches the leaf, and the record properly distinguishes acceptance from semantic compatibility. However, direct portability is not determined by set intersection alone, and the translation condition compares formulas that may use different signatures without defining corresponding interpretations. No source supports the proposed boundary or resolves these semantic details.

children.title: SMT Interaction Protocol
children.top_down_role: Standardized interaction containers without duplicating internal solver mechanisms.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Command scripts, solver options, responses, models, cores, and proofs

children.title: Symbol Declarations
children.top_down_role: Commands establishing solver-visible symbols, sorts, functions, or related signature elements.

assumptions_latex: A current SMT signature and sort environment \(\Gamma\) are fixed.
Each declaration uses previously available sorts and a fresh symbol.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid declaration extends \(\Gamma\) with one typed symbol and does not itself add a constraint to the assertion set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers constant and function declarations through the nullary-function convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a typing environment \(\Gamma\), a symbol declaration specifies a fresh symbol \(f\), argument sorts \(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_n\), and result sort \(\sigma\), producing \[\Gamma'=\Gamma\cup\{f:\sigma_1\times\cdots\times\sigma_n\to\sigma\}.\] Every listed sort must already be available, and subsequent applications \(f(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\) are well-sorted only when each \(t_i\) has sort \(\sigma_i\). A constant declaration is the case \(n=0\). The declaration changes the signature but adds no asserted formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symbol declaration adds a fresh typed constant or function to the current signature; it does not assert any constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Symbol Declarations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the command-interface leaf, introduces its notation, and correctly separates signature extension from assertion. No SMT-LIB command reference is cited, so freshness, sort availability, nullary declarations, and declaration lifetime remain unsupported and potentially version-dependent.

children.title: Constraint Assertions
children.top_down_role: Commands adding formulas to the active solver context.

assumptions_latex: The asserted term \(\varphi\) is well-sorted and has Boolean sort.
A current assertion context \(A\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assertion command replaces \(A\) by \(A\cup\{\varphi\}\), so the active constraint is the conjunction of all active assertions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes assertion-state semantics independently of any solver's internal representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be the multiset of formulas in the current assertion context. For a well-sorted Boolean term \(\varphi\), executing an assertion command updates the context to \[A'=A\cup\{\varphi\}.\] The resulting active constraint is \(\Phi_{A'}=\bigwedge_{\psi\inA'}\psi\). Consequently, a subsequent satisfiability check asks whether there exists a model \(\mathcal M\) of the selected background theory such that \(\mathcal M\models\Phi_{A'}\). Assertions remain active until removed by the applicable context-management operation or reset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asserting a Boolean formula adds it to the active context, and later satisfiability checks use the conjunction of all active assertions.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Assertions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property is appropriate for constraint assertions, and its plain and LaTeX formulations are consistent. The multiset-and-conjunction state model and the persistence claim need a specific SMT-LIB assertion and context-management locator; none is supplied.

children.title: Logic Selection
children.top_down_role: Commands identifying the intended standardized or implementation-supported logic fragment.

assumptions_latex: A named standardized logic \(L\) is supported by the implementation.
No command requiring a fixed logic has yet made a conflicting selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selecting \(L\) fixes the permitted language and theory for subsequent declarations, assertions, and checks in the session.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Version-neutral semantics of explicit logic selection; exact command-order rules are standard-version dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Selecting a standardized logic \(L\) establishes the admissible signature \(\Sigma_L\), formula fragment, and background theory \(T_L\) for the subsequent interaction. Every later declared symbol and asserted term must be well-sorted relative to the resulting environment and must respect the restrictions of \(L\). A subsequent satisfiability response for active formula \(\Phi\) concerns the predicate \[\text{there exists }\mathcal M\in\mathrm{Mod}(T_L)\text{ such that }\mathcal M\models\Phi.\] Selecting \(L\) does not itself assert a formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logic selection fixes the standardized signature, formula restrictions, and background theory governing later commands, without adding an assertion.
knowledge_statements.title: Logic Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the logic-selection leaf, but its claim that selection fixes a single background theory and governs every later declaration may depend on the SMT-LIB version, logic declaration, and rules for user-declared symbols. The required set-logic and command-order citations are absent.

children.title: Command Ordering Constraints
children.top_down_role: Lifecycle restrictions governing where declarations, assertions, or logic selection may occur.

assumptions_latex: Commands are interpreted as a state transition sequence \(s_0\to s_1\to\cdots\).
Each command has a domain of protocol states in which it is legal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A script is command-order valid exactly when every command is applied in a state belonging to its command domain.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract condition covering declaration, assertion, query, context, and termination ordering constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Model an SMT interaction as protocol states \(s_0,s_1,\ldots,s_n\) and commands \(c_1,\ldots,c_n\), where command \(c_i\) has legal-state domain \(D(c_i)\) and transition function \(T_{c_i}\). The command sequence is order-valid exactly when \[s_{i-1}\in D(c_i)\quad\text{and}\quad s_i=T_{c_i}(s_{i-1})\qquad(1\le i\le n).\] Thus every symbol must be available before use, state-dependent queries must follow an appropriate check, context removal must not underflow the context stack, and no command may follow termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SMT script is correctly ordered when every command is legal in the state produced by all preceding commands.
knowledge_statements.title: Command Ordering Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the command-order leaf, and the state-transition notation is internally coherent. Yet validity is defined through unspecified legal-state domains, while the concrete examples assert protocol rules that vary by standard version and options. Specific authoritative locators defining those domains and rules are required.

children.title: Incremental Context Commands
children.top_down_role: Commands managing reusable assertion contexts across multiple solver checks.

assumptions_latex: The solver maintains a stack of assertion frames \((F_0,\ldots,F_d)\).
A context-pop operation never requests more frames than the current depth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pushing creates empty frames, while popping deletes the most recent frames and exactly their contained assertions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stack representation of incremental assertion contexts with a persistent base frame.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the incremental assertion context by frames \((F_0,\ldots,F_d)\), with active formula \[\Phi_d=\bigwedge_{j=0}^{d}\bigwedge_{\varphi\inF_j}\varphi.\] Pushing \(k\ge 0\) levels appends \(k\) empty frames. Popping \(k\) levels, permitted only when \(k\le d\), removes \(F_{d-k+1},\ldots,F_d\). Assertions added after a push belong to the current top frame; after a valid pop they cease to contribute to the active formula, while declarations or other state components follow their separately specified lifetimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incremental contexts form a stack of assertion frames: push adds empty frames, and pop removes recent frames together with their assertions.
knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Context Commands

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stack representation is appropriate for incremental context commands and clearly states push/pop effects on assertions. No authoritative push/pop locator is supplied, so the persistent base-frame convention, the legality bound, and the separation of assertion lifetimes from other state components remain unsupported.

children.title: Assumption-Based Checks
children.top_down_role: Check requests scoped by temporary assumption literals.

assumptions_latex: The persistent active assertions form \(\Phi\).
Each temporary assumption \(a_i\) is a well-sorted Boolean literal admitted by the protocol.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The check result is satisfiable exactly when \(\Phi\land\bigwedge_i a_i\) has a model, without permanently asserting the assumptions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core satisfiability semantics of assumption-based checking; diagnostic-core behavior is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi\) be the conjunction of persistent active assertions and let \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\) be admissible assumption literals. An assumption-based check evaluates \[\Phi_A=\Phi\land\bigwedge_{i=1}^{m}a_i.\] It returns satisfiable exactly when some model \(\mathcal M\) of the selected theory satisfies \(\mathcal M\models\Phi_A\), and unsatisfiable exactly when no such model exists. The assumptions affect this check and its immediately associated results but are not inserted into the persistent assertion frames.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An assumption-based check temporarily conjoins supplied literals with active assertions; those literals do not become persistent assertions.
knowledge_statements.title: Assumption-Based Checks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property accurately targets assumption-based checks and explicitly restricts assumptions to admissible Boolean literals. Its satisfiability semantics, non-persistence rule, and reference to immediately associated results require a specific check-sat-assuming standard locator, which is absent.

children.title: Context Lifetime Semantics
children.top_down_role: Visibility and persistence of assertions, assumptions, results, plus artifacts across contexts.

assumptions_latex: Persistent assertions are stored in stack frames.
Assumptions are supplied only to a single assumption-based check.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Popping ends the lifetime of removed-frame assertions, whereas temporary assumptions expire after their check and do not alter the persistent context.

notation.meaning: persistent assertion context before a check

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes frame-scoped assertions from check-scoped assumptions in incremental sessions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) denote the persistent stack of assertion frames. During an assumption-based check with assumptions \(A\), the effective context is \(C[A]\), whose active formula is the conjunction of assertions in \(C\) and literals in \(A\). After that check, the persistent context is again \(C\); the assumptions have expired. A pushed frame remains active until a matching pop removes it, at which point every assertion stored only in that frame expires. Hence check-scoped assumptions and frame-scoped assertions have distinct lifetimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporary assumptions last for one check, while assertions in a pushed frame last until that frame is popped.
knowledge_statements.title: Context Lifetime Semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the context-lifetime leaf and clearly distinguishes check-scoped assumptions from frame-scoped assertions. No source supports the stated lifetimes, and any implications for derived query results are explicitly version-sensitive; authoritative incremental-state and assumption-command locators are required.

children.title: Result Status Queries
children.top_down_role: Queries retrieving the solver's satisfiability outcome.

assumptions_latex: A solver context has been checked after all preceding assertions and stack operations.
The solver implements the three-valued SMT result convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned status is one of \(\mathsf{sat}\), \(\mathsf{unsat}\), or \(\mathsf{unknown}\), with the stated semantic guarantees.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic meaning of the standard three-valued result returned after a satisfiability check.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For active formula \(F\) in theory \(T\), a result-status query returns \(r\in\{\mathsf{sat},\mathsf{unsat},\mathsf{unknown}\}\). If \(r=\mathsf{sat}\), then there exists a \(T\)-interpretation \(\mathcal M\) such that \(\mathcal M\models F\). If \(r=\mathsf{unsat}\), then no \(T\)-interpretation satisfies \(F\), equivalently \(T\models\neg F\). If \(r=\mathsf{unknown}\), neither satisfiability nor unsatisfiability is certified. The status concerns exactly the assertion stack used by the immediately preceding check.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A status query reports satisfiable, unsatisfiable, or unknown; only the first two answers carry the corresponding semantic guarantee for the active assertions.
knowledge_statements.title: Result Status Queries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The three-valued status semantics are plausible and fit the result-status-query container, but no SMT protocol or standard is cited. A specific authoritative section defining sat, unsat, unknown, and the relationship to the preceding check is required.

children.title: Model Queries
children.top_down_role: Queries retrieving models or selected value interpretations after compatible outcomes.

assumptions_latex: The immediately preceding satisfiability check returned \(\mathsf{sat}\).
Model production is enabled for the solver context.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned interpretation \(\mathcal M\) satisfies every active assertion, so \(\mathcal M\models F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic contract for retrieving a model after a satisfiable result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A model query following a satisfiable check returns a \(T\)-interpretation \(\mathcal M\) for the relevant declared symbols such that \(\mathcal M\models F\), where \(F\) is the conjunction of assertions active during that check. Consequently, evaluating each active ground assertion under \(\mathcal M\) yields true. Values of symbols not constrained by \(F\) may be chosen arbitrarily, and the query has no model-validity guarantee after \(\mathsf{unsat}\) or \(\mathsf{unknown}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a satisfiable check, a model query returns an interpretation satisfying all assertions active during that check.
knowledge_statements.title: Model Queries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role and local scope are appropriate, but model availability, symbol coverage, and validity after a preceding check are protocol-dependent claims with no cited specification. Supply a solver or SMT interface reference with a precise locator.

children.title: Unsatisfiable Core Queries
children.top_down_role: Queries retrieving assertion or assumption subsets associated with refutation.

assumptions_latex: The checked assertion set \(A=\{\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_n\}\) is unsatisfiable modulo \(T\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned set \(C\subseteq A\) satisfies \(T\models\neg\bigwedge_{\varphi\in C}\varphi\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core soundness only; minimality is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An unsatisfiable-core query following an \(\mathsf{unsat}\) result returns identifiers selecting a subset \(C\subseteq A\) of tracked active assertions such that \(C\) is itself \(T\)-unsatisfiable: \[T\models\neg\bigwedge_{\varphi\in C}\varphi.\] Soundness requires this implication, but does not require inclusion-minimality or minimum cardinality. Assertions introduced internally by preprocessing may be represented only through their tracked input antecedents, according to the solver's core interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unsatisfiable-core query returns a tracked subset that is already inconsistent with the background theory; the subset need not be minimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsatisfiable Core Queries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The core-soundness statement and absence of a minimality guarantee fit the container, but tracking and preprocessing behavior are interface-specific and unsupported. An authoritative protocol or solver specification with a section-level locator is required.

children.title: Proof Artifact Queries
children.top_down_role: Queries retrieving solver-produced proof or certificate artifacts.

assumptions_latex: The immediately preceding check returned \(\mathsf{unsat}\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned proof object \(\pi\) is accepted only if \(\operatorname{Check}_T(\pi,F)=\mathsf{true}\), thereby certifying \(T\models\neg F\).

notation.meaning: Proof checker for theory and formula

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract checker-based contract, independent of any solver-specific proof format.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proof-artifact query after an unsatisfiable check returns an object \(\pi\) in the solver's declared proof calculus. Its semantic contract is checker soundness: \[\operatorname{Check}_T(\pi,F)=\mathsf{true}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad T\models\neg F.\] A complete artifact records or reconstructs every inference from the active assertions and accepted theory lemmas to contradiction. Merely returning \(\mathsf{unsat}\), without a checker-accepted \(\pi\), is not a proof artifact under this contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proof query returns a checkable derivation of contradiction from the active assertions and theory rules, in a solver-specific proof format.
knowledge_statements.title: Proof Artifact Queries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The checker-based certificate framing fits proof-artifact queries, but proof production, completeness of artifacts, and checker semantics depend on the solver and proof format. No inspectable source identifies the applicable calculus or interface.

Well-sorted ground terms of the same sort

children.title: Functional Congruence
children.top_down_role: Equality propagation across applications sharing function symbols.

assumptions_latex: The terms \(s_i,t_i\) are well-sorted and \(f\) is an uninterpreted \(n\)-ary function symbol.
Equality is interpreted as identity in a first-order structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(s_i=t_i\) for every \(i\), then \(f(s_1,\ldots,s_n)=f(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Substitutivity of equality through applications of an uninterpreted function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(n\)-ary function symbol \(f\) and all well-sorted terms \(s_1,\ldots,s_n,t_1,\ldots,t_n\), functional congruence is the valid implication \[\left(\bigwedge_{i=1}^{n}s_i=t_i\right)\ \Longrightarrow\ f(s_1,\ldots,s_n)=f(t_1,\ldots,t_n).\] Thus every equivalence relation representing equality consequences must be closed under matching function applications: pairwise equivalent arguments force equivalent result terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal arguments may be substituted into an uninterpreted function: applications with pairwise equal arguments must have equal results.
knowledge_statements.title: Functional Congruence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The functional-congruence property is standard and matches the leaf container, but it has no cited textbook, paper, or standard section supporting the stated implication and closure interpretation.

children.title: Equality-Congruence Interaction
children.top_down_role: The joint closure behavior linking asserted equalities to congruent term applications.

assumptions_latex: The input consists of finitely many ground equalities and disequalities over an EUF signature.
All subterms of the input are included in the finite term set \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equalities induce the least congruence \(\equiv_E\), and the input is satisfiable exactly when no asserted disequality has equivalent endpoints.

notation.meaning: Least congruence containing the asserted equalities

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of ground EUF satisfiability by the least congruence closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be the asserted equalities and let \(\equiv_E\) be the least equivalence relation on \(V\) that contains \(E\) and is closed under functional congruence. Equalities merge classes directly, while congruence merges applications whose function symbols agree and whose corresponding arguments are equivalent. For asserted disequalities \(D\), the ground EUF instance is satisfiable if and only if \[\forall(s\ne t)\in D,\quad s\not\equiv_E t.\] Hence equality propagation and congruence propagation reach one common fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ground equalities generate the least function-compatible equivalence relation; satisfiability fails exactly when an asserted disequality joins one equivalence class.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Congruence Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The least-congruence characterization of finite ground EUF satisfiability is plausible and locally appropriate, but its equivalence claim requires an authoritative congruence-closure or EUF source with a precise locator.

assumptions_latex: The input is a finite set of well-sorted ground EUF equalities and disequalities.
The term graph contains every input subterm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns unsatisfiable exactly when some asserted \(s\ne t\) has \(\operatorname{find}(s)=\operatorname{find}(t)\); otherwise it returns satisfiable.

notation.meaning: Representative of a maintained equivalence class

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision procedure for finite ground EUF instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize one equivalence class for each term in \(V\). Merge the endpoints of every asserted equality. Repeatedly merge \(f(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\) and \(f(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\) whenever they have the same head symbol and \(\operatorname{find}(s_i)=\operatorname{find}(t_i)\) for all \(i\), continuing until no merge applies. Then inspect every \(s\ne t\) in \(D\): output \(\mathsf{unsat}\) if \(\operatorname{find}(s)=\operatorname{find}(t)\), and output \(\mathsf{sat}\) otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Congruence closure repeatedly merges asserted equals and applications with equivalent arguments, then detects whether any asserted disequality lies within one class.
knowledge_statements.title: Congruence-Closure Procedures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind correctly fits the procedures container, and the finite ground-EUF decision rule is standard. No source supports termination, completeness, or the stated satisfiability criterion, however.

assumptions_latex: The formula is quantifier-free and every occurrence of an uninterpreted function is ground after purification.
A fresh variable \(v_a\) replaces each distinct application \(a=f(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original formula is EUF-satisfiable exactly when the purified formula conjoined with all Ackermann constraints is equality-satisfiable.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ground Ackermannization eliminating uninterpreted function applications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every pair \(a=f(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\) and \(b=f(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\) of applications with the same head symbol, introduce the Ackermann constraint \[\left(\bigwedge_{i=1}^{n}s_i^{\flat}=t_i^{\flat}\right)\Longrightarrow v_a=v_b.\] Let \(A_F\) be the conjunction of all such constraints and let \(F^{\flat}\) replace each application by its fresh variable recursively. Then \[F\text{ is EUF-satisfiable}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F^{\flat}\land A_F\text{ is satisfiable in pure equality}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ackermann reduction replaces ground function applications by fresh variables and adds pairwise congruence implications, preserving satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.title: Ackermann Reduction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits Ackermann reduction, but the exact purification convention, recursive replacement, and equisatisfiability with the stated pure-equality target need an authoritative reduction source and locator.

children.top_down_role: Finite interpretations of equivalence classes and uninterpreted function applications.

The finite term set \(V\) is closed under subterms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quotient construction defines an EUF model satisfying every asserted equality and disequality.

Set of congruence classes of terms of sort \(\sigma\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical quotient model for a satisfiable finite ground EUF instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each sort \(\sigma\), take \(D_\sigma\) to contain the congruence classes \([t]\) of ground terms of sort \(\sigma\), adding an arbitrary element if necessary. Interpret each represented application by \[f^{\mathcal M}([t_1],\ldots,[t_n])=[f(t_1,\ldots,t_n)].\] Congruence makes this definition independent of representatives. Extend \(f^{\mathcal M}\) arbitrarily on tuples not represented by input terms. Interpret each ground term \(t\) by \([t]\). Then asserted equalities hold, and every asserted disequality holds because its endpoints occupy distinct classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A satisfying EUF model uses congruence classes as domain elements and maps each represented function application to its result class.
