knowledge_statements.title: Direct Theory-Axiom Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness criterion for eager replacement of theory reasoning by axioms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a quantifier-free formula over a theory signature and let \(A_T(F)\) be a finite set of constraints encoding the theory semantics for all terms relevant to \(F\) in a target logic \(L\). If every \(T\)-model of \(F\) expands to an \(L\)-model of \(F\land A_T(F)\), and every \(L\)-model of \(F\land A_T(F)\) induces a \(T\)-model of \(F\), then the direct encoding is equisatisfiable: \(F\) is \(T\)-satisfiable exactly when \(F\land A_T(F)\) is \(L\)-satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct theory-axiom encoding is correct when target models and theory models correspond in both directions, yielding equisatisfiability.
assumptions_latex: \(A_T(F)\) is finite and effectively constructible.
The encoding is sound and complete for terms relevant to \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SAT}_T(F)\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{SAT}_L(F\land A_T(F))\).

notation.meaning: finite theory-axiom encoding generated for F

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Property is the correct role for the stated bidirectional model-correspondence criterion, and the equisatisfiability conclusion follows at the specification level. No inspectable source supports this criterion or the relevant-term encoding assumptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Reductions to SAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eager Boolean encoding of finite-domain constraint satisfaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given variables \(x_i\) with finite domains \(D_i\) and constraints \(C\), introduce Boolean atoms \(b_{i,a}\) for \(a\in D_i\). Add exactly-one clauses requiring \(\bigvee_{a\in D_i}b_{i,a}\) and \(\neg b_{i,a}\lor\neg b_{i,a'}\) for distinct \(a,a'\). Encode each constraint by clauses excluding precisely its locally forbidden value tuples, using auxiliary variables when desired. Run a complete SAT solver on the resulting formula. Return unsatisfiable if it is unsatisfiable; otherwise decode the unique true \(b_{i,a}\) for each \(i\) as \(x_i=a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent every finite-domain value by Boolean atoms, enforce one value per variable, encode forbidden tuples, solve by SAT, and decode the model.
assumptions_latex: Every domain \(D_i\) is finite and explicitly enumerable.
The constraint encoding excludes exactly the violating assignments.
The SAT solver is complete.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\text{ is satisfiable}\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{Enc}(C)\text{ is propositionally satisfiable}\).

notation.meaning: propositional encoding of the finite-domain instance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct role and the direct finite-domain encoding is coherent under the explicit enumerability and exact-forbidden-tuple assumptions. An authoritative SAT-encoding source with a specific section, theorem, or page locator is absent.

knowledge_statements.title: Abstraction-Refinement Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample-guided refinement of a propositional abstraction for a quantifier-free theory formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a quantifier-free theory formula \(F\), replace each theory atom \(a\) by a Boolean variable \(p_a\), obtaining \(B_0\). At iteration \(k\), obtain a satisfying Boolean assignment \(\beta_k\) for \(B_k\). If no such assignment exists, return theory-unsatisfiable. Otherwise let \(M_k\) be the theory literals selected by \(\beta_k\). If \(M_k\) is theory-consistent, return the corresponding theory model. If it is inconsistent, extract an inconsistent core \(C_k\subseteq M_k\) and set \(B_{k+1}=B_k\land\neg\bigwedge_{\ell\in C_k}p_\ell\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve a Boolean abstraction, check the selected theory literals, and exclude each theory-inconsistent core until a theory model is found or the abstraction becomes unsatisfiable.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is quantifier-free and contains finitely many theory atoms.
The theory checker is sound and complete for finite conjunctions of literals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns satisfiable exactly when \(F\) is satisfiable modulo the theory.

notation.meaning: theory-literal assignment induced at iteration k

review_flags: Authoritative SMT source and exact locator are missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No cited source or inspectable locator supports the algorithm or its correctness conclusion. The refinement notation also uses p_ell for signed theory literals without defining how negative literals are represented.

knowledge_statements.title: Eager-Encoding Size Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating polynomial-size eager theory reductions from potentially impractical or superpolynomial encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) map each quantifier-free theory formula \(F\) to an equisatisfiable propositional formula \(E(F)\). An eager reduction is polynomial-size when there exists a polynomial \(p\) such that \(|E(F)|\le p(|F|)\) for every \(F\), with coefficients and finite-domain values represented in the chosen input encoding. If no such bound holds for the selected representation, explicit materialization may be superpolynomial. Even when \(|E(F)|\) is polynomial, auxiliary variables or clauses can make eager reduction operationally impractical; this is an engineering boundary, not a logical failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eager reduction has a formal size guarantee only when its propositional output is polynomial in the encoded input; polynomial encodings may still be too large in practice.
assumptions_latex: \(E(F)\) is equisatisfiable with \(F\).
Input and output sizes count symbols or bits under fixed encodings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absence of a polynomial bound permits superpolynomial eager encodings, whereas polynomial size alone does not guarantee practical solvability.
review_flags: Authoritative SMT encoding-complexity source and exact locator are missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary content kind fits the leaf, but no cited source supports the encoding-size claims or the distinction between formal polynomial size and practical size. The local inventory is not cited and is not SMT-specific.

children.title: DPLL(T) Lazy SMT Architecture
children.top_down_role: The principal Boolean-theory integration framework and its architectural variants.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Lazy SMT and DPLL(T)

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Search Layer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CDCL-style Boolean search over propositional abstractions in a DPLL(T) solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a quantifier-free theory formula \(F\), form its Boolean abstraction \(B\). Maintain a partial Boolean assignment \(\alpha\), a decision stack, and a clause database initially containing the clauses of \(B\). Repeatedly apply Boolean unit propagation; choose an unassigned variable when propagation reaches a fixpoint; and accept theory lemmas supplied by the theory layer. On a Boolean or theory conflict, analyze the conflict, learn an entailed clause, and backjump. Return unsatisfiable at a root-level conflict, or return a propositionally complete assignment once all clauses are satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Boolean layer performs CDCL search on the abstraction, incorporating theory lemmas and returning either a complete candidate assignment or a root-level contradiction.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite quantifier-free theory formula.
Every theory lemma added to the clause database is theory-valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The layer enumerates candidate Boolean assignments while preserving satisfiability modulo the theory.

notation.meaning: propositional abstraction of the input formula

review_flags: Authoritative DPLL(T) source and exact locator are missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Boolean-search leaf, but the CDCL(T) operations and satisfiability-preservation conclusion have no authoritative citation or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Theory-Consistency Checking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: On-demand consistency checks coupling a Boolean abstraction with a decision procedure for the background theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be the Boolean abstraction of a quantifier-free formula \(F\). During Boolean search, select an assignment \(\alpha\) and let \(M(\alpha)\) be its asserted theory literals. Invoke the theory solver only at the designated checkpoints. If \(M(\alpha)\) is inconsistent, obtain a theory-valid clause \(L\) falsified by \(\alpha\), add \(L\) to \(B\), and resume Boolean search. If a propositionally satisfying assignment has theory-consistent literals, return satisfiable; if the augmented Boolean problem becomes unsatisfiable, return unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lazy solver checks theory consistency at selected search states and converts each detected inconsistency into a learned theory-valid Boolean clause.
assumptions_latex: The Boolean abstraction preserves the logical structure of \(F\).
The theory solver is sound and complete on the checked literal sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The combined procedure decides satisfiability of \(F\) modulo the theory.

notation.meaning: theory literals selected by the assignment

review_flags: Authoritative lazy-SMT source and exact locator are missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches lazy theory-consistency checking, but no source supports the checkpoint scheme, learned-theory-clause requirements, or the claimed decision result.

children.title: Partial-Assignment Theory Checks
children.top_down_role: Theory-consistency checks performed before a complete Boolean assignment is available.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Assignment Theory Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Theory checking before the Boolean assignment is propositionally complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: During Boolean search, let \(\alpha\) be a partial assignment and \(M(\alpha)\) its currently asserted theory literals. At a prescribed checkpoint, query whether \(M(\alpha)\) is theory-consistent. If inconsistent, return a theory-valid conflict clause \(C\) that is falsified by \(\alpha\), learn \(C\), and backjump. If consistent, optionally return theory consequences whose Boolean atoms are unassigned, enqueue them, and continue search. Consistency of \(M(\alpha)\) does not certify satisfiability until a suitable complete assignment is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The theory solver checks incomplete Boolean assignments, learning conflicts early and optionally propagating theory consequences, but consistency of a partial assignment is not a final model certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha\) assigns only atoms occurring in the current abstraction.
Reported conflicts and propagations are theory-valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every inconsistent partial assignment is safely pruned, while a consistent partial assignment remains extendible only as an unresolved possibility.
review_flags: Authoritative source for partial-assignment theory checking is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but no source supports partial-assignment checking and propagation. The conclusion's phrase 'remains extendible only as an unresolved possibility' must be checked against a source because theory consistency alone does not imply Boolean or theory extendibility.

children.title: Total-Assignment Theory Checks
children.top_down_role: Theory-consistency checks performed on complete Boolean candidate assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: Total-Assignment Theory Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Theory checking restricted to propositionally complete candidate assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha\) be a total assignment satisfying the current Boolean abstraction, and let \(M(\alpha)\) contain the corresponding signed theory literals. Query the theory solver on \(M(\alpha)\). If consistent, combine \(\alpha\) with the returned theory model and report satisfiable. If inconsistent, extract a finite inconsistent subset \(K\subseteq M(\alpha)\), learn the clause \(\bigvee_{\ell\in K}\neg p_\ell\), and restart Boolean search. If no propositionally satisfying total assignment remains, report unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The solver invokes the theory checker only on complete Boolean candidates, accepting a consistent candidate or blocking an inconsistent core and continuing Boolean search.
assumptions_latex: The abstraction has finitely many Boolean atoms.
The theory solver is sound and complete for conjunctions of ground literals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure terminates with the correct satisfiability result modulo the theory.

notation.meaning: signed theory literals selected by the assignment

review_flags: Authoritative source for total-assignment theory checking is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No authoritative source supports the total-assignment procedure or termination claim. The learned clause uses p_ell for signed literals without defining their Boolean representatives.

children.title: Assignment-Check Timing Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Search costs, pruning opportunities, plus solver-state implications of check timing.

knowledge_statements.title: Assignment-Check Timing Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal pruning and cost tradeoff between partial- and total-assignment theory checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For partial assignments \(\alpha\subseteq\beta\), inconsistency is monotone: if \(M(\alpha)\) is theory-inconsistent, then \(M(\beta)\) is theory-inconsistent. Hence checking \(\alpha\) can prune every Boolean extension of \(\alpha\) before they are explored. However, partial checking can invoke the theory solver on assignments that Boolean propagation would later discard. Restricting checks to propositionally complete assignments avoids those intermediate calls but may rediscover many extensions sharing an already inconsistent theory core. Thus neither timing regime uniformly minimizes total solving cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Early checks can prune whole subtrees but may perform unnecessary theory calls; late checks reduce call frequency but may explore many assignments sharing the same theory conflict.
assumptions_latex: \(M(\alpha)\subseteq M(\beta)\) whenever \(\alpha\subseteq\beta\).
Theory inconsistency is preserved when additional literals are conjoined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Partial checking weakly dominates total checking in pruning power, but neither regime uniformly dominates in runtime.

notation.meaning: beta extends the partial assignment alpha

review_flags: Authoritative source for the timing tradeoff is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits the tradeoff leaf, and inconsistency monotonicity is standard, but the comparative pruning and runtime claims lack a cited authoritative source and locator.

children.title: Online Theory Integration

knowledge_statements.title: Online Theory Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental theory interaction synchronized with Boolean decisions, propagation, and backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a Boolean trail \(\alpha\) and an incremental theory state representing \(M(\alpha)\). Whenever the Boolean layer appends a theory literal \(\ell\), assert \(\ell\) to the theory solver. Before or during further Boolean search, request consistency and theory propagation. On inconsistency, learn a theory-valid clause falsified by \(\alpha\); on an implied literal, enqueue its Boolean representative with a theory explanation. When Boolean search backtracks, restore the theory state to the matching trail level. Stop under the ordinary DPLL(T) satisfiable or unsatisfiable conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Online integration updates and queries the theory solver throughout Boolean search, propagating consequences and synchronizing theory state with every backtrack.
assumptions_latex: The theory solver supports incremental assertion and restoration.
Every theory conflict or propagation has a theory-valid explanation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Online interaction preserves DPLL(T) correctness while allowing theory information to affect unfinished Boolean search.

notation.meaning: theory literals represented by the trail

review_flags: Authoritative source for online theory integration is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits online integration, but incremental synchronization, explanation requirements, and the DPLL(T) correctness conclusion have no cited source or exact locator.

children.title: Batch Theory Integration

knowledge_statements.title: Batch Theory Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Theory interaction performed on accumulated sets of literals at coarse search checkpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Run Boolean search without synchronously querying the theory solver after each trail update. At a designated checkpoint, collect the current batch \(M(\alpha)\) of asserted theory literals and submit it to the theory solver. If inconsistent, add a theory-valid clause blocking an inconsistent subset of the batch and resume Boolean search. If consistent but the Boolean assignment is incomplete, continue search without requiring immediate theory propagation. Report satisfiable only for a propositionally satisfying assignment whose full theory-literal set is consistent; report unsatisfiable after Boolean exhaustion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batch integration accumulates theory literals and checks them at coarse checkpoints, reducing interaction frequency while delaying conflicts and theory consequences.
assumptions_latex: Every returned conflict clause is theory-valid.
A final satisfying assignment is checked for theory consistency.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Batch integration is sound and complete when the Boolean search is exhaustive and final candidates receive complete theory checks.

notation.meaning: Boolean assignment at a batch checkpoint

review_flags: Authoritative source for batch theory integration is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits batch integration, but the checkpoint semantics and stated soundness-and-completeness conditions require an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Integration-Granularity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Communication frequency, state synchronization, plus amortized theory-processing costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Integration-Granularity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-versus-overhead tradeoff between online and batch theory integration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose online and batch integrations use sound theory explanations and eventually check every propositionally satisfying candidate. Online integration can expose a conflict or implied literal immediately after the responsible trail prefix appears, so its pruning is at least as early as a batch policy checking only later supersets. It may nevertheless incur more solver calls, state synchronization, and explanation traffic. Batch integration amortizes interaction over larger literal sets but can perform Boolean work that earlier theory feedback would have prevented. Therefore correctness is unchanged, while resource use depends on instance structure and implementation costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fine-grained integration supplies earlier theory information at greater interaction cost; batching amortizes calls but may waste Boolean search. Both remain correct under complete final checking.
assumptions_latex: Both regimes use sound theory lemmas.
Every complete Boolean candidate is eventually checked for theory consistency.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Online integration weakly improves feedback latency, but neither granularity uniformly minimizes runtime or memory.
review_flags: Authoritative source for integration-granularity tradeoffs is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits the tradeoff leaf, but the weak feedback-latency dominance and runtime/memory comparison are uncited and depend on precisely defined online and batch policies.

children.title: Eager Theory Propagation
children.top_down_role: Theory consequences communicated early during Boolean search.

knowledge_statements.title: Eager Theory Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Theory propagation performed whenever the Boolean trail gains relevant literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After each relevant extension of the Boolean trail \(\alpha\), query the theory solver on \(M(\alpha)\). For every unassigned theory atom \(q\) such that \(T\models M(\alpha)\rightarrow q\), enqueue \(q\) with an explanation clause \(\neg M'\lor q\), where \(M'\subseteq M(\alpha)\) suffices for the implication. If \(M(\alpha)\) is inconsistent, return an explained theory conflict immediately. Repeat Boolean and theory propagation to a joint fixpoint before making the next Boolean decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eager propagation queries the theory solver after relevant trail changes and adds every selected theory consequence before the next Boolean decision.
assumptions_latex: The theory solver returns only consequences valid in \(T\).
Each propagated literal or conflict has a finite explanation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every enqueued theory literal follows from the current trail, and detected theory conflicts are exposed before the next decision.

notation.meaning: theory literals asserted by the trail

review_flags: Authoritative source for eager theory propagation is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits eager theory propagation, but no source supports the timing and fixpoint claims. The quantified unassigned atom q should be restricted to a defined finite set of represented theory atoms.

children.title: Delayed Theory Propagation
children.top_down_role: Theory consequences deferred until selected search states or checkpoints.

knowledge_statements.title: Delayed Theory Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Theory consequences are requested only at selected checkpoints rather than after every trail extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain the Boolean trail \(\alpha\) while postponing propagation queries to designated checkpoints, such as a Boolean-propagation fixpoint or a complete candidate assignment. At a checkpoint, query the theory solver on \(M(\alpha)\). Enqueue each returned consequence \(q\) only with a theory-valid explanation \(T\models M'\rightarrow q\), where \(M'\subseteq M(\alpha)\); return an explained conflict if the set is inconsistent. Between checkpoints, Boolean decisions may proceed without all currently derivable theory consequences. A final candidate must still undergo a complete consistency check.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delayed propagation requests theory consequences only at checkpoints, lowering interaction frequency while permitting Boolean search to proceed temporarily without available theory implications.
assumptions_latex: All returned propagations and conflicts are theory-valid.
Every final Boolean candidate receives a complete theory-consistency check.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Delaying propagation preserves correctness but can postpone pruning that eager propagation would perform earlier.

notation.meaning: theory literals asserted by the trail

review_flags: Authoritative source for delayed theory propagation is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits delayed theory propagation, but the checkpoint policy, explanation conditions, and correctness conclusion have no authoritative citation or inspectable locator.

children.title: Propagation-Timing Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Pruning strength, communication overhead, plus search-state effects of propagation timing.

assumptions_latex: The background theory \(T\) has a sound consistency checker and a sound theory-propagation procedure.
The current Boolean trail \(M\) is a finite, theory-relevant partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Changing the propagation schedule preserves soundness but can change both theory-call cost and Boolean search size.

notation.meaning: Current Boolean trail viewed as a set of theory literals
Theory consequences generated from the trail

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Standard DPLL(T) scheduling tradeoff between propagation overhead and pruning.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares eager and delayed propagation schedules without asserting universal runtime dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every trail \(M\), sound propagation returns only literals \(P_T(M)\) satisfying \(T\models (\bigwedge M)\rightarrow (\bigwedge P_T(M))\). An eager regime invokes propagation after more trail extensions, whereas a delayed regime invokes it only at selected synchronization points. Eagerness may discover implications or conflicts at smaller trails and thereby reduce Boolean decisions and backtracking, but it incurs more theory calls and may generate low-value lemmas. Delay reduces interaction overhead and permits larger batched checks, but may explore Boolean assignments already inconsistent with \(T\). Thus soundness is schedule-invariant, while call count, explanation size, and search-tree size are schedule-dependent; neither regime uniformly dominates the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eager propagation can prune Boolean search earlier but costs more theory calls; delayed propagation saves interaction overhead but may discover theory conflicts later.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-Timing Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the propagation-timing tradeoff leaf and carefully avoids claiming uniform runtime dominance. The mathematical claims about call frequency, pruning, explanation size, and schedule-invariant soundness are plausible but have no cited SMT source or inspectable locator; the unrelated local inventory does not support them.

assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a fixed background theory over a designated finite set of theory atoms \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Propagation completeness means deriving every theory-literal consequence expressible over the designated atoms.

notation.meaning: Finite set of designated theory atoms
Theory-consistent trail of literals over the atoms

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Formalizes propagation completeness relative to a finite interface vocabulary.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness is relative to the finite atom vocabulary exposed to the Boolean engine.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\operatorname{Lit}(A)=A\cup\{\neg a:a\in A\}\). A sound theory-propagation operator \(P_T\) maps every \(T\)-consistent trail \(M\subseteq\operatorname{Lit}(A)\) to literals satisfying \(T\models(\bigwedge M)\rightarrow(\bigwedge P_T(M))\). It is propagation-complete over \(A\) when, for every such \(M\) and every \(\ell\in\operatorname{Lit}(A)\), \[T\models(\bigwedge M)\rightarrow\ell\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \ell\in P_T(M).\] A regime is incomplete when this implication fails for some \(M\) and \(\ell\), even if its eventual consistency checks remain decision-complete. Completeness therefore concerns exposed literal consequences, not arbitrary formulas outside \(\operatorname{Lit}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propagation-complete theory solver derives every theory-literal consequence of a consistent trail that is expressible using the designated interface atoms.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-Completeness Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally precise and appropriately makes completeness relative to a finite interface vocabulary. However, no authoritative source or specific locator supports this particular formulation or its distinction from decision completeness.

assumptions_latex: \(T\) is the background theory and \(M\) is a finite set of asserted theory literals.
The conjunction \(\bigwedge M\) is inconsistent with \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The clause formed by negating a conflicting subset is a theory-valid conflict lemma falsified by the current trail.

notation.meaning: Current set of asserted theory literals
Theory-inconsistent explanation contained in the trail
Conflict clause generated from the explanation

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Standard DPLL(T) conflict-clause construction from a theory-inconsistent subset.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses clausal explanations for conflicts under a fixed background theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A conflict explanation is a finite subset \(E\subseteq M\) such that \(T\models
eg igwedge E\). Its associated conflict lemma is \[C_E= igvee_{\ell\in E}
eg\ell.\] The entailment \(T\models C_E\) makes \(C_E\) globally valid under the background theory, while \(M\models
eg C_E\) shows that the current trail falsifies it. Consequently, adding \(C_E\) to the Boolean clause database excludes the present conflicting assignment and every future assignment containing \(E\), without excluding any \(T\)-model. The subset \(E\) need not be inclusion-minimal for the clause to be sound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negating a theory-inconsistent subset of the current trail yields a theory-valid clause that blocks the conflict and all assignments containing its explanation.
knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Lemmas

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits conflict lemmas, and the clause construction is mathematically standard and internally consistent. No SMT source with a specific section, theorem, definition, or page locator is cited, so the candidate cannot be source-reviewed.

assumptions_latex: \(T\) is the background theory and \(M\) is a finite, \(T\)-consistent trail.
A theory literal \(p\) is entailed by \(M\) modulo \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The clause \((\bigvee_{\ell\in E}\neg\ell)\vee p\) soundly communicates the propagated literal to the Boolean engine.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Standard DPLL(T) propagation-clause construction from a theory implication.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers clausal explanations of theory propagation over interface literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an explanation \(E\subseteq M\) satisfying \(T\models(\bigwedge E)\rightarrow p\). The associated propagation lemma is \[C_{E,p}=\left(\bigvee_{\ell\in E}\neg\ell\right)\vee p.\] Since \(T\models C_{E,p}\), adding the clause preserves the set of \(T\)-models. When every literal of \(E\) is true and \(p\) is unassigned, Boolean unit propagation on \(C_{E,p}\) assigns \(p\). If \(p\) is false, the same clause exposes a conflict. Thus the lemma provides a Boolean-checkable certificate of the theory implication; soundness requires the entailment above, but does not require \(E\) to be minimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A theory implication from trail literals to a new literal becomes a valid clause that enables Boolean unit propagation or exposes a conflict.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Lemmas

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role correctly captures a propagation lemma as a Boolean-checkable theory implication. Its hypotheses, clause, and operational consequences are coherent, but no authoritative SMT citation or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Theory-Lemma Strength
children.top_down_role: Relative explanatory or pruning power of generated theory lemmas.

assumptions_latex: Two theory lemmas are clauses over the same Boolean abstraction and are valid in the same theory \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Clause implication defines lemma strength: a stronger lemma excludes every Boolean assignment excluded by a weaker one, and possibly more.

notation.meaning: Boolean abstraction of a theory clause

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Uses semantic implication as the standard strength preorder for valid clauses.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength is semantic over a fixed Boolean interface, not merely clause length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(C_1\) to be at least as strong as \(C_2\) when \(\mathcal B(C_1)\models\mathcal B(C_2)\). Equivalently, every Boolean assignment satisfying \(C_1\) also satisfies \(C_2\). If additionally \(\mathcal B(C_2)\not\models\mathcal B(C_1)\), then \(C_1\) is strictly stronger. Replacing \(C_2\) by \(C_1\) preserves theory soundness when both satisfy \(T\models C_i\), and it cannot admit a Boolean abstraction assignment rejected by \(C_2\). Clause length alone does not determine this order: two short clauses may be incomparable, and a longer clause may participate in stronger propagation under surrounding clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One theory lemma is stronger than another when its Boolean abstraction implies the other; strength is semantic and is not determined solely by clause length.
knowledge_statements.title: Theory-Lemma Strength

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the theory-lemma-strength leaf and correctly distinguishes semantic implication from clause length. The exact abstraction-relative strength formulation and operational commentary lack an authoritative source and specific locator.

children.title: Theory-Lemma Reuse
children.top_down_role: Retention plus reuse of theory lemmas across search states or solver calls.

assumptions_latex: Every retained lemma \(C\) is valid in the fixed background theory \(T\).
Successive solver states use a compatible Boolean abstraction of the atoms occurring in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A retained theory lemma may be reused at any compatible later state without another theory-validity check.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Theory validity makes learned clauses reusable across compatible search states.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse applies while theory semantics and atom abstraction remain compatible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a generated lemma satisfies \(T\models C\), its validity is independent of the trail on which it was generated. Therefore, for every later compatible trail \(M'\), conjoining \(C\) to the Boolean clause database preserves all \(T\)-models. The retained clause may participate in unit propagation or conflict analysis whenever its literals become relevant, without rerunning the theory derivation that originally established it. Reuse is unsound if the meaning of an abstracted atom changes or if the active background theory is weakened so that \(T\models C\) no longer holds. Reuse across stronger theories remains sound whenever the stronger theory entails \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A theory-valid learned clause can be reused throughout compatible later search states, provided the theory and meanings of its abstract atoms remain suitable.
knowledge_statements.title: Theory-Lemma Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reuse principle matches the leaf and states the necessary compatibility limitations. Its claims about reuse without rechecking and reuse under stronger theories are mathematically plausible, but no relevant SMT source or locator is provided.

children.title: Theory-Lemma Deletion
children.top_down_role: Removal policies for controlling lemma-database growth.

assumptions_latex: The clause database is partitioned into permanent input clauses and deletable learned theory lemmas.
Every learned theory lemma was added only after establishing its validity in \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deleting learned theory lemmas preserves satisfiability equivalence, although it can remove useful propagation and permit repeated search.

notation.meaning: Current set of learned theory lemmas

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Redundant valid clauses may be removed without changing satisfiability modulo the theory.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Addresses semantic safety and search consequences of deleting redundant learned lemmas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq L\) and suppose \(T\models C\) for every \(C\in L\). Then \[T\wedge F\wedge\bigwedge L\text{ is satisfiable}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad T\wedge F\wedge\bigwedge(L\setminus D)\text{ is satisfiable}.\] Hence deletion of learned theory lemmas cannot create or destroy a model of the original problem. Operational behavior may nevertheless change: removing \(D\) can eliminate unit propagations, allow a previously blocked partial assignment to recur, and force regeneration of an equivalent explanation. A deletion policy must preserve any clauses required by the solver's current implication graph, proof object, or other implementation invariant until those dependencies are discharged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting redundant theory-valid learned clauses preserves satisfiability, but may weaken propagation, repeat conflicts, or violate implementation dependencies if clauses are removed too early.
knowledge_statements.title: Theory-Lemma Deletion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property correctly separates semantic satisfiability preservation from implementation dependencies and search degradation. It has no authoritative clause-database or SMT source with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Lemma-Lifecycle Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Interactions among lemma utility, memory pressure, plus future search value.

assumptions_latex: All stored theory lemmas are theory-valid and represented as Boolean clauses.
Clause evaluation, propagation, and memory use have nonzero implementation cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Lemma retention has no uniform optimum: additional valid clauses strengthen the database monotonically but can worsen operational cost.

notation.meaning: Retained lemma databases with inclusion ordering

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Clause-database management trades logical pruning against propagation and memory overhead.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates semantic monotonicity from implementation-dependent runtime effects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For retained databases \(L_1\subseteq L_2\), every Boolean assignment satisfying \(F\wedge\bigwedge L_2\) also satisfies \(F\wedge\bigwedge L_1\); thus retention monotonically strengthens the Boolean abstraction and can prevent recurrence of learned conflicts. However, evaluating and storing \(L_2\setminus L_1\) may increase memory consumption, watched-literal traffic, and propagation work. Deletion reduces those costs but can enlarge the subsequently explored search and cause lemma regeneration. Consequently, semantic strength is monotone under retention, whereas total solving time is not. A lifecycle policy balances expected future propagation or conflict value against maintenance cost while preserving clauses needed by active derivations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping more valid lemmas strengthens pruning and enables reuse, but consumes memory and propagation effort; deletion saves overhead while risking repeated search and regeneration.
knowledge_statements.title: Lemma-Lifecycle Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the lifecycle-tradeoff leaf and distinguishes monotone logical strengthening from nonmonotone runtime cost. The implementation-level claims about memory, watched-literal traffic, propagation work, and regeneration require a relevant cited source and locator.

children.title: Minimal Conflict Explanations
children.top_down_role: Conflict explanations minimized relative to a selected relevance criterion.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite set of theory literals inconsistent with the background theory \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A minimal conflict explanation is an inclusion-minimal inconsistent subset of the current trail.

notation.meaning: Current inconsistent set of theory literals

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Standard inclusion-minimal unsatisfiable-subset definition specialized to a theory trail.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal means inclusion-minimal, not necessarily minimum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A subset \(E\subseteq M\) is a minimal conflict explanation when \[T\models\neg\bigwedge E\] and, for every \(\ell\in E\), \[T\wedge\bigwedge(E\setminus\{\ell\})\text{ is satisfiable}.\] Equivalently, \(E\) is theory-inconsistent and every proper subset of \(E\) is theory-consistent. Its conflict clause \(\bigvee_{\ell\in E}\neg\ell\) is theory-valid, and deleting any one of its literals would correspond to a proper subset not certified inconsistent by minimality. Inclusion-minimality does not imply that \(|E|\) is smallest among all inconsistent subsets of \(M\); several incomparable minimal explanations may exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimal conflict explanation is theory-inconsistent, but becomes theory-consistent whenever any one of its literals is removed; it need not have minimum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Conflict Explanations

children.title: Nonminimal Conflict Explanations
children.top_down_role: Valid conflict explanations retaining literals beyond a minimal core.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite set of theory literals inconsistent with the background theory \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A nonminimal explanation is a sound inconsistent subset containing at least one redundant literal.

notation.meaning: Current inconsistent set of theory literals

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Negation of inclusion-minimality for an otherwise valid conflict explanation.
INVALID_TEX_CORRECTED: Replaced malformed \negigwedge expressions and removed the corrupted [0m token.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonminimality concerns redundant literals, not invalidity of the explanation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A subset \(E\subseteq M\) is a nonminimal conflict explanation when \(T\models
eg igwedge E\) and there exists \(r\in E\) such that \[T\models
eg igwedge(E\setminus\{r\}).\] The literal \(r\) is redundant for establishing this conflict. The associated clause \( igvee_{\ell\in E}
eg\ell\) remains theory-valid and is therefore a sound learned clause, but it is weaker than the clause obtained from \(E\setminus\{r\}\): the shorter clause implies the longer one. Repeated removal of redundant literals from the finite set \(E\) eventually yields an inclusion-minimal conflict explanation, though the result may depend on the removal order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonminimal conflict explanation is still sound, but contains a literal whose removal leaves the remaining set theory-inconsistent and yields a stronger conflict clause.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonminimal Conflict Explanations

children.title: Explanation-Minimality Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Generation cost, learned-clause quality, plus downstream search effects.

assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite theory-inconsistent explanation extracted from the current trail.
Testing inconsistency of candidate subsets incurs nonzero theory-solving cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Minimization strengthens the learned conflict clause but can require additional theory checks, so it need not minimize total solving time.

notation.meaning: Conflict clause generated from an explanation

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Explanation minimization trades stronger learned clauses against extra theory-oracle work.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares logical clause strength with the computational cost of obtaining it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(E'\subsetneq E\) and both sets are inconsistent with \(T\), then their conflict clauses satisfy \[C_{E'}=\bigvee_{\ell\in E'}\neg\ell\models C_E=\bigvee_{\ell\in E}\neg\ell.\] Thus reducing an explanation produces a semantically stronger clause that can block more assignments and may improve future propagation. Establishing inclusion-minimality, however, can require checking multiple subsets of \(E\) for theory consistency; minimum-cardinality search can require still more exploration. Returning \(E\) immediately avoids this minimization cost but learns a weaker clause. Therefore explanation strength improves monotonically under redundant-literal removal, whereas total solver runtime need not improve monotonically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Removing redundant literals strengthens a conflict clause and may improve pruning, but finding minimal or minimum explanations requires extra theory checks and may cost more overall.
knowledge_statements.title: Explanation-Minimality Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tradeoff principle fits the exact leaf, and the implication direction between clauses from nested inconsistent explanations is correct. The claims about minimization effort and runtime effects have no authoritative source or specific locator.

assumptions_latex: The theory solver decides consistency of every finite conjunction in its supported quantifier-free theory fragment.
For an inconsistent trail, the solver can expose a finite internal contradiction certificate or an inconsistent core.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a subset of the trail whose negated disjunction is a theory-valid conflict lemma.

notation.meaning: Current set of asserted theory literals
Theory-specific solver state built from the trail

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Abstract algorithm captures certificate-based explanation extraction across theory solvers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract interface covering graph, tableau, congruence, and certificate-based explanation procedures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite trail \(M\) and initialize the theory-specific state \(S_T(M)\) by asserting its literals while recording dependency links from derived facts to asserted premises. If \(S_T(M)\) is consistent, return no conflict explanation. Otherwise, select an internal contradiction certificate, traverse its dependency links to collect asserted premises \(E\subseteq M\), and optionally remove any \(r\in E\) for which \(T\wedge\bigwedge(E\setminus\{r\})\) remains inconsistent. Stop after the requested minimization criterion or resource limit is met. Output \(E\) together with \(C_E=\bigvee_{\ell\in E}\neg\ell\). Correct output requires \(T\models C_E\); the concrete certificate and dependency traversal are theory-specific.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A theory solver traces an internal contradiction back to asserted literals, optionally minimizes them, and returns their negated disjunction as a valid conflict lemma.
knowledge_statements.title: Theory-Specific Explanation Generation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits explanation generation, and the stated output condition is sound under the explicit certificate assumption. However, the proposed dependency-tracing interface generalizes across theory solvers without theory-specific evidence; no relevant sources or inspectable locators support that breadth.

children.title: Explanation Quality Criteria
children.top_down_role: Size, relevance, locality, plus strength criteria for theory explanations.

knowledge_statements.title: Explanation Quality Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criteria for theory-conflict explanations returned to a CDCL-style Boolean engine.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be the current set of asserted theory literals and let \(E\subseteq M\). The set \(E\) is a valid theory-conflict explanation when \(E\) is inconsistent in theory \(T\). Its Boolean clause is \(C_E=\bigvee_{\ell\in E}\neg\ell\). Explanation quality may be ordered by the tuple \(q(E)=(|E|,\operatorname{LBD}(C_E),\operatorname{cost}(E))\), minimized lexicographically; subset-minimality additionally requires every \(E'\subsetneq E\) to be \(T\)-consistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A theory explanation must be inconsistent, and quality can favor fewer literals, lower clause dispersion, lower generation cost, and subset-minimality.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite set of ground literals whose atoms are represented in the Boolean abstraction.
Theory inconsistency of finite subsets of \(M\) is decidable by the theory solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E\text{ is valid}\iff E\subseteq M\land E\models_T\bot\), and it induces the theory-valid clause \(C_E\).

notation.meaning: Boolean conflict clause induced by the explanation
number of decision levels represented in a clause

review_flags: No supplied locator addresses SMT theory-conflict explanation criteria.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validity and subset-minimality conditions are mathematically standard and fit the leaf, but no cited source supports them. More importantly, the lexicographic tuple involving explanation size, LBD, and generation cost is an implementation-dependent proposed ordering rather than a generally established definition; LBD also depends on the current Boolean trail. An SMT-specific source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Boolean-Search Consequences
children.top_down_role: Effects of theory explanations on learning, backjumping, branching, plus pruning.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean-Search Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of a valid theory explanation on CDCL search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(E\subseteq M\) satisfies \(E\models_T\bot\), then \(T\models C_E\), where \(C_E=\bigvee_{\ell\in E}\neg\ell\). Adding \(C_E\) to the Boolean clause database preserves satisfiability modulo \(T\), forbids every future Boolean assignment containing all literals of \(E\), and permits ordinary conflict analysis. A strict subset explanation \(E'\subsetneq E\) yields a clause \(C_{E'}\) that subsumes \(C_E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid explanation yields a sound learned clause; smaller explanations produce stronger clauses that exclude at least as much Boolean search.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) consists of theory literals simultaneously asserted by the current Boolean assignment.
The Boolean abstraction preserves complementation of theory literals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\models C_E\), and \(E'\subsetneq E\) implies \(C_{E'}\models C_E\).

notation.meaning: learned clause induced by explanation E

review_flags: No supplied locator supports SMT learning from theory explanations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The soundness and subsumption claims are mathematically coherent and the property kind fits Boolean-search consequences. However, the record supplies no citation for theory-lemma learning, preservation of satisfiability modulo T, or the interaction with ordinary conflict analysis. A source with a section, theorem, or page locator is required.

children.title: Explanation–Search Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Costs of producing stronger explanations relative to expected search benefits.

knowledge_statements.title: Explanation–Search Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal tradeoff between explanation strength and extraction effort.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a theory conflict \(M\models_T\bot\), let \(\mathcal E(M)=\{E\subseteq M:E\models_T\bot\}\). An explanation procedure selects \(E\in\mathcal E(M)\) by balancing extraction cost \(c(E)\) against an estimated Boolean-search penalty \(s(C_E)\). Thus it may minimize \(J_\lambda(E)=c(E)+\lambda s(C_E)\) for \(\lambda\geq0\). Minimizing \(|E|\) or strengthening \(C_E\) can require additional theory checks, so the cheapest valid explanation need not minimize downstream search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solvers trade the cost of shrinking an explanation against the expected search reduction from learning a stronger clause.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is theory-inconsistent and finite.
\(c\) and \(s\) are nonnegative implementation-dependent measures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An admissible selection is any \(E\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{F\in\mathcal E(M)}J_\lambda(F)\).

notation.meaning: valid explanations contained in the conflict set

review_flags: The scalar objective is a formalization of an implementation tradeoff and requires an SMT-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits the tradeoff leaf, but the scalar objective J_lambda is a proposed formalization, not a standard SMT principle established by the record. Neither the objective nor the asserted relationship between explanation minimization, theory checks, and downstream search is cited. An SMT-specific source is needed to determine whether this formulation is supportable.

children.title: Incremental SMT Architecture
children.top_down_role: Internal mechanisms supporting standardized incremental and assumption-based interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Backtrackable Theory State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trail-indexed representation of incremental theory-solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L=(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n)\) be the current assertion trail. A backtrackable theory state is a sequence \((S_0,\ldots,S_n)\) with \(S_i=\operatorname{extend}(S_{i-1},\ell_i)\). Each checkpoint \(k\) stores enough information to restore \(S_k\). Backtracking from level \(n\) to \(k\) removes precisely the effects of \(\ell_{k+1},\ldots,\ell_n\), while retaining all consequences represented by \(S_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A theory solver records trail-indexed checkpoints so that backtracking removes exactly the assertions and derived state above a chosen boundary.
assumptions_latex: Each trail literal is accepted by a sound incremental theory-state update.
Checkpoint restoration reverses all updates performed after the checkpoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{restore}(S_n,k)=S_k\) for every stored boundary \(0\leq k\leq n\).

notation.meaning: theory state after the first i trail literals

review_flags: No supplied source concerns incremental SMT state restoration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind matches the topic and the trail-indexed abstraction is internally coherent. Nonetheless, exact checkpoint and restoration semantics vary among incremental theory solvers, and no source supports the claimed state representation or the exact restoration equation. A specific incremental-SMT architecture reference is required.

children.title: Context Scoping
children.top_down_role: Organization of assertions and solver state into nested incremental contexts.

knowledge_statements.title: Context Scoping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stack discipline for creating incremental SMT assertion scopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input is a solver context stack \((F_0,\ldots,F_d)\) and backtrackable state \(S_d\). The operation \(\operatorname{push}()\) creates an empty frame \(F_{d+1}=\varnothing\), records a restoration checkpoint for \(S_d\), and increments the depth. Subsequent assertions are inserted into \(F_{d+1}\) and propagated incrementally. A satisfiability query at depth \(d+1\) concerns \(\bigcup_{i=0}^{d+1}F_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Push creates an empty assertion frame and a matching theory-state checkpoint; later assertions belong to that new scope.
assumptions_latex: The context uses properly nested stack scopes.
The solver state supports checkpoint creation and restoration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After \(\operatorname{push}()\), the active formula is initially unchanged and the scope depth is \(d+1\).
review_flags: No supplied locator documents incremental SMT push semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is suitable for context scoping, but the statement identifies push with creation of both an empty assertion frame and a theory-state checkpoint. That is a plausible implementation model rather than universal API semantics, and no cited source establishes it. A solver specification or incremental-SMT reference with a precise push locator is required.

children.title: Context Retraction
children.top_down_role: Removal or deactivation of context-local assertions and derived state.

knowledge_statements.title: Context Retraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stack-disciplined removal of incremental SMT scopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input is a context stack \((F_0,\ldots,F_d)\) with \(d>0\) and checkpoints aligned with frame boundaries. The operation \(\operatorname{pop}(m)\), where \(1\leq m\leq d\), discards frames \(F_{d-m+1},\ldots,F_d\), restores the checkpoint at depth \(d-m\), and sets the active formula to \(\bigcup_{i=0}^{d-m}F_i\). Any learned object retained after restoration must remain valid independently of the discarded frames.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pop removes the requested top scopes, restores their boundary checkpoint, and retains only learned information valid without retracted assertions.
assumptions_latex: Scope frames and theory checkpoints are aligned.
\(1\leq m\leq d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting depth is \(d-m\), and the active assertions are exactly \(\bigcup_{i=0}^{d-m}F_i\).
review_flags: No supplied locator documents incremental SMT pop semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits context retraction, and the frame-removal semantics are coherent. The exact checkpoint behavior and the condition governing retained learned objects depend on the solver architecture, however, and no source is cited. A precise pop-semantics and incremental-learning reference is required.

children.title: Scope-Restoration Boundaries
children.top_down_role: State components requiring restoration when incremental contexts are retracted.

knowledge_statements.title: Scope-Restoration Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness condition relating assertion frames and restorable solver states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every scope depth \(k\), let \(A_k=\bigcup_{i=0}^{k}F_i\) and let \(S_k\) be the stored solver checkpoint. A scope boundary is restoration-correct exactly when restoring \(S_k\) makes the solver's active assertions equal to \(A_k\), removes every state dependency on \(F_{k+1},\ldots,F_d\), and preserves only deductions whose validity follows from \(A_k\) and the background theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restoration boundary is correct when it reinstates exactly the assertions and deductions valid at that scope depth.
assumptions_latex: Scopes are properly nested.
Every mutable solver component is either checkpointed or safely reconstructible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Active}(\operatorname{restore}(S_d,k))=A_k\), with no retained dependency on any \(F_j\) for \(j>k\).
review_flags: No supplied locator addresses correctness of incremental SMT restoration boundaries.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, but the claims about removing every state dependency and retaining only deductions valid from A_k require a precise definition of solver state, dependency, and retention. Those architecture-sensitive notions are not sourced, so the exact correctness condition cannot be validated from the supplied evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Assumption-Literal Solving
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporary solving under literals without modifying the persistent assertion stack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input is a persistent formula \(F\) and finite assumption set \(A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\). Temporarily enqueue every \(a_i\) as a designated decision and solve \(F\land\bigwedge A\). Return \(\mathsf{sat}\) with a model satisfying both \(F\) and \(A\), or return \(\mathsf{unsat}\) with \(U\subseteq A\) such that \(F\land\bigwedge U\) is inconsistent. On return, retract all temporary assumptions while leaving \(F\) persistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The solver checks a persistent formula under temporary literals, optionally returning an unsatisfiable subset, then retracts those literals.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the formula in the current persistent context.
Each \(a_i\) is a Boolean literal recognized by the solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The result decides \(F\land\bigwedge A\); an unsatisfiable result may include \(U\subseteq A\) with \(F\land\bigwedge U\models\bot\).
review_flags: No supplied source covers SMT solving under assumptions and failed-assumption cores.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits assumption-literal solving, and the persistent-versus-temporary distinction is appropriate. However, designated-decision handling, cleanup behavior, and availability and meaning of an unsatisfiable assumption subset are solver-interface properties for which no source is supplied. A precise SMT API or solver reference is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Model Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model assembly from a satisfiable incremental Boolean-theory state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input is a satisfiable active context \(F\), a total Boolean assignment \(\alpha\) for its abstraction, and theory-consistent asserted literals \(M\). For each theory component, extend the partial interpretation induced by \(M\) to a total theory model \(\mathcal M_T\); then reconcile interpretations of shared symbols and evaluate eliminated terms from reconstruction definitions. Output \(\mathcal M\) only after checking \(\mathcal M\models F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A satisfiable incremental state is extended componentwise into a total model, reconstructed through preprocessing maps, and checked against active assertions.
assumptions_latex: The active Boolean assignment satisfies every abstracted clause.
The asserted theory literals are jointly consistent in the supported theory combination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns a total interpretation \(\mathcal M\) satisfying \(\mathcal M\models F\).

notation.meaning: theory literals selected by the assignment

review_flags: Exact model-construction obligations depend on the supported theory-combination architecture.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the topic, but the proposed componentwise extension and reconciliation of shared symbols are not valid as a theory-independent algorithm without specifying the supported combination method and its hypotheses. The treatment of preprocessing reconstruction is likewise architecture-dependent. An authoritative source is required to determine and state the necessary obligations.

knowledge_statements.title: Theory-Aware Simplification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Satisfiability-preserving simplification using theory-valid equivalences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input is a formula \(F\) over theory \(T\) and a finite ordered set of guarded rewrite rules \(R\). Repeatedly select an occurrence matching \(l\sigma\) in the current formula and replace it by \(r\sigma\) only when its guard \(G\sigma\) is established and \(T\models G\rightarrow(l=r)\). Stop when no rule applies, producing \(F'\), together with reconstruction data for eliminated symbols. The required invariant is \(T\models F\leftrightarrow F'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Theory-aware simplification applies only theory-valid guarded rewrites, preserves satisfiability, and records enough information to reconstruct models.
assumptions_latex: Rule selection terminates under a fixed reduction ordering.
Every applied rule is valid in the background theory under its guard.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\models F\leftrightarrow F'\), and every model of \(F'\) can be lifted using the reconstruction data.
review_flags: No supplied locator concerns SMT theory-aware simplification or model reconstruction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits theory-aware simplification, and guarded theory-valid rewriting can support equivalence preservation. The stronger conclusion that every model of F' can be lifted does not follow solely from T-valid rewriting plus unspecified reconstruction data, especially when symbols are eliminated. No source establishes the rewrite framework, termination conditions, or reconstruction invariant.

children.title: Term-Rewrite Systems
children.top_down_role: Theory-aware rewrite families used to simplify or normalize SMT terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Term-Rewrite Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Many-sorted term rewriting used in SMT canonicalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A many-sorted term-rewrite system is a set \(R\) of sort-preserving rules \(l\to r\), where \(l\) is not a variable and every variable of \(r\) occurs in \(l\). The one-step relation \(s\to_R t\) holds when some subterm of \(s\) equals \(l\sigma\) and replacing that occurrence by \(r\sigma\) yields \(t\). A term is an \(R\)-normal form when no such step applies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A term-rewrite system replaces matched subterms by sort-correct right sides; a normal form admits no further rewrite.
assumptions_latex: Terms belong to a fixed many-sorted signature.
Substitutions respect declared sorts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s\to_R t\) exactly when \(t\) results from one contextual instance of a rule in \(R\).
review_flags: The supplied source hints do not address term-rewrite systems.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind exactly fits the leaf, and the many-sorted rewrite-system statement is mathematically standard and internally consistent. The supplied inventory contains no relevant term-rewriting source or locator, however, so the record lacks the evidence required for candidate review.

children.title: Canonical Term Representations
children.top_down_role: Normalized representations supporting equivalence detection and term sharing.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Term Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unique representatives of terms modulo a chosen theory congruence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\equiv_T\) be congruence modulo theory \(T\) on well-sorted terms. A canonical representation is a function \(\operatorname{can}_T\) satisfying \(t\equiv_T\operatorname{can}_T(t)\), idempotence \(\operatorname{can}_T(\operatorname{can}_T(t))=\operatorname{can}_T(t)\), and uniqueness \(s\equiv_T t\iff\operatorname{can}_T(s)=\operatorname{can}_T(t)\). Consequently, syntactic equality of canonical representatives decides equivalence for terms in the represented fragment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonicalization maps theory-equivalent terms to one idempotent representative, making equivalence reducible to syntactic equality in the supported fragment.
assumptions_latex: \(\equiv_T\) is a congruence on the selected well-sorted term fragment.
The canonicalization procedure is total on that fragment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s\equiv_T t\iff\operatorname{can}_T(s)=\operatorname{can}_T(t)\).
review_flags: The supplied locators do not support canonical term representations for SMT.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf, and the displayed properties correctly characterize a complete canonical representative function on a chosen fragment. Existence and totality are substantial theory- and fragment-dependent assumptions, and the represented fragment is not identified beyond the assumptions. No relevant source or precise locator is supplied.

children.title: Rewrite–Canonicalization Interaction
children.top_down_role: Effects of rewrite choices on canonical forms, sharing, plus downstream reasoning.

knowledge_statements.title: Rewrite–Canonicalization Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point composition of sound rewriting and canonical normalization for well-sorted ground SMT terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G_T\) be a set of well-sorted ground terms, let \(\equiv_T\) denote equality modulo theory \(T\), and let \(R,N:\mathcal G_T\to\mathcal G_T\). Assume \(R(u)\equiv_T u\) and \(N(u)\equiv_T u\) for every \(u\in\mathcal G_T\), and assume \(N\) is idempotent and satisfies \(u\equiv_T v\Rightarrow N(u)=N(v)\). For an input \(t\in\mathcal G_T\), set \(t_0=N(t)\) and \(t_{k+1}=N(R(t_k))\). If some \(k\) satisfies \(t_{k+1}=t_k\), return \(t_k\). The returned term satisfies \(t_k\equiv_T t\), \(N(t_k)=t_k\), and \(N(R(t_k))=t_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate theory-sound rewriting with canonicalization. If the combined update reaches a fixed point, the returned term is theory-equivalent to the input, canonical, and stable under the combined rewrite–canonicalization update.
assumptions_latex: \(R,N:\mathcal G_T\to\mathcal G_T\) are theory-sound.
\(N\) is idempotent and canonical for \(\equiv_T\).
The iteration reaches a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t_k\equiv_T t\), \(N(t_k)=t_k\), and \(N(R(t_k))=t_k\).

notation.meaning: Set of well-sorted ground terms under consideration

children.title: Variable Elimination
children.top_down_role: Removal of variables through theory-compatible preprocessing transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitional elimination of one variable with an explicit reconstruction map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F(x,\mathbf y)=D(x,\mathbf y)\land G(x,\mathbf y)\), suppose \(D\) determines \(x\) by \(x=t(\mathbf y)\), where \(x\) does not occur in \(t\). Form \(F'(\mathbf y)=G(t(\mathbf y),\mathbf y)\). Solve \(F'\); for every model \(M'\models F'\), reconstruct \(M\) by retaining the interpretation of \(\mathbf y\) and assigning \(x^M=t^{M'}\). The transformation preserves satisfiability because \(\exists x\,F(x,\mathbf y)\) and \(F'(\mathbf y)\) are equivalent in the ambient theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate a definitionally determined variable by substitution, solve the reduced formula, and reconstruct the removed value from its defining term.
assumptions_latex: \(D(x,\mathbf y)\) is theory-equivalent to \(x=t(\mathbf y)\).
\(x\notin\operatorname{FV}(t)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\models \exists x\,F(x,\mathbf y)\leftrightarrow F'(\mathbf y)\), with \(x^M=t^{M'}\) reconstructing a model.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: definitional variable elimination by substitution is a standard equivalence-preserving transformation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definitional-elimination algorithm is mathematically plausible and fits the leaf, but it has no citation or inspectable locator. The unrelated local inventory cannot support the SMT transformation and reconstruction claim.

children.title: Term Substitution
children.top_down_role: Replacement of variables or terms using established equalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Term Substitution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous, capture-avoiding substitution in many-sorted first-order terms and formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A substitution \(\sigma\) is a finite sort-preserving map from variables to terms. For a variable \(x\), define \(x\sigma=\sigma(x)\) when \(x\in\operatorname{dom}(\sigma)\), and define \(x\sigma=x\) otherwise. Extend it to terms by \(f(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\sigma=f(t_1\sigma,\ldots,t_n\sigma)\), and extend it homomorphically to atoms and Boolean connectives. For \(Q\in\{\forall,\exists\}\), let \(\sigma\setminus x\) be \(\sigma\) with any mapping for \(x\) removed. If \(x\) occurs free in no term in the range of \(\sigma\), define \((Qx\,\varphi)\sigma=Qx\,(\varphi(\sigma\setminus x))\). Otherwise choose a same-sorted variable \(z\) fresh for \(\varphi\), the domain of \(\sigma\), and the variables occurring in its range, alpha-rename the displayed binder from \(x\) to \(z\), and define \((Qx\,\varphi)\sigma=Qz\,((\varphi[x:=z])(\sigma\setminus x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A substitution is a finite sort-preserving variable-to-term map extended recursively to terms and formulas; mappings for bound variables are suppressed, and binders are alpha-renamed when necessary to prevent capture.
assumptions_latex: \(\sigma\) maps every variable in its finite domain to a term of the same sort.
In the alpha-renaming clause, \(z\) has the sort of \(x\) and is fresh for the formula and substitution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recursively defined operation \(E\mapsto E\sigma\) is sort-correct and capture-avoiding.

notation.meaning: Substitution with any mapping for x removed

children.title: Model-Reconstruction Obligations
children.top_down_role: Information retained to recover models after elimination or substitution.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Reconstruction Obligations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness obligations for lifting reduced-formula models through an SMT transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a transformation map an original formula \(F\) to a reduced formula \(F'\), and let \(\rho\) map models of \(F'\) to interpretations of the original signature. Model reconstruction is correct when both obligations hold: for every \(M'\models_T F'\), the interpretation \(\rho(M')\) is defined and satisfies \(F\); and every value assigned by \(\rho\) respects the sorts, function congruence, and theory axioms of \(T\). If optimization objectives were transformed, reconstruction must additionally preserve their values under the declared objective correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reconstruction map must lift every reduced model to a well-sorted original model satisfying the original formula and preserving any transformed objective value.
assumptions_latex: \(F'\) results from a declared transformation of \(F\).
\(M'\models_T F'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(M')\models_T F\), and transformed objective values agree with their original counterparts when objectives are present.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sound lifting and theory consistency are standard model-reconstruction obligations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated lifting, theory-consistency, and objective-preservation conditions fit the model-reconstruction leaf, but no source or locator supports these obligations.

children.title: Elimination-Safety Regimes
children.top_down_role: Theory fragments plus contexts where elimination preserves required solver outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination-Safety Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Satisfiability, reconstruction, equivalence, and optimization conditions for eliminating variables from formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\) be a formula in theory \(T\), where \(\mathbf x\) are the variables to eliminate, and let \(E(F)(\mathbf y)\) contain no variable from \(\mathbf x\). The transformation is satisfiability-safe when \(F\) is \(T\)-satisfiable exactly when \(E(F)\) is \(T\)-satisfiable. It is model-reconstruction-safe when there is a computable map \(\rho\) such that every \(M'\models_T E(F)\) lifts to an interpretation \(\rho(M')\models_T F\). It is equivalence-safe when \(T\models \forall\mathbf y\,((\exists\mathbf x\,F(\mathbf x,\mathbf y))\leftrightarrow E(F)(\mathbf y))\). For an optimization problem, it is objective-safe when the transformation and reconstruction preserve the feasible objective-value set, and therefore preserve the optimum whenever it exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable elimination can preserve satisfiability, reconstructability of original models, existential logical equivalence, or feasible objective values; each regime requires its corresponding condition.
assumptions_latex: \(F(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\) is a well-sorted formula in theory \(T\).
\(E(F)(\mathbf y)\) contains none of the eliminated variables \(\mathbf x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Safety is classified by satisfiability equivalence, model reconstruction, equivalence to \(\exists\mathbf x\,F\), and preservation of feasible objective values.

notation.meaning: Variables retained in the reduced formula

knowledge_statements.title: Theory-Specific Rewriting Pipelines
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered fixed-point normalization using rewrite stages specialized to one background theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a formula \(F\) in theory \(T\), choose stages \(R_1,\ldots,R_m\). Each changing application of a stage must either preserve \(T\)-equivalence or preserve satisfiability while producing reconstruction data, and must strictly decrease a common well-founded measure \(\mu\). Initialize \(G=F\) with identity reconstruction data. In the order \(i=1,\ldots,m\), replace \(G\) by a canonicalized form of \(R_i(G)\) and compose any reconstruction data. Repeat complete passes until no stage changes \(G\). Return the stable formula \(G^*\) and the composed reconstruction data. Typical stages normalize theory operators, propagate theory constants, eliminate definitional variables, and simplify theory-valid or theory-inconsistent atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply ordered theory-specific rewrite stages in repeated passes until every stage is stable, while preserving the declared semantics and composing all required model-reconstruction data.
assumptions_latex: Each \(R_i\) is theory-equivalent or is equisatisfiable with valid reconstruction data.
Every changing stage application strictly decreases a common well-founded measure \(\mu\).
Canonicalization preserves the declared theory semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The process terminates at \(G^*\), which preserves the declared semantics of \(F\); the composed data reconstruct original models when required.

notation.meaning: Formula stable under every pipeline stage

children.title: Preprocessing Pipelines
children.top_down_role: Transformation pipelines applied before the main SMT search.

knowledge_statements.title: Preprocessing Pipelines
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantics-preserving transformation sequence executed before Boolean-theory search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an SMT formula \(F\), initialize \(F_0=F\) and an identity reconstruction map. Apply a finite sequence of transformations \(P_1,\ldots,P_k\) before search, setting \(F_i=P_i(F_{i-1})\). Each stage must preserve satisfiability and either preserve models directly or append sufficient reconstruction data. Stages may simplify, canonicalize, propagate constants, eliminate variables, or introduce fresh definitional symbols. Return \(F_k\) to the search engine.
