If search produces \(M_k\models F_k\), compose the recorded maps in reverse order to obtain a model of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Before search, run a finite sequence of satisfiability-preserving transformations and record enough information to reconstruct an original-formula model afterward.
assumptions_latex: Every \(P_i\) preserves satisfiability under the ambient theory.
Non-model-preserving stages provide valid reconstruction maps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is satisfiable exactly when \(F_k\) is satisfiable, and any model of \(F_k\) can be lifted to a model of \(F\).

notation.meaning: Model returned for the preprocessed formula

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: preprocessing as composed equisatisfiable transformations with reverse model reconstruction is standard SMT architecture
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits preprocessing and consistently requires reverse model reconstruction, but no SMT source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Inprocessing During Search
children.top_down_role: Transformations applied while search state and learned information evolve.

knowledge_statements.title: Inprocessing During Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant-preserving formula transformation interleaved with an active SMT search state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a search state be \(S=(F,A,L)\), where \(F\) is the current formula, \(A\) the active assignment, and \(L\) the retained learned constraints. At selected search points, apply an inprocessing transformation \(I\) and obtain \(S'=(F',A',L')\). Require \(F'\land L'\) to be equisatisfiable with \(F\land L\), translate or discard assignments invalidated by the transformation, retain only constraints sound for the transformed state, and record model reconstruction data. Resume propagation and theory checking from \(S'\); termination returns either unsatisfiability or a reconstructed model of the original formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transform the formula during search only while preserving satisfiability, repairing the active assignment, maintaining sound learned constraints, and retaining model reconstruction data.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is applied at a state where affected assignments and learned constraints can be identified.
Every retained learned constraint is entailed by the transformed problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Search from \(S'\) preserves the satisfiability result and permits reconstruction of any satisfying model for the original formula.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: invariant-preserving simplification interleaved with search is standard SAT/SMT inprocessing
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed inprocessing invariants are plausible, but their sufficiency for an active SMT state—including assignment repair and learned-constraint retention—requires an architecture-specific authoritative source.

children.title: Partial Model Construction
children.top_down_role: Construction of model information limited to relevant symbols or constrained values.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Model Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model candidate defined only on terms and atoms relevant to the current SMT state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a theory \(T\) and a finite relevant set \(U\) of ground terms and atoms, a partial model is a sort-correct partial interpretation \(p\) assigning values to selected terms in \(U\) and truth values to selected atoms in \(U\). It must respect interpreted constants and functions whenever all required arguments and results are assigned, assign equal values to terms constrained equal, and satisfy every asserted literal whose value is defined. Unassigned terms, atoms, and function applications remain unspecified; therefore \(p\) need not yet be a total first-order structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial model consistently interprets only relevant selected terms and atoms, satisfying defined asserted literals while leaving all other semantic values unspecified.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is a finite set of well-sorted ground terms and atoms.
Assignments in \(p\) are sort-correct.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\) is locally consistent on its domain but may leave symbols and applications uninterpreted.

notation.meaning: Finite set of relevant ground expressions

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: partial interpretations over relevant ground expressions are standard in SMT model construction
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but “partial model” has several non-equivalent formal meanings in SMT and model theory. No source identifies or supports this selected ground-expression interpretation.

children.title: Total Model Construction
children.top_down_role: Construction of complete interpretations for the required model vocabulary.

knowledge_statements.title: Total Model Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction target interpreting every symbol and satisfying the complete asserted formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a many-sorted signature \(\Sigma\) and theory \(T\), a total model of a formula \(F\) is a \(\Sigma\)-structure \(M\) with a nonempty carrier for every sort, a total function of the declared type for every function symbol, an element for every constant, and a total relation for every predicate. Construction is successful exactly when all axioms of \(T\) and the formula hold in \(M\), namely \(M\models T\cup\{F\}\). Every ground term then has a value and every ground formula has a truth value in \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A total model interprets every sort and symbol over full domains and satisfies both the background theory and the asserted formula.
assumptions_latex: \(\Sigma\) is a well-sorted first-order signature.
Every sort carrier of \(M\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\models T\cup\{F\}\), and evaluation is defined for every ground \(\Sigma\)-expression.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: total many-sorted first-order structures and satisfaction are standard model-theoretic definitions
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The many-sorted total-model definition is standard and internally consistent, but the record supplies no authoritative textbook section, page, or other inspectable citation.

children.title: Partial-to-Total Completion
children.top_down_role: Completion boundaries linking partial interpretations to total solver models.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-to-Total Completion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completion of an extendible partial interpretation using its finite semantic diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given theory \(T\), formula \(F\), and partial interpretation \(p\), construct a finite diagram \(\operatorname{Diag}(p)\) recording every assigned term value, asserted equality or disequality, and assigned predicate value. Invoke a model-construction procedure on \(T\cup\{F\}\cup\operatorname{Diag}(p)\). If it returns a structure \(M\), output \(M\); then \(M\) extends every assignment in \(p\) and is a total model of \(T\cup\{F\}\). If the augmented set is unsatisfiable, report that \(p\) is not extendible to a total model satisfying \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode the partial interpretation as a finite diagram and solve with it; a resulting structure is a total extension, while unsatisfiability proves non-extendibility.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a finite, sort-correct partial interpretation.
The model-construction procedure is sound and complete for the selected theory fragment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned \(M\) satisfies \(T\cup\{F\}\cup\operatorname{Diag}(p)\); otherwise no such total extension exists.

notation.meaning: Finite diagram encoding assignments of p

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: extending a partial interpretation through satisfiability of its diagram is standard model theory
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The completion idea is plausible, but the record does not explain how arbitrary assigned semantic values are named in the finite diagram or establish that the diagram faithfully encodes the chosen notion of partial interpretation. A supporting model-theory source is required before fixing the formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Theory Model Reconciliation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifier-free Nelson–Oppen model combination for disjoint, stably infinite theories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) be stably infinite first-order theories with disjoint nonlogical signatures, sharing only equality and sorts. Purify a quantifier-free conjunction as \(\varphi_1\land\varphi_2\), and let \(V\) be its shared variables. If there is a complete equality arrangement \(\alpha\) on \(V\) such that \(T_1\cup\{\varphi_1,\alpha\}\) and \(T_2\cup\{\varphi_2,\alpha\}\) are both satisfiable, then their component models can be reconciled into a model of \(T_1\cup T_2\cup\{\varphi_1\land\varphi_2\}\). Conversely, every combined model induces such a common arrangement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For disjoint stably infinite theories, component models combine exactly when they satisfy one common complete equality arrangement on all shared variables.
assumptions_latex: \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) are stably infinite and have disjoint nonlogical signatures.
\(\varphi_1\land\varphi_2\) is quantifier-free and purified.
\(\alpha\) is a complete equality arrangement on the shared variables \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_1\cup T_2\cup\{\varphi_1\land\varphi_2\}\) is satisfiable exactly when some \(\alpha\) makes both component problems satisfiable.

notation.meaning: Variables shared by the purified components
Complete equality and disequality arrangement on V

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: this is the standard quantifier-free Nelson–Oppen combination theorem for disjoint stably infinite theories
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is recognizably the quantifier-free Nelson–Oppen combination criterion and theorem is an appropriate content kind for this leaf, but no citation or theorem locator is supplied. The local optimization-book inventory does not support it.

children.title: Model Validation
children.top_down_role: Checking candidate interpretations against asserted constraints and theory semantics.

knowledge_statements.title: Model Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent validation of a purported SMT model against the original asserted formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an SMT formula \(F\) with free constants \(X\) and a candidate interpretation \(M\), independently parse \(F\), evaluate every ground term under \(M\), and check every asserted atom using a trusted evaluator for its theory. Return valid exactly when all assertions evaluate to true and every interpreted value satisfies its sort and theory-domain requirements; otherwise return invalid together with a failed assertion or ill-formed interpretation. Formally, valid may be returned only if \(M\models F\); invalid is witnessed by some assertion \(A\) with \(M\not\models A\), or by a domain violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Re-evaluate the original SMT assertions under the reported interpretation; accept only a well-sorted interpretation satisfying every assertion, and otherwise return a concrete failure witness.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) belongs to theories supported by the trusted evaluator.
\(M\) assigns every free constant needed to evaluate \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{validate}(F,M)=\mathrm{valid}\Rightarrow M\models F\).

notation.meaning: Original SMT formula or assertion set.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the Model Validation leaf and is internally coherent, but it has no citation. A specific authoritative SMT model-validation source and locator are required to support the trusted-evaluator procedure, domain checks, and failure-witness contract.

children.title: Model Repair
children.top_down_role: Correction of incomplete or inconsistent candidate interpretations.

knowledge_statements.title: Model Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained correction of an invalid candidate interpretation without changing the asserted SMT formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F\), an invalid candidate interpretation \(M_0\), an admissible repair set \(R\subseteq X\), and a cost \(d\), solve \[M^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{M}\{d(M,M_0):M\models F,\ M(x)=M_0(x)\text{ for every }x\in X\setminus R\}.\] Return \(M^*\) only after independent validation. If the feasible set is empty, return unrepairable relative to \(R\); if the optimization procedure is incomplete and finds no repair, return unknown rather than unrepairable. Ties may be resolved arbitrarily unless a deterministic rule is specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find a minimum-cost satisfying interpretation by changing only permitted assignments; validate the result, distinguish proven unrepairability from failure of an incomplete search, and preserve all protected values.
assumptions_latex: \(d(M,M_0)\ge 0\) is defined on admissible interpretations.
The repair procedure preserves the original formula \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M^*\models F\) and \(M^*(x)=M_0(x)\) for all \(x\in X\setminus R\).

notation.meaning: Set of assignments permitted to change.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Model Repair, but the proposed minimum-cost interpretation-repair semantics are not a universal SMT convention and have no cited support. A source with a specific locator must establish the admissible-repair model, optimality criterion, and distinction between proven unrepairability and incomplete search.

children.title: Validation-Failure Classification
children.top_down_role: Sources of candidate-model failure across Boolean, theory, plus combination layers.

knowledge_statements.title: Validation-Failure Classification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjoint operational classes for failures encountered while checking a reported SMT model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a formula \(F\), candidate interpretation \(M\), parser \(P\), and trusted theory evaluator \(E\), classify a validation failure by the first applicable predicate: syntax failure if \(P(F)\) or \(P(M)\) is undefined; sort failure if some interpreted symbol has an inadmissible value; coverage failure if a value required to evaluate \(F\) is absent; evaluation failure if \(E\) cannot decide a required supported operation; semantic failure if evaluation succeeds but \(M\not\models F\); validator failure if the checker violates its specified semantics. A priority order makes the reported class unique when several predicates hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classify validation failures as syntax, sort, coverage, evaluation, semantic, or validator failures, using a fixed priority order when multiple defects coexist.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) and \(E\) have specified accepted languages and failure outcomes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{class}(F,M)\in\{\mathrm{syntax},\mathrm{sort},\mathrm{coverage},\mathrm{evaluation},\mathrm{semantic},\mathrm{validator}\}\).

notation.meaning: Parser for formulas and model representations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the classification leaf, but the six classes and their priority ordering are architecture-specific rather than a standard canonical taxonomy. No evidence supports their exhaustiveness, meanings, or ordering.

children.title: Repairability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases distinguishable as locally repairable versus requiring renewed search.

knowledge_statements.title: Repairability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility boundary induced by permitted edits and the supported repair theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M_R(M_0)=\{M:M(x)=M_0(x)\text{ for all }x\in X\setminus R\}\) be the interpretations reachable by permitted repairs. The candidate is repairable exactly when \[\mathcal M_R(M_0)\cap\operatorname{Mod}(F)\ne\varnothing.\] It is unrepairable relative to \(R\) when this intersection is empty. Even when the intersection is nonempty, an implementation cannot guarantee finding a repair unless its search is complete for the formula fragment and repair language. Unsupported values, undecidable theory fragments, or an unbounded cost infimum not attained therefore form procedural boundaries distinct from semantic unrepairability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repair is semantically possible exactly when an allowed modification satisfies the formula; guaranteed discovery additionally requires completeness for the theory and repair language and attainment of any requested optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(R\subseteq X\) fixes the permitted edit coordinates.
\(\operatorname{Mod}(F)\) denotes all well-sorted models of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_0\text{ is repairable relative to }R\iff\mathcal M_R(M_0)\cap\operatorname{Mod}(F)\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Class of models satisfying the formula.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the reachability-intersection criterion is coherent relative to the stated repair framework. That framework and the listed procedural boundaries nevertheless lack any authoritative citation with an inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver Portfolios
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound orchestration of multiple SMT procedures on one instance under shared resource limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an SMT instance \(F\), solvers \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\), and resource allocations \(b_1,\ldots,b_k\), run the solvers concurrently or according to a schedule. Accept SAT only with a model \(M\) passing independent validation, and accept UNSAT only with a proof or certificate accepted by a trusted checker; otherwise continue until a certified answer is obtained or the global budget expires. Conflicting certified answers signal an assurance failure. On budget exhaustion without a certified result, return unknown. The portfolio is complete for a class \(\mathcal C\) if its schedule grants unbounded progress to at least one sound complete member for \(\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Schedule several SMT solvers, accept only independently certified answers, report unknown on exhausted resources, and inherit completeness when a complete member receives sufficient progress.
assumptions_latex: Every accepted SAT or UNSAT result is checked independently.
The scheduling policy specifies each solver's resource allocation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{portfolio}(F)\in\{\mathrm{SAT},\mathrm{UNSAT},\mathrm{unknown},\mathrm{assurance\ failure}\}\).

notation.meaning: Resource allocation for the constituent solver.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An orchestration algorithm is suitable for Solver Portfolios, but no source supports the certification protocol or the stated completeness condition. In particular, the meaning of granting unbounded progress and its scheduling assumptions require authoritative treatment.

children.title: Parallel Boolean Search
children.top_down_role: Concurrent exploration or sharing mechanisms within the Boolean search layer.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Boolean Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause-sharing parallelization of the Boolean abstraction in a lazy SMT architecture.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B(F)\) be the Boolean abstraction of an SMT formula. Initialize workers with \(B(F)\) and diversify them by search seeds, branching heuristics, restart policies, or disjoint guiding paths. Each worker performs sound CDCL search and may publish a learned clause \(C\) only when \(B(F)\) together with currently valid theory lemmas entails \(C\). Imported clauses are checked or trusted under the same invariant. Stop when a worker produces a theory-consistent total assignment, a checked refutation, or the resource budget expires; return respectively SAT with a validated model, UNSAT with a checked certificate, or unknown.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run diversified CDCL workers over one Boolean abstraction, share only entailed clauses, and terminate with a validated model, checked refutation, or unknown.
assumptions_latex: All workers use the same Boolean abstraction \(B(F)\).
Shared theory lemmas remain valid for the original formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\text{ is shared}\Rightarrow B(F)\land T_F\models C\).

notation.meaning: Boolean abstraction of the SMT formula.
Conjunction of valid theory lemmas learned for the instance.
A learned clause proposed for sharing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Parallel Boolean Search, but its clause-sharing invariant, theory-lemma interaction, and certified termination outcomes are unsupported. A parallel SMT or parallel CDCL source with a specific section or theorem locator is required.

children.title: Parallel Theory Search
children.top_down_role: Concurrent theory reasoning across solvers, partitions, or candidate states.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Theory Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concurrent theory reasoning for candidate Boolean assignments or independent theory partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a Boolean assignment \(\alpha\) selecting theory literals \(L(\alpha)\), dispatch sound theory procedures to analyze all of \(L(\alpha)\), alternative partitions, or alternative explanation strategies. A worker reporting inconsistency must return a subset \(K\subseteq L(\alpha)\) with \(T\models\neg\bigwedge K\); the orchestrator may learn \(\bigvee_{\ell\in K}\neg\ell\). A worker reporting consistency supplies a partial theory model, and SAT is returned only after the partial models are compatible and extend to a validated model of the original formula. If no decisive result is obtained within the budget, return unknown.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Analyze theory literals concurrently; translate checked inconsistent cores into theory lemmas, reconcile consistent partial models, and report SAT only after whole-model validation.
assumptions_latex: Each theory worker is sound for its assigned fragment.
Combination interfaces expose all equalities or shared values required for compatibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\text{ inconsistent in }T\Rightarrow T\models\bigvee_{\ell\in K}\neg\ell\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Parallel Theory Search, and the inconsistent-core implication is standard in form. However, the dispatch alternatives, partial-model compatibility requirements, and combination-interface assumptions have no cited source and depend on the theory-combination architecture.

children.title: Cross-Layer Synchronization
children.top_down_role: Exchange of assignments, conflicts, propagations, plus learned information across parallel layers.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Layer Synchronization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness conditions for exchanging assignments, lemmas, and cancellation signals between Boolean and theory workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate every Boolean trail and theory task with a monotonically ordered context identifier \(e\). A theory result derived in context \(e\) may affect the current Boolean search only if either its premises remain active or its conclusion is globally entailed by the background theory and original encoding. On backtracking to context \(e'<e\), cancel or ignore results depending on retracted premises. Publish a theory conflict only with an explanation over Boolean-visible literals, and publish consistency only for the complete dispatched literal set. Termination detection must wait until all work capable of producing an earlier decisive result is completed or cancelled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tag cross-layer work by context, discard stale premise-dependent results after backtracking, exchange explained theory consequences, and coordinate cancellation and termination consistently.
assumptions_latex: Context identifiers respect Boolean trail creation and retraction.
Every communicated theory consequence records its premises.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e'<e\land\operatorname{premises}(r)\not\subseteq\operatorname{trail}(e')\Rightarrow r\text{ is ignored at }e'\).

notation.meaning: A theory result communicated across layers.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A condition is an appropriate role for this synchronization leaf, but the epoch discipline, stale-result rule, publication requirements, and termination-detection condition describe a particular protocol without evidence. A source must identify the architecture and support these conditions.

children.title: Incomplete Front-End Procedures
children.top_down_role: Fast procedures used without a completeness guarantee over the full input class.

knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Front-End Procedures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided or heuristic cascade stages that may decide some instances but cannot guarantee termination on their input class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A front-end procedure \(P\) for an instance class \(\mathcal C\) is sound but incomplete when every conclusive answer it returns is correct, yet there exists \(F\in\mathcal C\) for which \(P(F)\) returns unknown or does not terminate although \(F\) has a definite satisfiability status. Within a cascade, impose a finite stage budget and forward every nonconclusive instance unchanged, or with an equisatisfiable transformation and recoverable model map, to the next stage. A timeout, heuristic failure, or unsupported feature is therefore an escalation event, not evidence of SAT or UNSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incomplete front end may soundly solve easy cases but must escalate every inconclusive case; timeout, unsupported syntax, or heuristic failure proves neither satisfiability nor unsatisfiability.
assumptions_latex: Conclusive outputs of \(P\) are sound.
Each front-end stage has an enforceable escalation condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(F)=\mathrm{unknown}\not\Rightarrow F\in\mathrm{SAT}\cup\mathrm{UNSAT}\text{ with either status identified}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is suitable, and the distinction between sound conclusive outputs and inconclusive outcomes is mathematically plausible. No cited source supports the cascade-specific requirements concerning finite budgets, unchanged or equisatisfiable forwarding, and model recovery.

children.title: Complete Backstop Procedures
children.top_down_role: Procedures supplying completeness for their supported theory fragments.

knowledge_statements.title: Complete Backstop Procedures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness inherited from a final decision procedure that receives every unresolved admissible instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be a sound, terminating, and complete decision procedure for an input class \(\mathcal C\). A cascade has \(B\) as a complete backstop when every instance unresolved by earlier stages reaches \(B\) after finitely many steps, and each preceding transformation preserves satisfiability and provides any model reconstruction required by the output contract. Then every \(F\in\mathcal C\) receives a correct SAT or UNSAT answer. Earlier incomplete stages may alter performance but do not reduce completeness, provided they cannot emit unchecked conclusions, discard unresolved instances, or prevent eventual execution of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sound complete terminating final solver makes the cascade complete when every unresolved instance reaches it through satisfiability-preserving transformations after finite front-end processing.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is sound, complete, and terminating on \(\mathcal C\).
Every unresolved \(F\in\mathcal C\) reaches \(B\) after finitely many stages.
All preprocessing transformations are satisfiability-preserving.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall F\in\mathcal C,\ \operatorname{cascade}(F)\in\{\mathrm{SAT},\mathrm{UNSAT}\}\text{ and is correct}\).

notation.meaning: Class on which the backstop is complete.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits Complete Backstop Procedures, and the stated hypotheses are broadly sufficient for the conclusion. The inheritance-of-completeness claim and its transformation and reconstruction conditions still require an authoritative source with a precise locator.

children.title: Cascade Escalation Policies
children.top_down_role: Criteria for transferring unresolved instances between cascade stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Cascade Escalation Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic transfer of unresolved instances through increasingly general SMT procedures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given ordered stages \(P_1,\ldots,P_k\), budgets \(b_1,\ldots,b_k\), and an instance \(F_1=F\), run \(P_i(F_i)\) for at most \(b_i\). Return a checked SAT or UNSAT result immediately. On unknown, timeout, unsupported input, or rejected certificate, construct \(F_{i+1}=T_i(F_i)\), where \(T_i\) is equisatisfiable and records a model-reconstruction map, then continue. If no stage returns a checked result, return unknown. Fairness requires that no incomplete stage indefinitely delays every later stage; completeness requires eventual admission to a complete backstop.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply ordered solver stages under explicit budgets, accept only checked answers, and escalate every inconclusive case through equisatisfiable transformations to later procedures.
assumptions_latex: Each stage has a finite enforceable budget or yields voluntarily.
Each transformation \(T_i\) preserves satisfiability and supports model reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_i(F_i)\text{ inconclusive}\Rightarrow F_{i+1}=T_i(F_i)\text{ is escalated}\).

notation.meaning: Solver procedure at cascade stage i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role matches Cascade Escalation Policies, but this particular checked-result, budget, transformation, and fairness protocol has no supporting citation. Its certificate-rejection behavior and model-reconstruction requirement are architecture-specific.

children.title: Cascade Completeness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which the combined cascade retains a completeness guarantee.

knowledge_statements.title: Cascade Completeness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary orchestration conditions separating complete solver cascades from merely sound partial procedures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an input class \(\mathcal C\), a cascade is complete only if every \(F\in\mathcal C\) follows a finite or fair execution path that reaches a procedure complete for the residual instance class, unless an earlier stage already returns a correct decision. Completeness can fail when an incomplete stage may run forever, escalation omits an unresolved case, preprocessing is not satisfiability-preserving, the backstop excludes a reachable residual fragment, or required resources are globally bounded. Thus a sound complete backstop alone is insufficient: reachability, transformation correctness, domain coverage, and fair resource allocation are also required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cascade completeness ends where unresolved cases can be trapped, transformed unsoundly, excluded from the backstop's domain, or denied the unbounded resources required for termination.
assumptions_latex: The cascade is evaluated on a specified class \(\mathcal C\).
Correct decisions returned by individual stages are sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{complete}(\operatorname{cascade},\mathcal C)\Rightarrow\operatorname{fair}\land\operatorname{coverage}\land\operatorname{preservation}\).

notation.meaning: Input class for the completeness claim.
Every reachable residual instance lies in a decisive stage's domain.
Interstage transformations preserve the decision status.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind matches the leaf, and the listed failure modes are plausible. The asserted necessary conditions and the use of fair execution paths are not sourced, while their exact necessity depends on the cascade and resource model.

children.title: Modular Theory Combination
children.top_down_role: Combination mechanisms, theorem families, applicability conditions, model constructions, and failure boundaries for multiple background theories.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Decision Procedures: An Algorithmic Point of View
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Combining decision procedures
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Decision Procedures: An Algorithmic Point of View

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Combined theories and modular decision procedures
Simplification by cooperating decision procedures

children.title: Nelson–Oppen Theory Combination
children.top_down_role: The classical combination family, separated into representations, information exchange, and theorem applicability.

children.title: Formula Purification
children.top_down_role: Separation of mixed-theory terms into theory-specific constraint components.

knowledge_statements.title: Formula Purification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Purification of quantifier-free formulas over two disjoint theory signatures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Sigma_1\cap\Sigma_2=\Sigma_0\), where \(\Sigma_0\) contains only equality and shared sorts. Given a quantifier-free formula \(F\), repeatedly replace every maximal alien subterm \(t\) occurring inside an atom of the other signature by a fresh variable \(v_t\), and conjoin the defining equality \(v_t=t\). The resulting formula \(F^{\mathrm p}\) contains only pure atoms and satisfies \[F\text{ is satisfiable in }T_1\cup T_2\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F^{\mathrm p}\text{ is satisfiable in }T_1\cup T_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace each cross-theory subterm by a fresh variable and its defining equality, obtaining an equisatisfiable formula whose atoms each belong to one component theory.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is quantifier-free over \(\Sigma_1\cup\Sigma_2\).
\(\Sigma_1\) and \(\Sigma_2\) share only equality and designated sorts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^{\mathrm p}\) is pure by theory and equisatisfiable with \(F\).

notation.meaning: purified form of the input formula
fresh variable representing alien subterm t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the Formula Purification leaf and is mathematically plausible, but no cited source or inspectable locator supports the purification procedure and its equisatisfiability claim.

children.title: Interface Variable Introduction
children.top_down_role: Fresh shared variables representing cross-theory term boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Interface Variable Introduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fresh-variable step used during Nelson–Oppen purification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a formula containing a maximal alien subterm \(t\) in a theory-pure context. Choose a fresh variable \(v_t\) of the same sort, replace every selected occurrence of \(t\) by \(v_t\), and add the constraint \(v_t=t\) to the component containing the symbols of \(t\). Reuse \(v_t\) for syntactically identical selected subterms. Stop when no atom contains nonshared symbols from both component signatures; output the transformed formula and all introduced variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introduce a same-sort fresh variable for each alien subterm, add its defining equality, and continue until every atom is theory-pure.
assumptions_latex: \(t\) is well-sorted.
\(v_t\) does not occur in the current formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists v_t\,(v_t=t\land F[v_t/t])\) is equivalent to \(F\) with respect to the original free variables.

notation.meaning: formula obtained by replacing selected occurrences of t by the interface variable

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic kind fits the interface-variable introduction step, and the variables and freshness condition are stated coherently. An authoritative source with a specific locator is required for the transformation and equivalence claim.

children.title: Purified-Constraint Partitioning
children.top_down_role: Allocation of purified constraints to component theory solvers.

knowledge_statements.title: Purified-Constraint Partitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition of a purified conjunction into component-theory constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a purified conjunction \(F^{\mathrm p}\), assign each conjunct whose nonlogical symbols lie in \(\Sigma_i\) to \(\Gamma_i\). Shared equalities may be assigned to either component or recorded separately. Then \[F^{\mathrm p}\equiv \Gamma_1\land\Gamma_2\land\Gamma_0,\] where every atom of \(\Gamma_i\) belongs to the language of \(T_i\), and \(\Gamma_0\) contains only equalities or disequalities over shared variables. The partition preserves satisfiability in \(T_1\cup T_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A purified conjunction separates into one pure constraint set per theory plus optional shared equalities and disequalities, without changing satisfiability.
assumptions_latex: \(F^{\mathrm p}\) is a conjunction of purified literals.
\(\Sigma_1\cap\Sigma_2=\Sigma_0\) contains only the shared equality language.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^{\mathrm p}\) and \(\Gamma_1\land\Gamma_2\land\Gamma_0\) have the same models.

notation.meaning: constraints assigned to component theory i
constraints using only the shared equality vocabulary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation matches purified-constraint partitioning, but the record has no evidence for the partition convention, treatment of shared literals, or satisfiability-preservation statement.

children.title: Interface-Vocabulary Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Shared symbols eligible for communication between component theories.

knowledge_statements.title: Interface-Vocabulary Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Permitted communication vocabulary for signature-disjoint Nelson–Oppen combination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_i\) be the variables occurring in \(\Gamma_i\), and let \(V=V_1\cap V_2\) be the same-sort shared variables. The interface-vocabulary condition is that every formula exchanged between component solvers is a Boolean combination of equalities \(x=y\) with \(x,y\in V\) of the same sort. No theory-specific function, predicate, or constant symbol may occur in an exchanged formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Component solvers communicate only same-sort equalities or disequalities among variables occurring in both purified partitions, never theory-specific symbols.
assumptions_latex: \(\Gamma_1\) and \(\Gamma_2\) are theory-pure.
\(V_1\) and \(V_2\) respect the common sort discipline.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Voc}_{\mathrm{exchange}}\subseteq\{x=y:x,y\in V\text{ have the same sort}\}\).

notation.meaning: set of variables shared by both component partitions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but no source supports the asserted exchange boundary. The notation also describes \(\operatorname{Voc}_{\mathrm{exchange}}\) as formulas while the conclusion treats it as a set of atomic equalities; a source is needed to determine the intended formal version.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality Arrangements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete equality type over a finite set of shared variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite same-sorted set \(V\), an equality arrangement is an equivalence relation \(\sim\) on \(V\), represented by \[\alpha_{\sim}=\bigwedge_{x\sim y}(x=y)\land\bigwedge_{x\not\sim y}(x\ne y),\] with one representative literal per unordered pair. In a many-sorted language, the construction is applied independently within each sort. Thus every pair of same-sort interface variables is declared equal or distinct, consistently with reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality arrangement is a consistent complete choice of equality or disequality for every same-sort pair of shared variables.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite.
Equality is interpreted as identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_{\sim}\) uniquely specifies a partition of \(V\) into equality classes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit Equality Arrangements, but no source with a specific locator is supplied for this complete equality-type formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality Sharing Between Theories
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exchange loop for interface equalities in Nelson–Oppen combination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize each solver with its purified constraint set \(\Gamma_i\). Whenever solver \(i\) establishes an interface equality \(x=y\) entailed by \(T_i\cup\Gamma_i\), add that equality to every other component containing \(x,y\). Repeat until a component reports inconsistency or no new interface equality is produced. In a complete convex regime, return satisfiable at the fixed point if every component remains satisfiable; in a nonconvex regime, supplement the loop by equality-arrangement branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solvers repeatedly exchange entailed equalities over shared variables until conflict or closure; nonconvex theories additionally require case splitting.
assumptions_latex: Each component procedure decides satisfiability of its received constraints.
Only interface equalities are exchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, either some \(T_i\cup\Gamma_i\) is inconsistent or the shared equality information is closed under component consequences.

notation.meaning: current constraint set of component solver i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exchange loop fits the algorithm leaf, but the satisfiable-at-fixed-point conclusion depends on precise Nelson–Oppen hypotheses, including the applicable signature, stable-infiniteness, and convexity conditions. No source is supplied to establish the correct hypothesis set.

children.title: Convex Theory-Exchange Regimes
children.top_down_role: Equality exchange for combinations whose component theories have convex consequence behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(\Gamma\) is a conjunction of theory literals.
All displayed variable pairs are same-sorted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Entailed equality disjunctions can be communicated through at least one individually entailed equality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality propagation when every component theory is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A theory \(T\) is convex for equality if, for every conjunction \(\Gamma\) of literals and every finite family \(\{(x_j,y_j):1\le j\le m\}\) of same-sort variable pairs, \[T\cup\Gamma\models\bigvee_{j=1}^{m}x_j=y_j\quad\Longrightarrow\quad T\cup\Gamma\models x_k=y_k\text{ for some }k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}.\] Consequently, when all component theories are convex, equality exchange may propagate individually entailed interface equalities; no branching solely to select one disjunct of an entailed equality disjunction is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In convex theories, any entailed finite disjunction of interface equalities contains an individually entailed equality, so no branching is needed solely to select a member of such a disjunction.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Theory-Exchange Regimes

children.title: Nonconvex Theory-Exchange Regimes
children.top_down_role: Disjunctive equality exchange required by nonconvex component theories.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Theory-Exchange Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of equality-only propagation for nonconvex component theories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A theory \(T\) is nonconvex for equality when there exist a conjunction \(\Gamma\) and same-sort pairs \((x_j,y_j)\) such that \[T\cup\Gamma\models\bigvee_{j=1}^{m}x_j=y_j\quad\text{but}\quad T\cup\Gamma\not\models x_j=y_j\text{ for every }j.\] In this case, a combination procedure that communicates only individually entailed equalities can reach a fixed point without representing the required disjunction; completeness therefore requires disjunctive exchange or branching over compatible equality arrangements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconvex theory may force a disjunction of equalities without forcing any member, making individual-equality propagation incomplete unless cases are represented.
assumptions_latex: \(T\cup\Gamma\) is satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Individual equality propagation alone is not complete for this witness.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind correctly matches the nonconvex-regime leaf, and the witness formulation is coherent. A source is still required for the claimed incompleteness of individual-equality propagation and the stated remedies.

children.title: Equality-Arrangement Branching
children.top_down_role: Search over alternative interface equalities induced by nonconvex exchange.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Arrangement Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite case splitting over shared-variable equality types.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input purified constraints \(\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2\) and their finite shared-variable set \(V\). Enumerate equivalence relations \(\sim\) on each same-sort subset of \(V\). For each combined arrangement \(\alpha_{\sim}\), test both \(T_1\cup\Gamma_1\cup\{\alpha_{\sim}\}\) and \(T_2\cup\Gamma_2\cup\{\alpha_{\sim}\}\). Return satisfiable with the first arrangement accepted by every component; return unsatisfiable if every arrangement is rejected. Equivalent implementations may generate arrangements lazily and prune inconsistent branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerate or lazily generate complete equality arrangements, accepting exactly when one arrangement is satisfiable with every purified component.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite.
Each component satisfiability test terminates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure accepts exactly when a common component-consistent equality arrangement exists.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits equality-arrangement branching, but the acceptance criterion as a decision procedure for the combined theory requires precise Nelson–Oppen compatibility hypotheses. No source is available to determine and support those hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.title: Signature-Disjointness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjoint-signature applicability condition for classical Nelson–Oppen combination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_i\) have nonlogical signature \(\Sigma_i\). The signature-disjointness condition requires \[\Sigma_1\cap\Sigma_2=\Sigma_0,\] where \(\Sigma_0\) consists only of equality and any explicitly shared sorts; no theory-specific function, predicate, or constant symbol is shared. After purification, interaction between components is therefore expressible solely through equalities and disequalities among same-sort shared variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical Nelson–Oppen components share equality and designated sorts but no theory-specific functions, predicates, or constants.
assumptions_latex: The component languages use compatible equality semantics.
Shared sorts are explicitly identified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every nonlogical symbol outside \(\Sigma_0\) belongs to at most one component signature.

notation.meaning: nonlogical signature of component theory i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the signature-disjointness leaf and states the intended classical boundary, but no authoritative Nelson–Oppen source with a specific locator is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: Stable-Infiniteness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-extension condition used by classical Nelson–Oppen completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A many-sorted theory \(T\) is stably infinite on a set of shared sorts \(S\) if every quantifier-free \(T\)-satisfiable formula \(\varphi\) has a \(T\)-model \(\mathcal M\) satisfying \(\varphi\) such that \(M_s\) is infinite for every \(s\in S\). For one-sorted theories this reduces to the requirement that every satisfiable quantifier-free formula has an infinite model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A theory is stably infinite when every satisfiable quantifier-free constraint has a model infinite on each sort shared with another component.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\) is quantifier-free.
\(S\) is the designated set of shared sorts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\cup\{\varphi\}\) has a model \(\mathcal M\) with \(|M_s|=\infty\) for all \(s\in S\).

notation.meaning: domain interpreting sort s in model M

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits Stable-Infiniteness Regimes and distinguishes the many-sorted shared-sort version from the one-sorted version. It nevertheless lacks an authoritative citation and locator.

children.title: Component Decision Requirements
children.top_down_role: Decision-procedure capabilities required from each component theory.

knowledge_statements.title: Component Decision Requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local decidability requirement for an effective Nelson–Oppen combination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each component theory \(T_i\), there must be an effective procedure \(D_i\) that terminates on every finite conjunction \(\Gamma_i\) of quantifier-free \(\Sigma_i\)-literals augmented by same-sort equalities and disequalities over interface variables, returning satisfiable exactly when \(T_i\cup\Gamma_i\) has a model. If equality propagation is used, the component must additionally decide whether \(T_i\cup\Gamma_i\models x=y\) for each relevant interface pair, either directly or through satisfiability of \(\Gamma_i\land x\ne y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each component must decide its purified constraints with interface equalities and disequalities, and support the equality-consequence queries required by exchange.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\Gamma_i\) is finite and quantifier-free.
Interface equalities are well-sorted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every local satisfiability and required interface-equality query terminates with a correct answer.

notation.meaning: decision procedure for component theory i
purified local constraints plus received interface literals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits Component Decision Requirements, and the reduction of equality entailment to a satisfiability query is plausible. No source supports the exact required input language or clarifies how this condition interacts with the sibling model-generation requirement.

children.title: Component Model-Generation Requirements
children.top_down_role: Model-construction capabilities required for combined satisfiability reasoning.

knowledge_statements.title: Component Model-Generation Requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-producing requirement for a component solver in equality-based theory combination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A component procedure for a theory \(T_i\) satisfies the model-generation requirement if, for every finite conjunction \(\Gamma_i\) of ground \(T_i\)-literals, it terminates and returns either \(\mathsf{unsat}\), only when \(T_i\cup\{\Gamma_i\}\) is inconsistent, or a \(T_i\)-model \(M_i\models\Gamma_i\). The returned model must determine the equality arrangement induced on every finite set \(V\) of interface constants: for all \(x,y\in V\), the procedure can report whether \(M_i\models x=y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each component solver must terminate, decide its ground constraints, and, when satisfiable, produce a model exposing all equalities among shared interface constants.
assumptions_latex: \(T_i\) is a first-order theory with equality.
\(\Gamma_i\) and the interface set \(V\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The component returns a sound inconsistency answer or an interface-observable model of \(\Gamma_i\).

notation.meaning: interface constants shared with other components

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard model-producing component-solver condition for equality-based theory combination
No supplied locator addresses SMT theory combination.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but no cited source establishes that this exact terminating, model-producing, interface-observable requirement is the intended component condition.

children.title: Requirement Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of component outputs with the selected theory-combination framework.

knowledge_statements.title: Requirement Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility of component models over their common equality interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_1\models\Gamma_1\) and \(M_2\models\Gamma_2\) be component models over disjoint nonlogical signatures sharing only sorts and equality. They are interface-compatible on shared constants \(V\) if they induce the same arrangement: \[M_1\models x=y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad M_2\models x=y\qquad(x,y\in V),\] and, for every shared sort \(\sigma\), their \(\sigma\)-carriers can be chosen with equal cardinality. Under these conditions, bijections matching interpretations of \(V\) identify the shared carriers, and the component interpretations form a model of \(\Gamma_1\land\Gamma_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Component models are compatible when they agree on interface equalities and can use equally sized shared-sort domains; then their disjoint interpretations can be combined.
assumptions_latex: The component signatures are disjoint apart from shared sorts and equality.
Each \(M_i\) satisfies its component constraints \(\Gamma_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatible component models yield a model of \(\Gamma_1\land\Gamma_2\).

notation.meaning: model of component theory and constraints

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard interface-model compatibility criterion for disjoint-signature combinations
A source is needed for the intended cardinality hypotheses.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The compatibility criterion fits the leaf, but its amalgamation conclusion depends on precise shared-sort, cardinality, and signature hypotheses for which no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Delayed Theory Combination
children.top_down_role: SAT-mediated alternatives to direct equality exchange.

knowledge_statements.title: Interface-Equality Abstraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propositional representation of equality arrangements over purified shared constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite set \(V\) of shared constants, introduce a Boolean atom \(e_{xy}\) for every unordered pair \(\{x,y\}\subseteq V\) of the same sort. An interface arrangement \(E\) is represented by the Boolean assignment satisfying \[e_{xy}=\mathsf{true}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\mathrel{E}y,\] where \(E\) is an equivalence relation separately on each sort. Reflexivity is implicit, symmetry follows from using unordered pairs, and transitivity is enforced by clauses \(
eg e_{xy}\lor
eg e_{yz}\lor e_{xz}\). Thus each admissible assignment denotes exactly one conjunction containing either \(x=y\) or \(x
e y\) for every same-sort pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Same-sort interface equalities become Boolean atoms constrained to encode an equivalence relation, giving a complete equality-or-disequality arrangement.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite and many-sorted.
Only constants of the same sort may be equated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Admissible Boolean assignments correspond bijectively to complete sorted equality arrangements on \(V\).

notation.meaning: Boolean abstraction of the equality between two interface constants
sorted equivalence relation on the interface

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard Boolean encoding of equality arrangements in delayed theory combination
No relevant source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Boolean equivalence-relation representation is mathematically coherent and matches the container, but no source with a specific locator supports its use as the delayed-combination interface abstraction.

knowledge_statements.title: SAT-Mediated Equality Exchange
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lazy exchange of interface equalities through a shared SAT assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given purified component literal sets \(\Gamma_1,\ldots,\Gamma_m\) and interface-equality atoms, a SAT solver selects a total Boolean assignment \(\alpha\). For each component, invoke its theory solver on the literals selected by \(\alpha\), including the selected interface equalities and disequalities. If component \(i\) returns a conflict set \(C_i\), add the clause \(\bigvee_{\ell\in C_i}\neg\ell\) and resume SAT search. If it derives an unassigned interface equality \(x=y\), propagate its atom to the SAT solver. Stop with \(\mathsf{sat}\) when every component accepts one common complete arrangement; stop with \(\mathsf{unsat}\) when the Boolean clause set is inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SAT proposes interface arrangements; theory solvers reject them with clauses or propagate equalities until a jointly accepted arrangement is found or exhausted.
assumptions_latex: Each component theory solver is sound and terminating on finite ground literal sets.
The interface-equality abstraction contains every relevant same-sort pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns \(\mathsf{sat}\) exactly upon finding an arrangement accepted by all components, subject to combination completeness.

notation.meaning: purified literals for component theory i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard DPLL(T)-style delayed combination loop
Completeness depends on combination hypotheses requiring a relevant source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches SAT-mediated equality exchange, but its correctness and stopping claims are conditional on an unspecified combination-completeness theorem. A relevant source must state the required theory hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.title: Delayed-Combination Search Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent search schedules for finite interface-arrangement exploration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(V)\) be the finite set of complete sorted equality arrangements over interface constants \(V\). Delayed combination may enumerate \(A(V)\) eagerly, test arrangements lazily under successive SAT assignments, or generate equality atoms and transitivity clauses on demand. If every rejected arrangement produces a sound blocking clause, every accepted arrangement is checked by all component solvers, and the schedule is fair—so no unblocked arrangement is postponed forever—then all three regimes decide the same disjunction \[\bigvee_{E\in A(V)}\ \bigwedge_i \mathsf{Sat}_{T_i}(\Gamma_i\land E).\] They differ in enumeration order and retained clauses, not in the represented combination problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eager, lazy, and on-demand searches are equivalent when conflicts are sound, candidates are jointly checked, and fair search eventually considers every surviving arrangement.
assumptions_latex: The interface set \(V\) is finite.
Component satisfiability checks terminate.
The search schedule is fair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each regime decides whether some \(E\in A(V)\) is satisfiable in every component.

notation.meaning: finite set of complete interface arrangements

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite fair-search equivalence for delayed combination regimes
No relevant source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the search-regimes leaf, but equivalence of eager, lazy, and on-demand generation requires a sourced formal account of completeness, fairness, and clause generation.

knowledge_statements.title: Shostak-Style Combination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonizer-and-solver combination for disjoint equational component theories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each component theory \(T_i\), assume a canonizer \(\mathsf{can}_i\) and an equation solver \(\mathsf{solve}_i(s=t)\) returning either inconsistency or an equivalent finite substitution. Purify mixed terms by fresh variables. Repeatedly select an unsolved equation in its owning theory, apply \(\mathsf{solve}_i\), propagate the resulting substitution to every component, and canonize all affected terms with their owning canonizers. Stop with \(\mathsf{unsat}\) upon an inconsistent solved form; otherwise stop when substitutions and canonical forms reach a fixed point. The fixed-point substitution is a solved representation of the original conjunction of equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Component canonizers and equation solvers alternately normalize, solve, and propagate substitutions until contradiction or a common solved form is reached.
assumptions_latex: Component signatures are pairwise disjoint and share equality.
Each canonizer is terminating, sound, and complete for ground equality in its theory.
Each solver returns an equivalent solved substitution and propagation terminates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns inconsistency or a fixed-point solved form equivalent modulo \(\bigcup_i T_i\).

notation.meaning: canonical-form operator for component theory i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: abstract canonizer-and-solver presentation of Shostak combination
Exact completeness conditions vary across Shostak frameworks and need a source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the leaf, but Shostak-style combination has framework-specific requirements on canonizers, solvers, substitutions, variable ordering, and termination. The stated assumptions and equivalence conclusion cannot be certified without a specialized source.

children.title: Polite Theory Combination
children.top_down_role: Combination regimes based on politeness conditions for selected sorts.

knowledge_statements.title: Polite Theory Combination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Politeness relative to a designated set of shared sorts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a theory \(T\) and designated shared sorts \(S\). The theory is polite with respect to \(S\) when it is both smooth and finitely witnessable. Smoothness means that any model of a quantifier-free formula can be replaced by another satisfying model whose carrier on each \(\sigma\in S\) has any prescribed cardinality at least as large as the original carrier. Finite witnessability means that a computable transformation \(\mathsf{wit}\) satisfies \[T\models\varphi\leftrightarrow\exists\bar w\,\mathsf{wit}(\varphi),\] and every satisfiable \(\mathsf{wit}(\varphi)\) has a model whose \(S\)-sorted carriers consist exactly of values assigned to its variables of those sorts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A theory is polite on shared sorts when models can be enlarged there and satisfiable formulas admit computable finite witnesses covering those domains.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a many-sorted first-order theory.
\(S\) is the designated set of shared sorts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) is polite with respect to \(S\) exactly when smoothness and finite witnessability both hold.

notation.meaning: fresh witness variables introduced by the transformation

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional smoothness-plus-finite-witnessability definition of polite theories
A theory-combination source is required to certify the exact witness convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition has the expected smoothness and finite-witnessability components, but the exact cardinality and witness-domain conventions vary in the literature and require a specific cited definition.

children.title: Strongly Polite Theory Combination
children.top_down_role: Combination regimes using strengthened politeness conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Polite Theory Combination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong politeness requires witnessability to persist under interface arrangements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A theory \(T\) is strongly polite with respect to shared sorts \(S\) if it is smooth on \(S\) and has a witness transformation \(\mathsf{wit}\) with the following arrangement-stability property. For every quantifier-free \(\varphi\) and every sorted equality arrangement \(E\) on the \(S\)-sorted variables of \(\mathsf{wit}(\varphi)\), \[T\models (\varphi\land E)\leftrightarrow\exists\bar w\,(\mathsf{wit}(\varphi)\land E),\] and whenever the right-hand matrix is satisfiable, it has a model whose carrier of each \(\sigma\in S\) consists exactly of the values of its \(\sigma\)-sorted variables. Thus finite witnessing remains valid after arbitrary interface identifications and separations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong politeness adds that finite witnesses remain valid after every equality-and-disequality arrangement imposed on shared-sort variables.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a many-sorted first-order theory.
\(S\) is the designated set of shared sorts.
Arrangements equate only variables of the same sort.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The witness property holds uniformly for every interface arrangement \(E\).

notation.meaning: sorted equality arrangement on shared-sort variables

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: strong finite witnessability is ordinary witnessability stable under arrangements
Terminology and exact quantified variables require confirmation from a specialized source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits the strong-politeness leaf, but the precise placement and scope of arrangements and witness quantifiers are specialized and cannot be validated from standard-field rationale alone.

children.title: Politeness-Strength Gap
children.top_down_role: Differences in admissible component theories and combination guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Politeness-Strength Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between ordinary and arrangement-stable finite witnessability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Ordinary politeness does not by definition guarantee strong politeness. The gap occurs when a witness transformation \(\mathsf{wit}\) provides a finite-domain model for every satisfiable \(\mathsf{wit}(\varphi)\), but there exist a satisfiable formula \(\varphi\) and an arrangement \(E\) such that \(\mathsf{wit}(\varphi)\land E\) is satisfiable while no satisfying model has each shared-sort carrier equal to the values of its variables. Hence the implication \[\text{strongly polite}\Longrightarrow\text{polite}\] follows by taking the unrestricted arrangement, whereas the converse requires arrangement-stable finite witnessing and cannot be inferred from smoothness plus ordinary finite witnessability alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong politeness implies politeness, but the converse fails whenever finite witnesses cease to cover shared domains after an imposed interface arrangement.
assumptions_latex: Politeness uses ordinary finite witnessability.
Strong politeness requires finite witnessability under every sorted arrangement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong politeness implies politeness; the reverse implication requires an additional arrangement-stability property.

notation.meaning: interface equality arrangement exposing the gap

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: definitional implication and operational characterization of the strength gap
A sourced concrete separating theory is needed to assert strictness existentially.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The implication from strong politeness to politeness is definitional, but the plain statement says the converse fails, which asserts a genuine separation. A sourced separating theory or theorem is required; the LaTeX statement otherwise only says the converse cannot be inferred without arrangement stability.

children.title: Many-Sorted Theory Combination
children.top_down_role: Combination frameworks respecting multiple sorts plus sort-specific sharing.

knowledge_statements.title: Many-Sorted Theory Combination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-amalgamation form of disjoint many-sorted combination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) be many-sorted theories whose nonlogical signatures are disjoint, although designated sorts and equality may be shared. After purification, write a ground conjunction as \(\Gamma_1\land\Gamma_2\), and let \(V_\sigma\) contain its shared constants of sort \(\sigma\). If there is a sorted arrangement \(E\) such that each \(T_i\cup\{\Gamma_i,E\}\) has a model and the two models can be selected with equal carrier cardinalities on every shared sort, then \(\Gamma_1\land\Gamma_2\) is satisfiable in \(T_1\cup T_2\). Conversely, every combined model induces such an arrangement and compatible component reducts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A purified many-sorted combination is satisfiable exactly when component models share a sorted equality arrangement and compatible cardinalities on every shared sort.
assumptions_latex: Nonlogical component signatures are disjoint.
Shared symbols are restricted to sorts and equality.
Compatible component models exist for one complete sorted arrangement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_1\cup T_2\cup\{\Gamma_1\land\Gamma_2\}\) is satisfiable exactly when compatible arranged component models exist.

notation.meaning: complete equality arrangement sorted by shared sort

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard reduct-and-amalgamation criterion for disjoint many-sorted theories
A source is needed for precise cardinality and signature hypotheses.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem matches the many-sorted combination leaf, but its biconditional depends on exact signature-sharing and carrier-cardinality hypotheses. No inspectable theorem or section supports those hypotheses.

children.title: Finite-Model Theory Combination
children.top_down_role: Combination frameworks for components with finite-domain or finite-model constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Model Theory Combination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility criterion when shared-sort carriers must remain finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For purified constraints \(\Gamma_1\) and \(\Gamma_2\), finite-model combination succeeds exactly when there are finite component models \(M_i\models T_i\cup\{\Gamma_i,E\}\) for one complete sorted arrangement \(E\), and \[|M_1(\sigma)|=|M_2(\sigma)|<\infty\] for every shared sort \(\sigma\). Bijections between corresponding shared carriers can then be chosen to respect the values of interface constants, after which the disjoint component interpretations form a finite combined model. Agreement on \(E\) alone is insufficient when the component theories force incompatible finite cardinalities on a shared sort.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite component models combine when they agree on interface equalities and have identical finite cardinalities for every shared sort.
assumptions_latex: Component signatures are disjoint apart from shared sorts and equality.
All selected shared-sort carriers are finite.
Both components realize the same complete sorted arrangement \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite combined model exists exactly when finite arranged component models have matching shared-sort cardinalities.

notation.meaning: carrier of shared sort sigma in component model i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite carrier matching is the model-amalgamation criterion for shared sorts
No supplied source addresses finite-model theory combination.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is plausible and fits the finite-model combination leaf, but the exact necessity and sufficiency of matching finite shared-sort cardinalities requires a source specifying the permitted shared signature and amalgamation construction.

children.title: Shared-Sort Cardinality Constraints
children.top_down_role: Cardinality compatibility across shared sorts in combined models.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Sort Cardinality Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite certificate for cardinality compatibility on shared sorts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each shared sort \(\sigma\), a cardinality certificate consists of an integer \(k_\sigma\ge 1\), constants \(a_{\sigma,1},\ldots,a_{\sigma,k_\sigma}\), pairwise disequalities \(a_{\sigma,p}\ne a_{\sigma,q}\) for \(p\ne q\), and the coverage constraint \[\forall x{:}\sigma\;\bigvee_{j=1}^{k_\sigma}x=a_{\sigma,j}.\] Any model of these constraints has exactly \(k_\sigma\) elements of sort \(\sigma\). If each component theory solver accepts its purified constraints together with the same certificates and interface arrangement, the resulting component models have matching shared-sort cardinalities and are eligible for finite-model amalgamation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Named distinct representatives give a lower bound, and a universal coverage constraint gives the matching upper bound, certifying an exact shared-sort size.
assumptions_latex: Each \(k_\sigma\) is a positive integer.
The same certificate is imposed on every component sharing \(\sigma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed constraints certify \(|M(\sigma)|=k_\sigma\) in every accepting component model.

notation.meaning: certified cardinality of shared sort sigma
named representatives of the shared-sort elements

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact finite cardinality is certified by distinct representatives plus domain coverage
A relevant sorted-combination source was not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed distinctness and coverage constraints correctly force an exact positive finite sort size and the certificate kind fits the leaf. A relevant source is still required to support this quantified certificate within the intended sorted theory-combination framework.

children.title: Finite-Model Compatibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions limiting combined finite-model construction.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Model Compatibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary finite-cardinality compatibility condition for a shared sort.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i\in\{1,2\}\), define \(\operatorname{Spec}_s(T_i,G_i)=\{n\in\mathbb N_{>0}:\text{some }\mathcal M_i\models T_i\cup G_i\text{ has }|s^{\mathcal M_i}|=n\}\). If \(T_1\cup T_2\cup G_1\cup G_2\) has a model \(\mathcal M\) with \(|s^{\mathcal M}|<\infty\), then \(|s^{\mathcal M}|\in\operatorname{Spec}_s(T_1,G_1)\cap\operatorname{Spec}_s(T_2,G_2)\). Consequently, disjoint finite-cardinality spectra preclude a combined model whose shared sort \(s\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A combined model with a finite shared sort can exist only if both components can realize the same finite cardinality for that sort.
assumptions_latex: \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) share a sort \(s\).
\(G_i\) is a finite ground constraint over the signature of \(T_i\).
The combined model under consideration has \(|s^{\mathcal M}|<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Spec}_s(T_1,G_1)\cap\operatorname{Spec}_s(T_2,G_2)\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Positive finite cardinalities realizable by the shared sort in models of the indicated theory and constraint

children.title: Non-Disjoint Theory Combination
children.top_down_role: Combination frameworks permitting shared nonlogical symbols across component theories.

assumptions_latex: \(T_i\) is a theory over \(\Sigma_i\) for \(i\in\{1,2\}\).
\(\Sigma_0=\Sigma_1\cap\Sigma_2\) may contain nonlogical symbols.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A model of the non-disjoint combination is exactly a \(\Sigma_1\cup\Sigma_2\)-structure satisfying \(T_1\cup T_2\), with one common interpretation of every symbol in \(\Sigma_0\).

notation.meaning: Signature shared by the component theories
Reduct of a structure to a subsignature

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic definition allowing shared function, predicate, and sort symbols.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The non-disjoint combination of \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) is the theory \(T_1\cup T_2\) over \(\Sigma_1\cup\Sigma_2\) when \(\Sigma_0=\Sigma_1\cap\Sigma_2\) is not restricted to equality and shared sorts. A structure \(\mathcal M\) is a combined model precisely when \(\mathcal M\upharpoonright_{\Sigma_i}\models T_i\) for both \(i\), so the two reducts induce identical carriers and interpretations on every sort, function, and predicate belonging to \(\Sigma_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Non-disjoint combination forms the union of two theories while requiring their models to agree on every shared symbol.
knowledge_statements.title: Non-Disjoint Theory Combination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The semantic definition is plausible and fits the definition container, but it has no citation or inspectable locator establishing the intended non-disjoint-combination framework.

children.title: Theory-Extension Combination
children.top_down_role: Combination of a base theory with constrained extension symbols or axioms.

assumptions_latex: \(T_0\subseteq T_1=T_0\cup K\), where \(K\) contains extension symbols absent from \(T_0\).
The extension is local for finite ground satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every finite ground \(G\), deciding \(T_1\cup G\) reduces to deciding \(T_0\cup K[G]\cup G\) after purification and congruence constraints.

notation.meaning: Instances of extension axioms whose extension terms occur in the ground problem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ground satisfiability reduction for a local first-order theory extension.
