knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Numeric OMT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single numeric objective optimized over models satisfying hard theory constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scalar numeric OMT instance over theory \(T\) is a pair \((\varphi,f)\), where \(\varphi\) is a formula over the signature of \(T\) and \(f\) is a numeric term interpreted in a totally ordered domain \(D\). For minimization, its value is \(v^*=\inf\{f^{\mathcal M}:\mathcal M\models T\cup\{\varphi\}\}\). A model \(\mathcal M^*\) is optimal when \(\mathcal M^*\models T\cup\{\varphi\}\) and \(f^{\mathcal M^*}=v^*\); if the infimum is unattained, the instance has an infimum but no optimal model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scalar numeric OMT minimizes one ordered numeric term over all models satisfying the hard theory constraints, with the optimum possibly unattained.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is totally ordered and admits the relevant infimum in an order completion.
The feasible-model class is nonempty when an optimal value is requested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^*=\inf_{\mathcal M\models T\cup\{\varphi\}}f^{\mathcal M}\), with optimality requiring attainment.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The single-objective infimum semantics, including possible nonattainment, are precise and definition is the correct content kind. No inspectable OMT source is supplied.

children.title: Soft-Constraint OMT
children.top_down_role: OMT problem families containing relaxable constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Soft-Constraint OMT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted cardinality optimization of violated soft constraints under mandatory hard constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An unweighted soft-constraint OMT instance over theory \(T\) consists of a hard formula \(H\) and a finite family of soft formulas \(S=(s_1,\ldots,s_m)\). For every model \(\mathcal M\models T\cup\{H\}\), define its violation cost by \(c(\mathcal M)=|\{i:\mathcal M\not\models s_i\}|\). An optimal model \(\mathcal M^*\) satisfies the hard formula and minimizes \(c\); equivalently, it maximizes the number of satisfied soft formulas. Repeated soft formulas count with their multiplicities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Soft-constraint OMT keeps hard constraints mandatory and finds a model violating the fewest unweighted soft constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and each \(s_i\) is interpreted in theory \(T\).
At least one model satisfies \(T\cup\{H\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathcal M\models T\cup\{H\}}|\{i:\mathcal M\not\models s_i\}|\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record correctly defines the unweighted cardinality version of soft-constraint OMT, handles multiplicities, and fits the definition container. An authoritative MaxSMT or OMT source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Weighted OMT
children.top_down_role: OMT problem families assigning quantitative importance to optimization elements.

assumptions_latex: The background theory \(T\) fixes the meaning of all hard and soft formulas.
Every soft formula has a nonnegative weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal model minimizes the total weight of violated soft formulas while satisfying all hard formulas.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty-minimizing OMT over weighted soft formulas and hard theory constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a finite set of hard formulas and \(S=\{(C_i,w_i)\}_{i=1}^m\) a finite family with \(w_i\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\). A weighted OMT solution is a \(T\)-model \(M^*\models H\) such that, with \(P(M)=\sum_{i:M\not\models C_i}w_i\), one has \[P(M^*)=\min\{P(M):M\models_T H\}.\] Equivalently, \(M^*\) maximizes \(\sum_{i:M\models C_i}w_i\) among the \(T\)-models of \(H\). If no \(T\)-model satisfies \(H\), the instance is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted OMT satisfies every hard constraint and minimizes the total weight of violated soft constraints, equivalently maximizing satisfied soft weight.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted OMT

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent, but no citation establishes that this weighted-soft-constraint formulation is properly classified as Weighted OMT rather than Weighted MaxSMT or an OMT encoding thereof.

children.title: Weighted Soft-Constraint Semantics
children.top_down_role: Interpretation of weights attached to relaxable constraints.

assumptions_latex: The hard formulas and soft formulas are interpreted in a fixed theory \(T\).
Soft weights are nonnegative real numbers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Model preference is determined by the weighted sum of violated soft formulas.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive violation-cost semantics for weighted soft constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For weighted soft formulas \(S=\{(C_i,w_i)\}_{i=1}^m\), define the violation cost of each \(T\)-model \(M\models H\) by \[c_S(M)=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\,\mathbf{1}[M\not\models C_i].\] For feasible models \(M,N\), the weighted soft-constraint preference is \(M\prec_S N\) exactly when \(c_S(M)<c_S(N)\), and they are indifferent exactly when \(c_S(M)=c_S(N)\). Thus weights trade violations additively; they do not alter whether a model satisfies the hard formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each feasible model is charged the sum of weights of its violated soft constraints; smaller total charge is preferred.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Soft-Constraint Semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive violation-cost semantics is precise and fits the container, but the record has no inspectable MaxSMT or OMT source supporting this semantic convention.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(F\) is nonempty.
All objective values lie in linearly ordered sets and every required stage minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A lexicographic OMT solution is a feasible model having a lexicographically minimal objective vector.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization with fixed objective priority from \(f_1\) through \(f_k\).

source_refs.locator: 3.2.2 Multiple and conflicting objectives p. 26

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the set of models satisfying the hard \(T\)-constraints, and let \(f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)\) list minimization objectives in decreasing priority. A model \(M^*\in F\) is lexicographically optimal when \[f(M^*)\le_{\mathrm{lex}} f(M)\quad\text{for every }M\in F,\] where \(a<_{\mathrm{lex}}b\) holds exactly when, at the least index \(j\) with \(a_j\ne b_j\), one has \(a_j<b_j\). Lower-priority objectives may distinguish only models tied on all higher-priority objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lexicographic OMT minimizes the first objective, then the second among first-objective optima, continuing in the declared priority order.
knowledge_statements.title: Lexicographic OMT

source_witnesses.locator: 3.2.2 Multiple and conflicting objectives p. 26

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(F\) is nonempty.
All objectives are minimized and take values in ordered sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A Pareto-optimal model is feasible and is not dominated by any other feasible model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nondominated-model semantics for multiple minimization objectives.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.2 Multiple and conflicting objectives p. 26

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M,N\in F\), define \(N\prec_P M\) when \(f_i(N)\le f_i(M)\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and \(f_j(N)<f_j(M)\) for at least one \(j\). A feasible model \(M^*\in F\) is Pareto optimal if no \(N\in F\) satisfies \(N\prec_P M^*\). Its vector \(f(M^*)\) is a Pareto point; the Pareto front is the set of all such attainable nondominated vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pareto OMT returns feasible models whose objective vectors cannot be improved in one component without worsening at least one other component.
knowledge_statements.title: Pareto OMT

source_witnesses.locator: 3.2.2 Multiple and conflicting objectives p. 26

children.title: Independent Objectives
children.top_down_role: Multiple-objective regimes treating each objective as a separate optimization query.

assumptions_latex: The feasible theory-model set \(F\) is nonempty.
Each scalar minimization problem attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Independent optimization returns the componentwise ideal values, possibly witnessed by different feasible models.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise optimization without imposing another objective's optimum as a constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Objectives \(f_1,\ldots,f_k\) are optimized independently over the common feasible set \(F\) when the reported value for component \(i\) is \[v_i^*=\min_{M\in F}f_i(M),\] computed without constraining any \(f_j\), \(j\ne i\), to its optimum. A witness \(M_i\in F\) may be returned separately for each component. The ideal vector \(v^*=(v_1^*,\ldots,v_k^*)\) need not equal \(f(M)\) for any single \(M\in F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each objective is minimized over the original feasible set, so different objectives may have different witness models and the combined ideal vector may be unattainable.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Objectives

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise ideal-vector formulation is coherent, but the exact meaning of independent objectives in this solver-oriented taxonomy requires an authoritative source distinguishing it from boxed objective semantics.

children.title: Boxed Objectives
children.top_down_role: Multiple-objective regimes evaluating objectives within boxed optimization contexts.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(F\) is nonempty.
Each scalar objective minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Boxed optimization reports one independently optimal model-value pair per objective.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-style box priority interpreted as separate scalar optimizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under boxed objective semantics, each objective \(f_i\) defines its own optimization box with the original hard feasible set \(F\). The result is a family \(\{(M_i^*,v_i^*)\}_{i=1}^k\) satisfying \[M_i^*\in F,\qquad v_i^*=f_i(M_i^*)=\min_{M\in F}f_i(M).\] No equality \(M_i^*=M_j^*\) is required for \(i\ne j\), and an optimum obtained in one box is not added as a hard restriction in another box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boxed objectives are solved in separate optimization contexts sharing only the original hard constraints; each objective may therefore return a different model.
knowledge_statements.title: Boxed Objectives

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Box priority is solver-specific terminology. A solver manual or OMT reference is required to substantiate the asserted separate-context semantics and the form of the reported model-value family.

children.title: Cross-Objective Coupling Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which objective independence ceases to preserve intended results.

assumptions_latex: Both objectives are minimized over a common feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Separate scalar optima characterize a joint model only when their optimal solution sets have nonempty intersection.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between independent objective values and jointly attainable multiobjective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A_i=\operatorname*{argmin}_{M\in F}f_i(M)\), the independently optimal values are jointly attainable exactly when \(\bigcap_{i=1}^k A_i\ne\varnothing\). Without this intersection condition, combining componentwise optima is invalid. Concretely, let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb{Z}:0\le x\le1\}\), \(f_1(x)=x\), and \(f_2(x)=1-x\). Then the separate minima are both \(0\), attained at \(x=0\) and \(x=1\), respectively, but no feasible \(x\) realizes the ideal vector \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent optima can be combined only when one feasible model attains all of them; conflicting objectives provide a two-point counterexample.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Objective Coupling Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The intersection criterion and counterexample are mathematically sound, but no source is cited. The assumptions also refer to two objectives while the general statement quantifies over k objectives.

children.title: Feasibility Semantics
children.top_down_role: The role of theory-satisfying assignments within OMT problem interpretation.

assumptions_latex: A fixed background theory \(T\) supplies the model relation.
The hard constraint set \(H\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility means existence of a \(T\)-model satisfying every hard constraint, independently of objective quality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard-constraint feasibility underlying every OMT objective regime.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.6 Hard and soft constraints p. 31

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For hard formulas \(H\), define the feasible-model set by \[F_H=\{M:M\models_T C\text{ for every }C\in H\}.\] The associated OMT instance is feasible exactly when \(F_H\ne\varnothing\), and infeasible exactly when \(F_H=\varnothing\). Objective terms, soft formulas, weights, and priority rules compare members of \(F_H\); they do not make a model violating a hard formula feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An OMT instance is feasible exactly when the background theory has a model satisfying every hard constraint; objectives only rank such models.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Semantics

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.6 Hard and soft constraints p. 31

children.title: Objective Comparison Semantics
children.top_down_role: Ordering regimes used to compare feasible objective outcomes.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(F\) is fixed.
The objective domain is equipped with a specified preorder.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: OMT optimality is minimality under the declared preorder restricted to attainable objective values.

notation.meaning: objective preorder and its strict part

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-theoretic semantics encompassing scalar, weighted, lexicographic, and Pareto comparisons.

source_refs.locator: 3.2 Defining objectives p. 23

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:F\to V\) assign each feasible model its objective value, and let \(\preceq\) be the declared preference preorder on \(V\), with strict part \(u\prec v\) meaning \(u\preceq v\) and not \(v\preceq u\). A model \(M^*\in F\) is objective-optimal when there is no \(M\in F\) such that \(g(M)\prec g(M^*)\). If \(\preceq\) is total, this selects globally least attainable values; if partial, several incomparable minimal values may remain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective semantics consists of a value map and preference order; optimal models are those with no strictly preferred feasible competitor.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Comparison Semantics

source_witnesses.locator: 3.2 Defining objectives p. 23

children.title: MaxSMT Problem Families
children.top_down_role: MaxSMT formulations are separated from their solving architectures.

assumptions_latex: Hard and soft formulas are interpreted in a fixed theory \(T\).
The hard formulas are jointly \(T\)-satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Partial MaxSMT maximizes the number of satisfied soft formulas subject to satisfaction of every hard formula.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted partial MaxSMT with mandatory hard formulas and optional soft formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partial MaxSMT instance is a pair \((H,S)\) of finite formula sets. Every admissible solution is a \(T\)-model \(M\models H\); soft formulas may be violated. Defining \(u(M)=|\{C\in S:M\not\models C\}|\), an optimal solution \(M^*\) satisfies \[u(M^*)=\min\{u(M):M\models_T H\}.\] Equivalently, \(M^*\) maximizes \(|\{C\in S:M\models C\}|\). If \(H\) has no \(T\)-model, the instance is infeasible rather than merely suboptimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial MaxSMT requires all hard formulas and maximizes how many unweighted soft formulas are satisfied.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial MaxSMT

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unweighted partial-MaxSMT formulation is precise and standard, but the record contains no inspectable source supporting the terminology and hard/soft semantics.

assumptions_latex: Hard and soft formulas are interpreted in a fixed theory \(T\).
Every soft formula has a nonnegative weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weighted MaxSMT minimizes violated soft weight while enforcing all hard formulas.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial MaxSMT generalized by additive nonnegative soft-formula weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A weighted MaxSMT instance consists of hard formulas \(H\) and weighted soft formulas \(S=\{(C_i,w_i)\}_{i=1}^m\), where \(w_i\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\). For each \(T\)-model \(M\models H\), let \(c(M)=\sum_{i:M\not\models C_i}w_i\). A model \(M^*\) is optimal exactly when \[c(M^*)=\min\{c(M):M\models_T H\}.\] Setting every weight to \(1\) recovers unweighted partial MaxSMT, up to ties among equal-cardinality violation sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted MaxSMT satisfies all hard formulas and minimizes the sum of weights assigned to violated soft formulas.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted MaxSMT

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The optimization formula is coherent, but an authoritative source is needed both for Weighted MaxSMT semantics and for the claimed allowance of arbitrary nonnegative real weights, since standard formulations often use positive integer weights.

children.title: Lexicographic MaxSMT
children.top_down_role: MaxSMT regimes ordered by strict objective priority.

assumptions_latex: Soft formulas are partitioned into finitely many priority tiers.
Within each tier, violations have nonnegative weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Lexicographic MaxSMT minimizes the tier-cost vector in decreasing priority order subject to all hard formulas.

notation.meaning: weighted soft formulas in priority tier \(r\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Priority-tier MaxSMT using lexicographic comparison of weighted violation costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be the hard formulas and \(S_1,\ldots,S_p\) the weighted soft tiers in decreasing priority. For \(M\models_T H\), define \(c_r(M)=\sum_{(C,w)\in S_r,\,M\not\models C}w\) and \(c(M)=(c_1(M),\ldots,c_p(M))\). A lexicographic MaxSMT solution is a model \(M^*\models_T H\) satisfying \[c(M^*)\le_{\mathrm{lex}}c(M)\quad\text{for every }M\models_T H.\] Consequently, no improvement in a lower-priority tier can compensate for a strictly worse cost in the first higher-priority tier where two models differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lexicographic MaxSMT first minimizes violation cost in the highest tier, then optimizes each lower tier while preserving all higher-tier optima.
knowledge_statements.title: Lexicographic MaxSMT

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lexicographic tier-cost formulation fits the container, but no source supports this stratified MaxSMT convention. The record should also establish finite tier sums and address feasibility or attainment before promotion.

children.title: Stratified MaxSMT
children.top_down_role: MaxSMT regimes partitioned into weight or priority strata.

knowledge_statements.title: Stratified MaxSMT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential priority-stratum semantics for weighted partial SMT instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a finite set of hard SMT formulas and let \(S_1,\ldots,S_p\) be ordered strata of soft formulas, with stratum \(1\) having highest priority. Each \(\varphi\in S_k\) has weight \(w_\varphi>0\). For every theory model \(M\models H\), define \(c_k(M)=\sum_{\varphi\in S_k,\,M\not\models\varphi}w_\varphi\). A stratified MaxSMT solution is a model \(M^*\models H\) whose cost vector \((c_1(M^*),\ldots,c_p(M^*))\) is lexicographically minimal among all models of \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stratified MaxSMT lexicographically minimizes violated soft-formula weight, processing ordered priority strata from highest to lowest while always satisfying the hard formulas.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) has at least one theory model.
The soft-formula family is finite and every weight is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((c_1(M^*),\ldots,c_p(M^*))=\min_{\mathrm{lex}}\{(c_1(M),\ldots,c_p(M)):M\models H\}\).

notation.meaning: finite set of hard SMT formulas
soft formulas in priority stratum k
violated weight in stratum k under model M

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no inspectable source or locator supports the stated stratified MaxSMT semantics.

children.title: Priority-Tier Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationships between lexicographic priorities and stratified weight tiers.

knowledge_statements.title: Priority-Tier Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between lexicographic tiers and sufficiently separated scalar weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c_k(M)\in[0,C_k]\) be integer-valued violation costs for tiers \(k=1,\ldots,p\), ordered from highest to lowest priority. Choose positive multipliers \(\lambda_k\) satisfying \(\lambda_k>\sum_{j=k+1}^{p}\lambda_j C_j\) for every \(k<p\). Then models minimizing the scalar objective \(\sum_{k=1}^{p}\lambda_k c_k(M)\) are exactly the models whose vector \((c_1(M),\ldots,c_p(M))\) is lexicographically minimal. Thus finite priority tiers admit a dominance-weight scalarization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lexicographic priority tiers equal one weighted objective when every tier’s multiplier dominates the largest possible contribution of all lower tiers.
assumptions_latex: Every tier cost is integer-valued and has a finite upper bound \(C_k\).
The feasible model set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{M}\sum_{k=1}^{p}\lambda_kc_k(M)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{M}^{\mathrm{lex}}(c_1(M),\ldots,c_p(M)).\]

notation.meaning: violation cost of priority tier k
finite upper bound on tier-k cost

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The integer-cost dominance condition appears sufficient for the claimed correspondence, but the exact equivalence and multiplier condition require a relevant cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: MaxSMT Representations
children.top_down_role: Native representations of hard constraints, soft constraints, and optimization costs.

knowledge_statements.title: MaxSMT Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical violated-soft-weight representation of weighted partial MaxSMT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A weighted partial MaxSMT instance is represented by a finite hard set \(H\) and a finite indexed family \(S=\{(\varphi_i,w_i)\}_{i=1}^{m}\) of soft theory formulas with \(w_i>0\). Its feasible objects are theory models \(M\models H\), and its objective is \(C(M)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i\mathbf 1[M\not\models\varphi_i]\). Equivalently, one may maximize \(\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i\mathbf 1[M\models\varphi_i]\), because the two objectives sum to the constant \(\sum_iw_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted partial MaxSMT represents feasibility by hard formulas and optimization by the total weight of violated soft formulas, equivalently the satisfied soft weight.
assumptions_latex: The hard and soft families are finite.
All soft weights are positive real or rational numbers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{M\models H}C(M)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{M\models H}\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i\mathbf 1[M\models\varphi_i].\]

notation.meaning: soft formula and its penalty weight

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and equivalence of violated and satisfied soft weight are precise and locally appropriate, but no supporting MaxSMT source is cited.

children.title: Pseudo-Boolean Representations
children.top_down_role: Representations based on Boolean variables with integer-valued constraints or objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Pseudo-Boolean Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-one linear representation of Boolean feasibility and cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pseudo-Boolean optimization representation consists of variables \(x\in\{0,1\}^{n}\), integer linear constraints \(Ax\ge b\), and an integer linear objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x+c_0\) to be minimized. A Boolean literal is represented by \(x_j\) or \(1-x_j\). In particular, a clause \(\ell_1\vee\cdots\vee\ell_q\) is represented by \(v(\ell_1)+\cdots+v(\ell_q)\ge1\), where \(v(x_j)=x_j\) and \(v(\neg x_j)=1-x_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pseudo-Boolean optimization uses binary variables, integer linear constraints, and a linear objective; clauses become inequalities requiring at least one literal value to equal one.
assumptions_latex: All variables have domain \(\{0,1\}\).
Constraint and objective coefficients are integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x+c_0:Ax\ge b,\ x\in\{0,1\}^{n}\}.\]

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical description is standard, but it lacks a source. The leaf title suggests content_kind representation may fit more exactly than definition and should be checked when sourcing the record.

children.title: MaxSMT–Pseudo-Boolean Translations
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondences between MaxSMT instances and pseudo-Boolean forms.

knowledge_statements.title: MaxSMT–Pseudo-Boolean Translations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxation-variable translation for formulas admitting exact pseudo-Boolean encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every hard formula \(h\) and soft formula \(\varphi_i\) has an exact pseudo-Boolean encoding \(E(h)\) and \(E(\varphi_i)\). Introduce a relaxation variable \(r_i\in\{0,1\}\) for each weighted soft formula. Replace hard formulas by \(E(h)\), replace each soft formula by an encoding of \(\varphi_i\vee r_i\), and minimize \(\sum_iw_ir_i\). For every feasible assignment, an optimal extension sets \(r_i=1\) exactly when \(\varphi_i\) is false; hence the translated optimum equals the minimum violated soft weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactly encodable MaxSMT instances become pseudo-Boolean programs by adding one relaxation bit per soft formula and minimizing the weighted sum of those bits.
assumptions_latex: Each formula has a satisfaction-preserving pseudo-Boolean encoding.
Soft weights are nonnegative integers or are scaled to integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\min_{M\models H}\sum_iw_i\mathbf 1[M\not\models\varphi_i]=\min\left\{\sum_iw_ir_i:E(H),\ E(\varphi_i\vee r_i),\ r_i\in\{0,1\}\right\}.\]

notation.meaning: exact pseudo-Boolean encoding of formula psi
relaxation indicator for soft formula i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relaxation-variable construction is plausible under exact satisfaction-preserving encodings, but its encoding scope and optimum-preservation claim require a specific source.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Bound Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone tightening for integer-valued offline OMT objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given constraints \(F\), an integer objective \(f\), a valid lower bound \(L\), and a feasible incumbent of value \(U\), initialize \(b=U-1\). Repeatedly query satisfiability of \(F\land(f\le b)\). If a model \(M\) is returned, store it, set \(U=f(M)\), and set \(b=U-1\). If the query is unsatisfiable, return the stored incumbent as optimal. The procedure may also stop when \(U=L\). Each successful query strictly lowers the integer incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear bound search repeatedly asks for a model strictly better than the incumbent and stops when that tighter bound is infeasible or meets a certified lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The objective is integer-valued and bounded below on models of \(F\).
An initial feasible incumbent and valid lower bound are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M^*\models F\) and \(f(M^*)=\min\{f(M):M\models F\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The integer linear-bound algorithm is internally coherent and fits the leaf, but its correctness claim has no cited OMT source or locator.

children.title: Binary Bound Search
children.top_down_role: Bound-search architectures using interval subdivision.

knowledge_statements.title: Binary Bound Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dichotomic search over a bounded integer objective interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given constraints \(F\), an integer objective \(f\), and certified bounds \(L\le f^*\le U\) with a feasible incumbent of value \(U\), query \(F\land(f\le m)\) at \(m=\lfloor(L+U)/2\rfloor\). If satisfiable with model \(M\), store \(M\) and set \(U=\min\{U,f(M)\}\); otherwise set \(L=m+1\). Repeat until \(L=U\), then return the stored model of value \(U\). At most \(\lceil\log_2(U_0-L_0+1)\rceil\) bound decisions are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary bound search halves a certified integer objective interval after each satisfiable or unsatisfiable threshold query and returns the incumbent when both bounds coincide.
assumptions_latex: The optimum is integer-valued within a finite initial interval \([L_0,U_0]\).
A feasible model of value \(U_0\) is stored.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=U=f^*\), with at most \(\lceil\log_2(U_0-L_0+1)\rceil\) threshold queries.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary threshold-search invariant is coherent, but both the algorithm and its logarithmic query bound require an inspectable source.

children.title: Adaptive Bound Search
children.top_down_role: Bound-search architectures changing query placement from observed solver behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Bound Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant-preserving threshold search with dynamically selected probes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain certified integer bounds \(L\le f^*\le U\) and a feasible incumbent attaining \(U\). At each iteration, a policy selects any threshold \(t\in\{L,\ldots,U-1\}\) from solver history. Query \(F\land(f\le t)\). If satisfiable with model \(M\), replace \(U\) by \(\min\{U,f(M)\}\) and store \(M\); if unsatisfiable, replace \(L\) by \(t+1\). The policy may alternate linear, midpoint, or interpolation probes. Stop at \(L=U\) and return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive bound search chooses each threshold from solver history while preserving lower and upper certificates; any admissible choices terminate on a finite integer interval.
assumptions_latex: The objective is integer-valued in a finite certified interval.
Every bound query is decided correctly by the underlying SMT solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=U=f^*\) after finitely many iterations, and the returned incumbent is optimal.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The invariant-preserving adaptive scheme terminates on a finite integer interval, but the claimed algorithm family and permitted policy variants are unsupported by a source.

children.title: Bound-Search Regime Selection
children.top_down_role: Problem characteristics governing the choice of bound-search architecture.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Search Regime Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-model criterion for choosing linear or binary threshold search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=U_0-L_0\) be the initial integer objective gap. Suppose a linear-search query has estimated cost \(q_{\mathrm{lin}}>0\) and a binary-search query has estimated cost \(q_{\mathrm{bin}}>0\), constant within the run. Under the conservative call bounds \(D\) and \(\lceil\log_2(D+1)\rceil\), select binary search precisely when \(q_{\mathrm{bin}}\lceil\log_2(D+1)\rceil\le q_{\mathrm{lin}}D\); otherwise select linear search. This criterion compares estimated total query cost, not query count alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under constant per-query cost estimates, choose binary search exactly when its logarithmic query-cost bound does not exceed the linear search bound.
assumptions_latex: The objective interval is finite and integer-valued.
Per-query costs are represented by fixed positive estimates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{binary is selected}\iff q_{\mathrm{bin}}\lceil\log_2(D+1)\rceil\le q_{\mathrm{lin}}D.\]

notation.meaning: estimated cost of one linear-search query
estimated cost of one binary-search query

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selection inequality follows from the stipulated constant-cost model, but that model and the asserted regime-selection rule need a source establishing their relevance to OMT bound search.

knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Bound Querying
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound testing with a persistent incremental SMT solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an incremental SMT solver with permanent constraints \(F\). For thresholds \(t_0,t_1,\ldots\), submit each temporary bound \(f\le t_k\) by an assumption literal or by pushing a solver frame, call the satisfiability procedure, record the returned model or unsatisfiability result, and then retract only that temporary bound. Retain sound learned clauses valid independently of the retracted assumption. Update the objective bounds from each result and terminate when the maintained lower and upper bounds coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incremental querying keeps the base SMT problem and reusable learned information while asserting and retracting successive objective bounds.
assumptions_latex: The solver supports assumptions or push-pop frames.
Retained learned clauses remain logical consequences of the permanent constraints and active assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is asserted once, while every query decides \(F\land(f\le t_k)\) without rebuilding the base solver state.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits incremental bound querying, but the conditions governing safe retention of learned clauses across retracted assumptions or frames require authoritative sourcing.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization-Aware Theory Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inline pruning using theory-derived objective lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a feasible incumbent value \(U\) during DPLL-style search. For each theory-consistent partial assignment \(\alpha\), invoke an optimization-aware theory procedure that returns a valid lower bound \(\ell(\alpha)\le\min\{f(M):M\models F\land\alpha\}\), or reports theory inconsistency. Prune the branch if it is inconsistent or \(\ell(\alpha)\ge U\). When a complete feasible model \(M\) with \(f(M)<U\) is found, set \(U=f(M)\). Exhaustion of all unpruned branches returns the stored incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inline optimization-aware search obtains theory-valid lower bounds for partial assignments and prunes any branch unable to improve the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The search space is finite or the underlying decision procedure terminates.
Every returned lower bound is valid for all completions of the partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M^*\models F\) and \(f(M^*)=\min\{f(M):M\models F\}\) after exhaustive termination.

notation.meaning: current partial Boolean or theory assignment
valid lower bound for completions of alpha

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The branch-and-bound logic is coherent under valid completion lower bounds, but the characterization as inline optimization-aware theory search and its optimality claim require a relevant source.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Driven Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch selection guided by predicted objective-bound improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a theory-consistent partial assignment \(\alpha\), let \(B(\alpha)\) be the eligible branching literals. For each \(b\in B(\alpha)\), compute valid or heuristic child-bound estimates \(\widehat\ell(\alpha\land b)\) and \(\widehat\ell(\alpha\land\neg b)\). Select a literal maximizing a prescribed score, for example \(s(b)=\min\{\widehat\ell(\alpha\land b),\widehat\ell(\alpha\land\neg b)\}-\ell(\alpha)\), and visit first the child with smaller estimated bound. Branching changes search order only; feasibility checks and certified pruning must use sound theory reasoning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective-driven branching selects literals whose children are predicted to raise objective lower bounds most, while leaving correctness to sound feasibility and pruning checks.
assumptions_latex: The eligible branching set is finite and nonempty at every incomplete search state.
Heuristic estimates are not used as unsound pruning certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[b^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{b\in B(\alpha)}s(b),\qquad s(b)=\min_{\sigma\in\{b,\neg b\}}\widehat\ell(\alpha\land\sigma)-\ell(\alpha).\]

notation.meaning: eligible branching literals at state alpha

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record clearly separates heuristic ordering from certified pruning, but the proposed score is only one possible heuristic and lacks a source connecting it to objective-driven branching in OMT.

children.title: Lower-Bound Management
children.top_down_role: Representation and maintenance of lower objective bounds during inline optimization.

assumptions_latex: The hard formula \(H\) and current search constraints are interpreted in a fixed background theory \(T\).
The objective \(f\) is minimized and has a known ordered value domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every search state, \(L\leq f^*\), and any sound strengthening may replace \(L\) by \(L'\) only when \(L\leq L'\leq f^*\).

notation.meaning: Optimal objective value over theory-feasible models

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound lower-bound invariant for minimization in inline OMT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^*=\inf\{f(M):M\models_T H\}\). Lower-bound management maintains \(L\) such that \(L\leq f^*\). A theory conflict, relaxation, or infeasibility certificate may produce \(\ell\) satisfying \(\ell\leq f^*\); the sound update is \(L\leftarrow\max\{L,\ell\}\). If the query \(H\land(f<U)\) is unsatisfiable for a candidate threshold \(U\), then the bound implied by that query may be incorporated only according to the objective domain, preserving \(L\leq f^*\). Thus lower bounds are monotone nondecreasing and never exclude an optimal model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inline OMT may raise its lower bound only using sound theory or infeasibility certificates, so the bound remains below the optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Bound Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation is supplied. An authoritative inline-OMT source is required to fix the domain-dependent lower-bound update implied by unsatisfiability of H and f<U. Moreover, defining f* as an infimum does not ensure an optimal model exists, so the claim that no optimal model is excluded requires an attainment assumption or different wording.

children.title: Upper-Bound Management
children.top_down_role: Representation and maintenance of incumbent upper objective bounds.

assumptions_latex: The hard formula \(H\) is interpreted in a fixed theory \(T\).
Every accepted incumbent is a model of \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maintained incumbent value satisfies \(f^*\leq U\), and successive accepted incumbents make \(U\) monotone nonincreasing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent-based upper-bound invariant for minimization in inline OMT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f^*=\inf\{f(M):M\models_T H\}\), upper-bound management stores either \(U=+\infty\) or a feasible incumbent \(M_U\models_T H\) with \(U=f(M_U)\). Whenever a newly found model \(M\models_T H\) satisfies \(f(M)<U\), update \(M_U\leftarrow M\) and \(U\leftarrow f(M)\). Consequently \(f^*\leq U\) always holds, and adding the cutoff \(f<U\) searches only for strict incumbent improvements without removing any model that could improve the current objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent supplies an upper bound; replacing it only by a strictly better feasible model preserves validity and decreases the bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Upper-Bound Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incumbent invariant is mathematically standard, but the record has no inspectable citation supporting its placement and formulation as inline-OMT upper-bound management.

children.title: Bound-Gap Coordination
children.top_down_role: Interaction between lower-bound progress and incumbent improvement.

assumptions_latex: The minimization objective has optimum \(f^*\) and maintained sound bounds \(L\leq f^*\leq U\).
A tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The search may terminate when \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\); then the incumbent is \(\varepsilon\)-optimal in additive objective error.

notation.meaning: Sound lower and upper objective bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive-gap coordination for a single minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Bound-gap coordination preserves \(L\leq f^*\leq U\) while interleaving lower-bound strengthening with incumbent improvement. Define the additive gap by \(g=U-L\). If \(g>\varepsilon\), the coordinator issues a theory-consistent search query whose objective region lies between the current bounds and routes its result to either a valid lower-bound update or a feasible upper-bound update. If \(g\leq\varepsilon\), the incumbent satisfies \(U-f^*\leq U-L\leq\varepsilon\). For \(\varepsilon=0\), equality \(L=U\) certifies exact optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate sound lower and upper bounds until their additive gap is within tolerance; the incumbent is then certified approximately optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Gap Coordination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive-gap implication follows from the stated bound invariant, but no source supports the claimed inline-OMT coordination procedure. The phrase describing a query whose objective region lies between the bounds is not precise enough to identify a sound architecture without a cited variant.

assumptions_latex: The hard constraints \(H\) and soft constraints \((C_i,w_i)\) have positive weights \(w_i\).
A selected set \(K\) is an unsatisfiable core: \(H\land\bigwedge_{i\in K}C_i\) is theory-inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Relaxing the core by fresh indicators preserves feasible cost accounting and raises the certified lower bound by \(\delta=\min_{i\in K}w_i\).

notation.meaning: Indices in the extracted unsatisfiable core
Fresh relaxation indicator for core constraint i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted core relaxation using minimum residual weight and relaxation indicators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a core \(K\), set \(\delta=\min_{i\in K}w_i\) and increase the lower bound by \(\delta\). For each \(i\in K\), introduce a fresh Boolean \(r_i\), replace the active core occurrence by \(C_i\lor r_i\), and retain residual weight \(w_i-\delta\) when it is positive. Add the core constraint \(\sum_{i\in K}r_i\geq1\), or an equisatisfiable encoding thereof. Repeat core extraction and relaxation until the residual instance is satisfiable; combine the accumulated lower bound with the residual model cost to obtain the reported objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relax every constraint in an unsatisfiable core at its minimum residual weight, add a core-hitting constraint, and accumulate that weight as a lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsatisfiable-Core Relaxation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No MaxSMT source or algorithm variant is cited. The proposed minimum-weight split, relaxation indicators, hitting constraint, residual weights, accumulated lower bound, and residual model cost must be tied to one exact core-guided algorithm; as written, the constraints ensuring that relaxation costs are neither omitted nor double counted are underdefined.

children.title: Weight Splitting
children.top_down_role: Decomposition of weighted soft constraints across core-guided search.

assumptions_latex: A soft constraint \(C\\) has positive integer residual weight \(w\).
A split amount \(\delta\) satisfies \(0<\delta\leq w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
The split pieces preserve the penalty exactly: \(w[
eg C]=\delta[
eg C]+(w-\delta)[
eg C]\).

notation.meaning: Indicator equal to one when proposition P holds
Weight extracted from the original soft constraint

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty-preserving split of one weighted soft constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Represent the weighted soft constraint \((C,w)\) by two co-located copies \((C,\delta)\) and \((C,w-\delta)\), omitting the second copy when \(w=\delta\). For every interpretation \(M\), both copies have the same truth value as \(C\), so their combined violation cost is \(\delta[ M
ot\models C]+(w-\delta)[ M
ot\models C]=w[ M
ot\models C]\). Hence splitting changes neither the cost of any interpretation nor the set of optimal interpretations, while permitting the \(\delta\)-weighted part to participate independently in core relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted soft constraint can be divided into equal-form pieces whose weights sum to the original, preserving every assignment's penalty.
knowledge_statements.title: Weight Splitting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cost-preserving identity is plausible, but no weighted MaxSAT/MaxSMT source is supplied. The first assumption also contains malformed notation, "\(C\\\)", which must be repaired when a sourced replacement is prepared.

children.title: Weight Stratification
children.top_down_role: Organization of weighted constraints into prioritized strata.

assumptions_latex: All residual soft weights are positive integers.
The distinct residual weights are \(\tau_1>\tau_2>\cdots>\tau_m>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Processing strata in descending \(\tau_j\) is exact only when lower-stratum costs remain represented or earlier decisions are protected by valid dominance constraints.

notation.meaning: Distinct weight thresholds in descending order
Soft constraints active at threshold j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descending-threshold organization of weighted MaxSMT constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For residual weighted soft constraints \((C_i,w_i)\), define the cumulative stratum \(S_j=\{i:w_i\geq\tau_j\}\). A stratified procedure activates strata in the order \(S_1\subseteq S_2\subseteq\cdots\subseteq S_m\), applying satisfiability or core-guided reasoning at each threshold before admitting lower weights. This ordering is an exact optimization device only if contributions below the current threshold remain in the objective and any commitments made at earlier strata are justified by weight dominance or enforced by constraints that preserve a globally optimal completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weight stratification activates soft constraints from larger to smaller residual weights, while exactness requires preserving all lower-tier costs and globally valid earlier commitments.
knowledge_statements.title: Weight Stratification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No authoritative source identifies the intended stratified weighted-MaxSMT procedure. The statement blends cumulative threshold activation with broad dominance or commitment conditions but does not specify a particular exact algorithm or sufficient formal exactness condition.

children.title: Split-Tier Interaction
children.top_down_role: Effects of weight decomposition across stratified optimization tiers.

assumptions_latex: Each weighted soft constraint is decomposed into positive-weight pieces whose weights sum to its original weight.
Each piece is assigned to the stratum matching its piece weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global exactness is preserved when all split pieces remain costed and cross-tier constraints do not remove any minimum-cost interpretation.

notation.meaning: Original weight and its split piece weights
Violation indicator of soft constraint i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness condition for combining weight splitting with tiered processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w_i=\sum_k\delta_{ik}\) with \(\delta_{ik}>0\), and require all pieces derived from \(C_i\) to share the violation indicator \(v_i=[\neg C_i]\). Then \(w_iv_i=\sum_k\delta_{ik}v_i\), independently of the tiers in which the pieces are processed. Split-tier processing preserves the original optimum provided that every piece remains in the final cost, accumulated lower-bound increments are disjointly justified, and constraints frozen after a tier exclude no interpretation having minimum total cost across all tiers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting and tiering commute only when pieces share the original violation, all piece costs remain counted, and tier commitments preserve a global optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Split-Tier Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The elementary split-cost identity is clear, but the claimed global exactness condition depends on undefined notions of disjointly justified lower-bound increments and frozen tier constraints. A source for a specific split-tier algorithm is needed before the mathematical condition can be fixed.

children.title: Core Minimization
children.top_down_role: Reduction of unsatisfiable cores before optimization processing.

assumptions_latex: The formula \(H\land\bigwedge_{i\in K}C_i\) is theory-unsatisfiable.
Satisfiability checks are sound for the background theory.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(K'\subseteq K\) is an unsatisfiable core; if irreducibility is requested, every \(K'\setminus\{i\}\) is satisfiable with \(H\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion-based minimization to an inclusion-minimal theory core.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(K'\leftarrow K\). For each selected \(i\in K'\), query whether \(H\land\bigwedge_{j\in K'\setminus\{i\}}C_j\) is unsatisfiable. If it is, set \(K'\leftarrow K'\setminus\{i\}\); otherwise retain \(i\). Continue until every remaining member has been tested against the current core, repeating tests if the chosen deletion schedule requires it. Output \(K'\). The result is inclusion-minimal when \(H\land\bigwedge_{j\in K'}C_j\) is unsatisfiable and, for every \(i\in K'\), \(H\land\bigwedge_{j\in K'\setminus\{i\}}C_j\) is satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly delete a core member when unsatisfiability survives; the final core is irreducible when deleting any remaining member makes it satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.title: Core Minimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deletion-based core-minimization algorithm and its inclusion-minimal output condition are standard and fit the leaf, but no source with a specific section, theorem, algorithm, or page locator is supplied.

children.title: Core Reuse
children.top_down_role: Retention of useful core information across optimization iterations.

assumptions_latex: A stored core \(K\) was certified under formula \(F\), so \(F\land\bigwedge_{i\in K}C_i\) is unsatisfiable.
The current formula \(F'\) entails every assumption used by that certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the entailment condition, \(F'\land\bigwedge_{i\in K}C_i\) remains unsatisfiable, so \(K\) may be reused soundly.

notation.meaning: Formula under which the core was learned

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entailment-based reuse of previously certified unsatisfiable cores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a stored certificate establishes \(F\land\bigwedge_{i\in K}C_i\models_T\bot\). The core \(K\) is reusable in a later state \(F'\) whenever \(F'\models_T F\), or more generally whenever \(F'\) entails all clauses and assumptions actually used by the certificate. Then \(F'\land\bigwedge_{i\in K}C_i\models_T\bot\). Reuse may therefore avoid a new theory check, but any relaxation variables, weights, or activation literals attached to the stored core must be translated to their current semantically equivalent counterparts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A learned core remains reusable when the current state entails every constraint used in its unsatisfiability certificate and its literals retain equivalent meanings.
knowledge_statements.title: Core Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The entailment argument is mathematically sound, but no incremental SMT/MaxSMT source supports the operational reuse claim or the required translation of relaxation and activation literals.

children.title: Core-Reuse Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions limiting when retained core information remains applicable.

assumptions_latex: A core was learned from active assumptions \(A\) under formula \(F\).
The current state may retract constraints, rename activation literals, or alter relaxed soft-constraint semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reuse is unsound in general unless the current assumptions imply the certificate context and every reused literal preserves its former semantics.

notation.meaning: Original certificate context and current context

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for core reuse after weakening or semantic mutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Core reuse is not preserved under arbitrary formula weakening. For example, let \(F=(p)\) and let the stored assumption set be \(A=\{\neg p\}\); then \(F\land\bigwedge A\) is unsatisfiable. After retracting \(p\), take \(F'=\top\); now \(F'\land\bigwedge A\) is satisfiable. The same failure can occur when a relaxation or activation literal is reused after its defining constraint or weight meaning changes. Thus a core may be reused only with a valid implication from the current context to the certificate context and a semantics-preserving literal mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retracting a constraint or changing an activation literal's meaning can invalidate a stored core; reuse requires contextual entailment and semantic stability.
knowledge_statements.title: Core-Reuse Validity Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly shows that weakening can invalidate a stored core, and failure_boundary is the appropriate content kind. An authoritative incremental SMT/MaxSMT citation is still required for candidate-review admission.

children.title: Cardinality Encodings
children.top_down_role: Boolean encodings for bounded counts of satisfied or violated literals.

assumptions_latex: The variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) are Boolean.
The desired constraint is \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\leq k\), where \(0\leq k\leq n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A cardinality encoding \(E(x,y)\) is correct exactly when \(\exists y\,E(x,y)\leftrightarrow\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\leq k\) for every assignment to \(x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existentially correct CNF representation of an at-most cardinality constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A CNF formula \(E(x,y)\), with fresh auxiliary Boolean variables \(y\), encodes the at-most-\(k\) cardinality constraint when, for every assignment \(a\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\leq k\) if and only if there exists an assignment \(b\) such that \(E(a,b)\) is true. Consequently, conjoining \(E\) to a MaxSMT Boolean abstraction preserves precisely those assignments to the original variables satisfying the bound. At-least and equality constraints follow by literal complementation or by conjoining sound at-most and at-least encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cardinality encoding uses auxiliary Boolean variables so its existential projection accepts exactly assignments with at most the permitted number of true literals.
knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The existential-projection criterion is a suitable representation statement for cardinality encodings, but no citation with an inspectable locator is supplied. The local inventory contains no relevant cardinality-encoding source.

children.title: Pseudo-Boolean Encodings
children.top_down_role: Encodings supporting weighted Boolean sums and integer thresholds.

assumptions_latex: The variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) are Boolean and coefficients \(a_i\) and bound \(B\) are integers.
The target inequality is \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_ix_i\leq B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A pseudo-Boolean encoding \(P(x,y)\) is correct exactly when \(\exists y\,P(x,y)\leftrightarrow\sum_{i=1}^n a_ix_i\leq B\) for every assignment to \(x\).

notation.meaning: CNF encoding with auxiliary variables y

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existentially correct CNF representation of a pseudo-Boolean inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A CNF formula \(P(x,y)\), with fresh auxiliary Boolean variables \(y\), encodes \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_ix_i\leq B\) when, for every \(c\in\{0,1\}^n\), there exists an assignment to \(y\) satisfying \(P(c,y)\) if and only if \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_ic_i\leq B\). Coefficients may first be normalized by moving negative terms and adjusting \(B\). Under this projection condition, replacing the inequality by \(P\) preserves feasibility over the original variables and can represent weighted relaxation budgets in encoding-based MaxSMT.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pseudo-Boolean encoding projects to exactly the Boolean assignments satisfying the weighted linear inequality, thereby preserving feasibility over original variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Pseudo-Boolean Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The existential-projection criterion fits pseudo-Boolean encodings, but no relevant source is cited. The normalization claim for negative coefficients also needs a precise transformation or a supporting locator before acceptance.

children.title: Encoding-Family Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Size, propagation, and backend compatibility differences across encoding families.

assumptions_latex: The Boolean inputs are \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), and the intended constraint is either \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le k\) or \(\sum_{i=1}^n w_i x_i\le B\), with \(w_i,B\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For unit weights, a cardinality encoding can represent the bound without binary arithmetic, whereas a pseudo-Boolean encoding also represents nonuniform weights. The appropriate family is therefore selected by comparing its encoded size and propagation behavior on the required bound: cardinality encodings exploit \(w_i=1\), while weighted instances generally require pseudo-Boolean machinery or an expansion whose size depends on the weights.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the comparative encoding claim; an authoritative SAT or pseudo-Boolean encoding source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection principle for cardinality versus weighted pseudo-Boolean constraints in encoding-based MaxSMT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\{0,1\}\). A cardinality constraint has the form \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le k\), while a pseudo-Boolean constraint has the form \(\sum_{i=1}^n w_i x_i\le B\) with \(w_i,B\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). A cardinality encoding directly exploits unit coefficients and need only distinguish counts relevant to \(k\). A pseudo-Boolean encoding preserves arbitrary coefficients but must additionally represent weighted accumulation or equivalent decompositions. Consequently, family selection is governed jointly by encoded size, coefficient magnitude, and propagation strength; neither family uniformly dominates on all instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cardinality encodings specialize to unit weights; pseudo-Boolean encodings handle arbitrary integer weights. Their practical tradeoff depends on formula size, coefficient magnitude, and propagation strength.
knowledge_statements.title: Encoding-Family Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the tradeoff leaf and is mathematically plausible, but no citation supports the claims about encoded size, coefficient magnitude, propagation, or lack of uniform dominance.

children.title: Sorting Networks
children.top_down_role: Comparator-network representations that order Boolean inputs.

assumptions_latex: The inputs are Boolean variables \(x_1,\\ldots,x_n\).
Every comparator is represented by clauses enforcing its two outputs as the maximum and minimum of its two inputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output variables satisfy \(y_1\ge\cdots\ge y_n\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^n y_i=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\); hence \(y_j=1\) exactly when at least \(j\) inputs are true.

notation.meaning: a comparator's high and low outputs

review_flags: No supplied locator covers sorting-network CNF encodings; a direct encoding reference is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean sorting-network representation used to encode cardinality bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Boolean sorting network is an acyclic network of comparators. Each comparator maps inputs \(a,b\in\{0,1\}\) to outputs \(h=a\lor b\) and \(\ell=a\land b\). For every input vector \((x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), the network outputs \((y_1,\ldots,y_n)\) satisfying \(y_1\ge\cdots\ge y_n\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^n y_i=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\). Thus \(y_j=1\) if and only if \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\ge j\), so the bound \(\sum_i x_i\le k\) is imposed by the unit clause \(\neg y_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Boolean sorting network orders its inputs while preserving their number of true values. A cardinality upper bound is enforced by setting the output at position k+1 to false.
knowledge_statements.title: Sorting Networks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits Sorting Networks and the mathematical statement is standard, but it has no cited source. The first assumption also contains malformed `\\ldots` notation and should use `\ldots`.

children.title: Cardinality Networks
children.top_down_role: Network representations specialized for Boolean cardinality constraints.

assumptions_latex: The inputs are Boolean variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), and only the first \(k+1\) sorted ranks are relevant.
The network's comparator relations are encoded propositionally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The designated outputs satisfy \(y_j=1\iff\sum_i x_i\ge j\) for \(1\le j\le k+1\), and \(\neg y_{k+1}\) encodes \(\sum_i x_i\le k\).
review_flags: No supplied locator supports the specialized cardinality-network construction or size bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated sorting networks specialized to an at-most-\(k\) constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\{0,1\}\) and \(0\le k<n\), a cardinality network computes only the sorted ranks needed to decide whether more than \(k\) inputs are true. Its designated outputs \(y_1,\ldots,y_{k+1}\) satisfy \(y_j=1\) if and only if \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\ge j\). Consequently, conjoining the network encoding with \(\neg y_{k+1}\) is equisatisfiable, over the original inputs, with \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le k\). The construction may discard ranks beyond \(k+1\) without changing this equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cardinality network computes only threshold ranks needed for an at-most-k test. Its k+1 output is false exactly when no more than k inputs are true.
knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality Networks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits Cardinality Networks, but a direct source is required for the truncated-network construction, threshold-output semantics, and equisatisfiability claim.

children.title: Network-Family Selection
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria for choosing between sorting-oriented and cardinality-oriented networks.

assumptions_latex: The target is a Boolean constraint \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le k\).
Candidate encodings are compared under the same SAT solver and incremental usage pattern.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A full sorting network is reusable for many bounds on the same inputs, while a cardinality network can omit irrelevant ranks for a fixed bound; selection must account for reuse, encoded size, and propagation rather than asymptotic size alone.
review_flags: The selection rule is standard but requires a comparative source on sorting and cardinality networks.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection between full sorting and bound-specialized cardinality networks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed constraint \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le k\), a cardinality network may retain only ranks \(1,\ldots,k+1\), whereas a full sorting network computes all \(n\) ranks. The truncated family can therefore reduce auxiliary variables and comparator clauses when \(k\ll n\). Conversely, if optimization repeatedly changes the bound on the same inputs, a full network permits each bound to be asserted through an output literal without rebuilding the network. Selection should minimize total encoding and solver cost across all anticipated bounds, including reuse and propagation, not merely the initial clause count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use truncated cardinality networks for a fixed small bound; full sorting networks may be preferable when many bounds reuse the same inputs. Compare total size, reuse, and propagation.
knowledge_statements.title: Network-Family Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selection principle fits the leaf, but the asserted size, reuse, and propagation tradeoffs require a comparative sorting/cardinality-network source.

assumptions_latex: The hard formula is \(H\), and soft clauses \(C_i\) have nonnegative integer weights \(w_i\).
The backend accepts weighted partial MaxSAT and returns an optimum model or unsatisfiability of \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The translated instance has optimum \(\min\{\sum_i w_i r_i:H\land\bigwedge_i(C_i\lor r_i)\}\), equal to the minimum total weight of violated soft clauses.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports weighted partial MaxSAT backend integration.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-preserving interface from encoding-based MaxSMT to weighted partial MaxSAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given hard clauses \(H\) and weighted soft clauses \((C_i,w_i)\) with \(w_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), introduce a relaxation variable \(r_i\) for each soft clause and submit \(H\land\bigwedge_i(C_i\lor r_i)\) to a weighted partial MaxSAT backend with objective \(\min\sum_i w_i r_i\). For any assignment satisfying \(H\), setting \(r_i=1\) exactly for violated \(C_i\) yields the same cost as the soft-clause violation cost. Therefore the backend optimum and an optimal projected assignment constitute an optimum for the encoded MaxSMT abstraction, provided all theory constraints have been soundly Booleanized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relax each weighted soft clause with a costed Boolean variable. A weighted partial MaxSAT backend then minimizes exactly the total weight of violated encoded soft clauses.
knowledge_statements.title: MaxSAT Backend Integration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is appropriate for MaxSAT backend integration, but no source supports the relaxation-variable translation or its objective-preservation and projection guarantees.

children.title: Theory-Specific OMT

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Optimization Modulo Theories with Linear Rational Costs
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Linear rational cost minimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Optimization Modulo Theories with Linear Rational Costs

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb Q^n\) is defined by a quantifier-free linear-rational-arithmetic formula.
The objective is the affine rational function \(c(x)=c^\top x+d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimization value is \(v=\inf_{x\in F}c(x)\); an optimal model exists exactly when some \(x^*\in F\) satisfies \(c(x^*)=v\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly treats OMT over linear rational arithmetic and nonattained optima.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-objective minimization over quantifier-free linear rational arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb Q^n:\varphi(x)\}\), where \(\varphi\) is a quantifier-free Boolean combination of linear rational equalities and inequalities, and let \(c(x)=c^\top x+d\) with \(c\in\mathbb Q^n\) and \(d\in\mathbb Q\). Rational-objective minimization asks for \(v=\inf\{c(x):x\in F\}\) in \(\mathbb Q\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}\). If \(F=\varnothing\), then \(v=+\infty\); if the objective is unbounded below, then \(v=-\infty\). Otherwise, an optimal model is required only when some \(x^*\in F\) attains \(c(x^*)=v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rational-objective OMT minimizes an affine rational function over an LRA-definable feasible set. Its value may be infeasible, unbounded, attained, or a finite unattained infimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Rational-Objective Minimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits rational-objective minimization and consistently distinguishes infeasibility, unboundedness, attainment, and finite unattained infima, but no inspectable OMT/LRA source is cited.

children.title: Strict-Inequality Regimes
children.top_down_role: Linear rational OMT settings containing strict objective-relevant inequalities.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb Q^n\) includes at least one strict linear inequality.
The affine objective \(c(x)\) is bounded below on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite value \(v=\inf_{x\in F}c(x)\) need not be attained; for example, \(F=\{x\in\mathbb Q:x>0\}\) and \(c(x)=x\) have \(v=0\) but no minimizer.
review_flags: Concrete claim is self-checking, but a direct OMT source for strict-bound semantics is still required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonattainment caused by strict rational inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Strict linear inequalities can make an LRA-feasible set nonclosed and thereby prevent objective attainment. Concretely, take \(F=\{x\in\mathbb Q:x>0\}\) and minimize \(c(x)=x\). Then every feasible point has positive cost, while for every \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\), the point \(x=\varepsilon/2\) is feasible with \(c(x)<\varepsilon\). Hence \(\inf_{x\in F}c(x)=0\), but no \(x^*\in F\) satisfies \(c(x^*)=0\). An OMT result must therefore distinguish a finite infimum from an attained minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict inequalities can exclude the boundary carrying the best value. Minimizing x subject to x>0 has infimum zero over the rationals but no optimal model.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Inequality Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the example is mathematically correct, but the record lacks a source for its interpretation within LRA-based OMT result semantics.

children.title: Infimum Regimes
children.top_down_role: Optimization settings where the best bound is approached without a matching feasible value.

assumptions_latex: The nonempty feasible set is \(F\subseteq\mathbb Q^n\).
The affine objective \(c:F\to\mathbb Q\) is bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The finite value \(v=\inf c(F)\) satisfies \(v\le c(x)\) for all \(x\in F\) and, for every rational \(\varepsilon>0\), some \(x_\varepsilon\in F\) satisfies \(c(x_\varepsilon)<v+\varepsilon\); attainment additionally requires \(v\in c(F)\).
review_flags: The order-theoretic characterization is standard, but no supplied source addresses its OMT interpretation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite lower bounds represented as infima, including unattained values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty \(F\subseteq\mathbb Q^n\) and an affine objective \(c\) bounded below on \(F\), a rational number \(v\) is the infimum value exactly when both conditions hold: \(v\le c(x)\) for every \(x\in F\), and for every \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\) there exists \(x_\varepsilon\in F\) such that \(c(x_\varepsilon)<v+\varepsilon\). This characterization does not imply \(v\in c(F)\). The regime is attained precisely when some \(x^*\in F\) satisfies \(c(x^*)=v\); otherwise it is an unattained-infimum regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite infimum is a lower bound approached arbitrarily closely by feasible costs. It is a minimum only when the infimum itself is an attainable cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Infimum Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly characterizes a finite infimum and fits the leaf, but no citation supports its intended OMT interpretation.

children.title: Objective-Attainment Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural distinctions between attained optima and unattained limiting values.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb Q^n\) is nonempty and defined by linear rational constraints.
The affine objective \(c\) has finite infimum \(v\) on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The boundary at value \(v\) is attained exactly when \(F\cap\{x:c(x)=v\}\ne\varnothing\); otherwise every feasible point satisfies \(c(x)>v\) although feasible costs approach \(v\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports objective-attainment boundaries in LRA-based OMT.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact test separating attained minima from excluded optimal boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v=\inf_{x\in F}c(x)\in\mathbb Q\). The objective-attainment boundary is the level set \(L_v=\{x\in\mathbb Q^n:c(x)=v\}\). The optimum is attained if and only if \(F\cap L_v\ne\varnothing\). If \(F\cap L_v=\varnothing\), then every feasible point satisfies \(c(x)>v\), while the infimum property ensures that for every \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\) some feasible point has cost below \(v+\varepsilon\). Thus satisfiability of the boundary constraint \(c(x)=v\) exactly separates minimum and unattained-infimum regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a finite infimum v, objective attainment is exactly feasibility of the level set c(x)=v. If infeasible, costs approach v without reaching it.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Attainment Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits objective-attainment boundaries and is mathematically precise, but it has no source supporting the boundary-feasibility criterion in LRA OMT.

children.title: OMT over Linear Integer Arithmetic
children.top_down_role: SMT–optimization coordination only; polyhedral theory, general cuts, branching, fixed-dimension algorithms, and decomposition remain in the integer-optimization chapter.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) is defined by linear integer arithmetic.
The integer-valued objective \(c(x)\) has known integer bounds \(L\le c(x)\le U\) on feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Repeated feasibility queries at integer bounds terminate with the least \(b\) for which \(F\cap\{x:c(x)\le b\}\ne\varnothing\), which equals the attained optimum.
review_flags: The supplied integer-programming locator supports the ambient problem class but not the stated SMT bound-search algorithm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary feasibility search for a bounded integer-valued objective.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.1 Linear integer program p. 29

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(F\ne\varnothing\), \(c(F)\subseteq\mathbb Z\), and integers \(L\le U\) bracket every feasible objective value. While \(L<U\), set \(m=\lfloor(L+U)/2\rfloor\) and query satisfiability of \(F\cap\{x:c(x)\le m\}\). If satisfiable, retain a model and set \(U=m\); otherwise set \(L=m+1\). Upon termination, output the retained model satisfying \(c(x)=L\). Monotonicity of the bound query and discreteness of \(c(F)\) imply that \(L\) is the smallest feasible objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary-search integer objective bounds using SMT feasibility queries. Satisfiable bounds lower the upper endpoint; unsatisfiable bounds raise the lower endpoint until the exact optimum remains.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Objective Bound Search

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.1 Linear integer program p. 29
