children.title: Signed Bit-Vector Optimization
children.top_down_role: Bit-vector optimization under signed numeric interpretation.

assumptions_latex: \(w\ge 1\) is a fixed bit width.
\(\Phi\) is a quantifier-free bit-vector formula whose objective term \(t\) has width \(w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{m\models\Phi}\operatorname{sval}_w(t^m)\), when \(\Phi\) is satisfiable.

notation.meaning: unsigned integer encoded by a width-w bit vector

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-objective minimization under the two's-complement interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a width-\(w\) bit vector \(b\), define \(\operatorname{sval}_w(b)=\operatorname{uval}_w(b)\) when \(\operatorname{uval}_w(b)<2^{w-1}\), and \(\operatorname{sval}_w(b)=\operatorname{uval}_w(b)-2^w\) otherwise. Signed bit-vector minimization of \(t\) subject to \(\Phi\) asks for a model \(m^*\models\Phi\) satisfying \[\operatorname{sval}_w(t^{m^*})=\min_{m\models\Phi}\operatorname{sval}_w(t^m).\] Because the signed codomain is the finite ordered set \(\{-2^{w-1},\ldots,2^{w-1}-1\}\), every satisfiable instance attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the two's-complement value of a fixed-width bit-vector objective over all models of the bit-vector constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Signed Bit-Vector Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The signed two's-complement formulation is mathematically precise and fits a definition container, but no inspectable source supports the bit-vector semantics or OMT formulation.

children.title: Unsigned Bit-Vector Optimization
children.top_down_role: Bit-vector optimization under unsigned numeric interpretation.

assumptions_latex: \(w\ge 1\) is a fixed bit width.
\(\Phi\) is a quantifier-free bit-vector formula whose objective term \(t\) has width \(w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{m\models\Phi}\operatorname{uval}_w(t^m)\), when \(\Phi\) is satisfiable.

notation.meaning: natural-number interpretation of a width-w bit vector

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-objective minimization under the unsigned interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a width-\(w\) bit vector \(b=b_{w-1}\cdots b_0\), define its unsigned value by \[\operatorname{uval}_w(b)=\sum_{i=0}^{w-1}2^i b_i\in\{0,\ldots,2^w-1\}.\] Unsigned bit-vector minimization of an objective term \(t\) subject to \(\Phi\) asks for a model \(m^*\models\Phi\) such that \[\operatorname{uval}_w(t^{m^*})=\min_{m\models\Phi}\operatorname{uval}_w(t^m).\] The objective range is finite, so every satisfiable instance has an attaining optimal model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the natural-number value encoded by a fixed-width bit-vector objective over all feasible models.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsigned Bit-Vector Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unsigned formulation is mathematically precise and appropriately classified as a definition, but it has no cited source with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Signedness Interpretation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where objective ordering changes with the selected bit-vector interpretation.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Signed and unsigned optimization can select different optimal bit patterns from the same feasible set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary caused solely by interpreting the most significant bit as a sign bit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=10\cdots0\) and \(y=01\cdots1\) be width-\(w\) bit vectors. Their interpretations satisfy \[\operatorname{sval}_w(x)=-2^{w-1}<2^{w-1}-1=\operatorname{sval}_w(y),\] but \[\operatorname{uval}_w(y)=2^{w-1}-1<2^{w-1}=\operatorname{uval}_w(x).\] Hence, for the feasible set \(\{x,y\}\), signed minimization uniquely selects \(x\), whereas unsigned minimization uniquely selects \(y\). Signed and unsigned comparison or optimization operators therefore cannot be interchanged unless the feasible objective values remain within a region where both interpretations induce the same order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sign bit can reverse objective order: the same two feasible bit patterns may have opposite signed and unsigned minima.
knowledge_statements.title: Signedness Interpretation Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly exhibits reversal between signed and unsigned order and fits the failure-boundary container, but no source is cited.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a fixed IEEE-style floating-point format with a specified rounding mode.
\(\Phi\) and objective term \(t\) are evaluated entirely in the selected floating-point semantics.
Objective NaNs are excluded, and a fixed total order handles infinities and signed zeros.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(M=\{m:m\models_F\Phi\}\neq\varnothing\), optimization returns an order-minimal value in \(\{t^m:m\in M\}\).

notation.meaning: the regime's specified total order on non-NaN floating-point values

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic regime with explicit NaN, infinity, signed-zero, and rounding policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A floating-point optimization regime is the tuple consisting of a format \(F\), a rounding mode, floating-point satisfaction \(\models_F\), an admissible objective set excluding NaN, and a total order \(\preceq_F\) on admissible values. Minimization of \(t\) subject to \(\Phi\) seeks \(m^*\models_F\Phi\) such that \[t^{m^*}\preceq_F t^m\quad\text{for every }m\models_F\Phi.\] All operations, including conversions and comparisons, use the declared finite-precision semantics. Since a fixed format has finitely many values, every nonempty feasible objective image has a minimum under the declared total order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Floating-point optimization requires fixed precision, rounding, comparison, NaN, infinity, and signed-zero policies; under a total order, every feasible finite-format instance attains a minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Floating-Point Optimization Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition appropriately exposes the format, rounding, NaN, infinity, signed-zero, and ordering policies, but these noncanonical policy choices and their OMT interpretation require an authoritative floating-point source.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Model Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper-bound certificate for minimization; inequalities reverse for maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the minimization problem \(v^*=\inf\{f(m):m\models\Phi\}\), a feasible-model bound certificate consists of a model \(\hat m\) and an exactly evaluated value \(U=f(\hat m)\). Verification checks \(\hat m\models\Phi\) in the background theory and verifies the objective evaluation. The certified conclusion is \[v^*\le U.\] If an independently certified lower bound \(L\) satisfies \(L=U\), then \(\hat m\) attains the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible model with checked objective value U certifies that the optimal infimum is at most U; a matching certified lower bound proves attainment and optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(M=\{m:m\models\Phi\}\neq\varnothing\).
The problem minimizes a real-valued objective \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A checkable model \(\hat m\models\Phi\) certifies \(v^*\le f(\hat m)\), where \(v^*=\inf_{m\in M}f(m)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible-Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict bound query for a real-valued minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization subject to \(\Phi\), an infeasible-bound certificate for \(L\in\mathbb{R}\) is a checkable refutation of \[\Phi\land(f<L).\] Sound validation certifies \[m\models\Phi\implies f(m)\ge L\] and hence \[L\le\inf_{m\models\Phi}f(m).\] Without a feasible model of value \(L\), this certificate does not establish attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checked refutation of feasibility below L certifies that every feasible objective value is at least L, but does not by itself certify attainment.
assumptions_latex: \(M=\{m:m\models\Phi\}\) and \(f:M\to\mathbb{R}\).
A sound theory checker validates unsatisfiability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unsatisfiability of \(\Phi\land(f<L)\) certifies \(f(m)\ge L\) for every \(m\in M\).

children.title: Optimum-Attainment Certification
children.top_down_role: Certificate evidence associated with a feasible model realizing the optimum.

assumptions_latex: \(M=\{m:m\models\Phi\}\neq\varnothing\).
The objective \(f:M\to\mathbb{R}\) is minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible model of value \(v\) plus a refutation of \(\Phi\land(f<v)\) certifies \(v=\min_{m\in M}f(m)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An optimum-attainment certificate consists of a model \(m^*\), a value \(v\), and a sound refutation of the strict-improvement query. Verification checks \[m^*\models\Phi,\qquad f(m^*)=v,\qquad \Phi\land(f<v)\text{ is unsatisfiable}.\] The first two checks establish attainability and the upper bound \(\inf_{m\models\Phi}f(m)\le v\). The refutation establishes the matching lower bound \(f(m)\ge v\) for every \(m\models\Phi\). Consequently, \[v=\min_{m\models\Phi}f(m)=f(m^*).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible model of value v and a checked refutation of every strictly better value certify an attained optimum v.

knowledge_statements.title: Infimum Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical certification criterion; a finite encoding of the approximation family is solver-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An infimum-certification criterion for \(v\in\mathbb{R}\) validates both \[m\models\Phi\implies f(m)\ge v\] and \[\forall\varepsilon>0\;\exists m_\varepsilon\models\Phi:\ f(m_\varepsilon)<v+\varepsilon.\] The lower-bound condition may be represented by a refutation of \(\Phi\land(f<v)\). The approximation condition requires a checkable family, symbolic construction, or sound theory argument. Together the conditions certify \[v=\inf_{m\models\Phi}f(m).\] They do not assert that a feasible model attains \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infimum certificate combines a global lower bound with feasible values arbitrarily close above it; no feasible model need attain the value.
assumptions_latex: \(M=\{m:m\models\Phi\}\neq\varnothing\).
The objective \(f:M\to\mathbb{R}\) is minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lower-bound and arbitrarily-close feasibility conditions certify \(v=\inf_{m\in M}f(m)\), without asserting attainment.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

children.title: Attainment–Infimum Distinctions
children.top_down_role: Certification differences between realized objective values and unattained limits.

knowledge_statements.title: Attainment–Infimum Distinctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete open-domain example separating a finite infimum from an attained minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(0,1]\subset\mathbb{R}\) and \(f:M\to\mathbb{R}\) be defined by \(f(x)=x\). Then \[\inf_{x\in M}f(x)=0\] while \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in M}f(x)=\varnothing.\] Thus certification of an infimum does not imply certification of an attained optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the domain (0,1], minimizing x has infimum 0 but no minimizing point, so infimum certification and optimum-attainment certification are distinct.
assumptions_latex: The feasible domain is \(M=(0,1]\subset\mathbb{R}\).
The objective is \(f(x)=x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in M}f(x)=0\), but \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in M}f(x)=\varnothing\).

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Optimality and Relaxation p. 25

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Optimality and Relaxation p. 25

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a set of hard clauses and \(S\) is a finite set of unit-cost soft clauses.
\(U_1,\ldots,U_k\subseteq S\) are pairwise disjoint.
Each \(H\cup U_j\) is certified unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every model of \(H\) violates at least \(k\) clauses of \(S\), so the MaxSMT cost is at least \(k\).

notation.meaning: pairwise disjoint unsatisfiable soft cores relative to H

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjoint-core lower bound for unweighted partial MaxSMT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A disjoint-core lower-bound certificate is a family \(U_1,\ldots,U_k\subseteq S\) such that the \(U_j\) are pairwise disjoint and each formula \[H\land\bigwedge_{C\in U_j}C\] is accompanied by a checkable unsatisfiability certificate. Any assignment satisfying \(H\) must falsify at least one soft clause in every \(U_j\). Disjointness makes these falsified clauses distinct, so every hard-feasible assignment has unit-cost MaxSMT value at least \(k\). Thus the verified cores certify the lower bound \[\operatorname{OPT}(H,S)\ge k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each of k disjoint certified unsatisfiable soft cores forces a distinct violated clause, certifying a unit-cost MaxSMT lower bound k.
knowledge_statements.title: Core-Based Lower-Bound Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The disjoint-core argument is correct for the explicitly restricted unweighted setting and certificate is the appropriate content kind, but no MaxSMT source or certificate specification is cited.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a hard formula and \(C_1,\ldots,C_n\) are soft clauses.
Each relaxation variable \(r_i\) has cost \(w_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A satisfying relaxation assignment certifies the upper bound \(\operatorname{OPT}\le\sum_i w_i r_i\).

notation.meaning: relaxation variable permitting violation of soft clause i
positive weight of soft clause i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper-bound certificate for weighted partial MaxSMT using relaxation variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce a Boolean relaxation variable \(r_i\) for each weighted soft clause \((C_i,w_i)\). A satisfying-relaxation certificate is an assignment \(m\) for which \[m\models H\land\bigwedge_{i=1}^n(C_i\lor r_i).\] Its checked cost is \[U=\sum_{i=1}^n w_i\,m(r_i),\] where Boolean values are identified with \(0\) and \(1\). Clauses with \(m(r_i)=0\) must be satisfied, while clauses with \(m(r_i)=1\) are paid for. Therefore the assignment is a feasible weighted relaxation and certifies \(\operatorname{OPT}\le U\), although unnecessary true relaxation variables may make the bound non-tight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model satisfying every hard clause and every relaxed soft clause certifies an upper bound equal to the weight of enabled relaxations.
knowledge_statements.title: Satisfying-Relaxation Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The satisfying-relaxation assignment correctly supplies a weighted MaxSMT upper bound, but the record has no inspectable source for the relaxation encoding or certificate interpretation.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is hard, and soft clause \(C_i\) has weight \(w_i>0\).
Each \(U_j\) is an unsatisfiable core relative to \(H\).
Multipliers satisfy \(\lambda_j\ge0\) and \(\sum_{j:i\in U_j}\lambda_j\le w_i\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible assignment of cost \(U\) with \(U=\sum_j\lambda_j\) certifies weighted MaxSMT optimality.

notation.meaning: verified unsatisfiable soft core relative to the hard constraints
nonnegative weight assigned to core j
cost of a certified satisfying relaxation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal feasible assignment paired with a capacitated weighted-core lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each verified core \(U_j\), assign a multiplier \(\lambda_j\ge0\). If \[\sum_{j:i\in U_j}\lambda_j\le w_i\quad\text{for every soft clause }C_i,\] then the cores and multipliers certify the lower bound \(L=\sum_j\lambda_j\): every hard-feasible assignment violates at least one clause in each core, and the capacity inequalities charge no clause beyond its weight. Separately, a satisfying-relaxation assignment of cost \(U\) certifies \(\operatorname{OPT}\le U\). When the two checked values coincide, \[U=L,\] the combined certificate establishes \(\operatorname{OPT}=U=L\) and certifies the assignment as weighted-optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verified weighted cores give a lower bound; a feasible relaxation gives an upper bound. Equality of the two certifies weighted MaxSMT optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Optimality Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The capacitated fractional core packing and matching feasible upper bound form a plausible weighted optimality certificate, but the nontrivial weighted-core lower-bound construction requires authoritative source validation.

assumptions_latex: The OMT formula \(F\) is interpreted in a fixed background theory, with feasible set \(S=\{x:x\models F\}\neq\varnothing\).
Each objective \(f_i:S\to D_i\) is minimized with respect to a linear order on \(D_i\), and every stage minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model \(x^\star\) is lexicographically optimal.

notation.meaning: Feasible models remaining after the first i objectives are fixed optimally

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization with a fixed priority order and attained stagewise optima.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(S_0=S\). For \(i=1,\ldots,k\), define \(v_i=\min\{f_i(x):x\in S_{i-1}\}\) and \(S_i=\{x\in S_{i-1}:f_i(x)=v_i\}\). A feasible model \(x^\star\in S\) is lexicographically optimal precisely when \(x^\star\in S_k\). Equivalently, there do not exist \(y\in S\) and \(j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) such that \(f_i(y)=f_i(x^\star)\) for every \(i<j\) and \(f_j(y)<f_j(x^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model is lexicographically optimal when it minimizes the first objective, then the second among first-objective minimizers, and so on.
knowledge_statements.title: Lexicographic Optimality

assumptions_latex: The OMT formula \(F\) has feasible set \(S\), and all objectives \(f_i:S\to D_i\) are minimized.
Objective values are compared componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The supplied model and dominance-unsatisfiability result certify Pareto optimality.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate for strong Pareto optimality under componentwise minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Pareto-optimality certificate consists of a model \(x^\star\models F\) and a theory-unsatisfiability certificate for \[F(y)\land\bigwedge_{i=1}^{k} f_i(y)\le f_i(x^\star)\land\bigvee_{i=1}^{k} f_i(y)<f_i(x^\star).\] Feasibility of \(x^\star\) establishes an attainable objective vector, while unsatisfiability establishes that no feasible \(y\) weakly improves every objective and strictly improves at least one. Hence \(x^\star\) is Pareto optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible model is certified Pareto optimal by proving that no feasible model weakly improves every objective and strictly improves at least one.
knowledge_statements.title: Pareto-Optimality Certification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate exactly characterizes strong Pareto optimality for componentwise minimization, and certificate is the correct role for this certification leaf. No inspectable citation is supplied, so the theory-unsatisfiability certificate formulation remains unsupported.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(S=\{x:x\models F\}\) is nonempty.
Every scalar objective \(f_i:S\to D_i\) has an attained minimum \(v_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certificate proves simultaneous attainment of all independently computed objective minima.

notation.meaning: Independently optimal value of objective i

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous certification of separately minimized objectives, not merely Pareto optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An independent-objective certificate contains a common model \(x^\star\models F\), values \(v_1,\ldots,v_k\), and, for every \(i\), a certificate that \(F(x)\land f_i(x)<v_i\) is theory-unsatisfiable. It additionally verifies \(f_i(x^\star)=v_i\) for every \(i\). Thus each \(v_i\) is the global minimum of \(f_i\) over the original feasible set, and \(x^\star\) attains all these minima simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common feasible model attains every objective's separately certified global minimum; incompatibility among the separate minima makes such a certificate impossible.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent-Objective Certification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement correctly distinguishes simultaneous attainment of separately established scalar minima from ordinary Pareto optimality, and certificate fits the leaf. The specialized independent-objective certificate semantics have no cited source.

children.title: Infeasible OMT
children.top_down_role: OMT instances lacking any theory-consistent feasible solution.

assumptions_latex: The OMT instance minimizes an objective \(f\) subject to a theory formula \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimization status is infeasible, so no feasible objective value or optimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infeasibility status for an OMT instance, checkable through theory unsatisfiability before objective comparison.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Optimality and Relaxation p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The OMT instance is infeasible exactly when \(S=\varnothing\), equivalently when \(F\) is unsatisfiable in the background theory. A sound theory-unsatisfiability derivation for \(F\) certifies this status. Since no model satisfies the constraints, there is no attainable objective value and no optimizing model; the instance is classified as infeasible rather than bounded or unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An OMT instance is infeasible when its constraints have no theory model; a sound unsatisfiability derivation certifies this status independently of the objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible OMT

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Optimality and Relaxation p. 25

children.title: Unbounded OMT
children.top_down_role: Feasible OMT instances lacking a finite optimum in the optimization direction.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(S=\{x:x\models F\}\) is nonempty.
The OMT instance minimizes \(f:S\to\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The infimum is \(-\infty\), so no finite optimum exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unboundedness below for a feasible real-valued minimization OMT instance.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The OMT instance is unbounded below when \[\forall B\in\mathbb{R}\;\exists x\in S:\ f(x)<B.\] Equivalently, every threshold formula \(F(x)\land f(x)<B\) is satisfiable. A sufficient symbolic certificate may exhibit a feasible parametric family \(x(t)\), defined for every \(t\ge t_0\), such that \(f(x(t))\to-\infty\), together with theory checks establishing its feasibility. In either case, \(\inf f(S)=-\infty\), so no finite optimum exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible minimization OMT instance is unbounded below when feasible objective values fall below every real threshold, giving infimum minus infinity.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded OMT

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

children.title: Feasibility–Boundedness Status Distinctions
children.top_down_role: Separation of feasibility status from objective boundedness status.

assumptions_latex: The OMT instance minimizes \(f:S\to\mathbb{R}\), where \(S=\{x:x\models F\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility, boundedness, and attainment determine distinct solver statuses.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive status distinctions for scalar real-valued minimization.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Exactly one of the following holds: \(S=\varnothing\) (infeasible); \(S
eq\varnothing\) and \(v=-\infty\) (unbounded below); \(S
eq\varnothing\), \(v\in\mathbb{R}\), and some \(x^\star\in S\) satisfies \(f(x^\star)=v\) (finite attained optimum); or \(S
eq\varnothing\), \(v\in\mathbb{R}\), and no feasible model attains \(v\) (finite nonattained infimum). Thus satisfiability alone does not determine boundedness or attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An OMT instance is distinctly infeasible, feasible and unbounded, feasible with an attained finite optimum, or feasible with a nonattained finite infimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility–Boundedness Status Distinctions

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(S=\{x:x\models F\}\) is nonempty, and the minimization objective \(f:S\to\mathbb{R}\) is bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The instance has a finite infimum but no optimal model.

notation.meaning: Nonstrict bound query at the infimum

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of attainment despite feasibility and a finite lower bound.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite nonattained infimum occurs when \(v\in\mathbb{R}\) and \(f(x)>v\) for every \(x\in S\). Equivalently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), the formula \(F(x)\land f(x)<v+\varepsilon\) is satisfiable, whereas \(F(x)\land f(x)\le v\) is unsatisfiable. For example, \(S=\{x\in\mathbb{R}:x>0\}\) with \(f(x)=x\) has infimum \(0\) but no minimizing model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded feasible instance can have a finite infimum approached arbitrarily closely but attained by no feasible model, as when minimizing x over the positive reals.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonattained Optima

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14

children.title: Dense Objective Domains
children.top_down_role: Objective domains containing arbitrarily close distinct values.

assumptions_latex: The feasible objective-value set is \(V=f(S)\subseteq D\), where \(D\) is linearly ordered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objective domain is dense on the feasible range.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-density of attainable values, distinguished from density of the ambient numeric theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The OMT objective has a dense feasible domain when, for every \(a,b\in V\) with \(a<b\), there exists \(c\in V\) satisfying \(a<c<b\). If only the ambient domain \(D\) has this property, density of attainable values does not follow. In particular, a rational- or real-valued objective may have a discrete feasible image, while an infinite feasible image may be dense on an interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible objective values are dense when another attainable value lies strictly between every two distinct attainable values; ambient numeric density alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Objective Domains

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement consistently defines order-density of the attainable image rather than density of the ambient theory domain, and definition fits the leaf. Because density terminology can also mean topological density in an ambient interval, the selected convention needs an inspectable source.

children.title: Infinite Objective Domains
children.top_down_role: Objective domains with unboundedly many candidate values.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set is \(S=\{x:x\models F\}\), and the objective maps \(S\) into an ordered domain \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible objective image is infinite.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinitude of attainable values, not merely an infinite variable domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An OMT objective has an infinite feasible domain precisely when \(|V|=\infty\). This property is distinct from both unboundedness and density: \(V=\mathbb{N}\) is infinite and unbounded but not dense, while \(V=\{1/n:n\in\mathbb{N},\ n\ge1\}\) is infinite and bounded but not dense. Infinitude also does not imply that \(\inf V\) is unattained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective domain is infinite when infinitely many distinct values are attainable; this neither implies density, unboundedness, nor failure to attain an optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Infinite Objective Domains

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cardinality definition and distinctions from density, boundedness, and attainment are mathematically correct, and definition is the appropriate role. No source supports the OMT-specific use of 'objective domain' for the attainable image.

children.title: Dense Infinite-Domain Effects
children.top_down_role: Search and termination pressures arising when density occurs over an infinite domain.

assumptions_latex: The feasible objective values \(V=f(S)\subseteq\mathbb{R}\) are dense in a nondegenerate interval.
An OMT procedure learns only finitely many strict threshold constraints per iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite progress does not by itself imply exact termination or attainment.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination boundary for threshold-based exact optimization over dense infinite values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Density removes any positive minimum gap between distinct feasible values. Consequently, a sequence of satisfiable improvements \(b_{n+1}<b_n\) can be infinite even when bounded below, and an unsatisfiable query at a current value need not arise after finitely many strict improvements. For example, minimizing \(x\) subject to \(0<x\le1\) permits \(b_n=1/n\) indefinitely and has unattained infimum \(0\). Exact termination therefore requires additional structure, such as attainment, symbolic minimization, or a certified discreteness gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense attainable values permit infinitely many strict improvements and nonattained limits, so threshold refinement needs extra structure to guarantee exact finite termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Infinite-Domain Effects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The example validly demonstrates that strict threshold improvement can continue indefinitely over dense attainable values with a nonattained limit, and failure_boundary fits the effects leaf. The broader procedural termination claim depends on the exact OMT refinement scheme and requires an OMT-specific source.

children.title: Weak Objective Bounds
children.top_down_role: Optimization regimes where available bounds prune little of the search space.

assumptions_latex: A minimization OMT procedure maintains a valid lower bound \(L\) and an incumbent upper bound \(U\) with \(L\le v\le U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A large certified gap limits pruning and delays an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar minimization bounds and their effect on search exclusion.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The bound pair certifies only \(L\le v\le U\). Exact optimality follows when \(L=U\); under absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), termination may be declared when \(U-L\le\varepsilon\). A weak lower bound has \(U-L\) large and excludes only objective levels below \(L\). Hence threshold or branch-and-bound reasoning must leave a larger unresolved range, although the precise number of additional SMT calls depends on the bound-selection policy and theory solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak lower bounds leave a large gap to the incumbent, certify little exclusion, and generally enlarge the unresolved range searched by the OMT procedure.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Objective Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

children.title: Repeated SMT Calls
children.top_down_role: Cost accumulation from numerous closely related satisfiability queries.

assumptions_latex: The OMT instance minimizes \(f\) subject to \(F\).
The procedure has an initial incumbent bound \(U_0\) and a rule for choosing stricter thresholds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The last incumbent is returned when the next strict-improvement query is unsatisfiable.

notation.meaning: Incumbent objective upper bound at iteration t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic repeated-call scheme; finite termination depends on threshold policy and objective domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(t=0\) with a feasible incumbent \(x_0\) and \(U_0=f(x_0)\). Choose \(b_t<U_t\) and submit \(Q_t\) to an incremental SMT solver. If \(Q_t\) is satisfiable with model \(x_{t+1}\), set \(U_{t+1}=f(x_{t+1})\), increment \(t\), and repeat. If the exact strict-improvement query \(F(x)\land f(x)<U_t\) is unsatisfiable, output \(x_t\) with its unsatisfiability certificate. Otherwise continue or return the prescribed approximate or unknown status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated OMT calls impose improving objective bounds, replace the incumbent after satisfiable calls, and certify optimality when the exact strict-improvement query is unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.title: Repeated SMT Calls

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The repeated-call scheme is internally consistent and appropriately avoids claiming finite termination for arbitrary threshold policies or dense domains. Algorithm is a suitable role for this procedural leaf, but no inspectable OMT source is supplied.

children.title: Bound–Call Feedback
children.top_down_role: Escalation of solver calls caused by limited progress in objective bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound–Call Feedback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes the interaction between incremental objective bounds and repeated satisfiability calls in minimization OMT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)\) be a theory formula, let \(f(x)\) be minimized, and let \(b^*=\inf\{f(x):F(x)\}\). An iterative OMT procedure makes calls on \(F(x)\land f(x)<b_k\) and, after a satisfiable call returning \(x_k\), sets \(b_{k+1}=f(x_k)<b_k\). If every successful improvement satisfies \(0<b_k-b_{k+1}\leq\delta\), then reaching \(b_N\leq b^*+\varepsilon\) requires \(N\geq\lceil(b_0-b^*-\varepsilon)/\delta\rceil\) successful calls. Its total oracle work is \(W=\sum_{k=0}^{N}C(b_k)\), where \(C(b)\) is the cost of deciding the bounded formula. Thus small bound improvements increase the call count, while expensive tight-bound calls amplify total work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small objective improvements force many bounded SMT calls; if tighter bounds are also harder to decide, their accumulated cost creates a scalability feedback loop.
assumptions_latex: \(F(x)\land f(x)<b_k\) is submitted to a sound theory solver at every iteration.
The procedure minimizes \(f\) and terminates only after obtaining \(b_N\leq b^*+\varepsilon\).
Every successful update improves the bound by at most \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\geq\lceil(b_0-b^*-\varepsilon)/\delta\rceil\) and \(W=\sum_{k=0}^{N}C(b_k)\).

notation.meaning: objective upper bound before call k
cost of deciding the formula under bound b

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but no cited evidence supports this particular bound–call cost model. The indexing also needs correction: reaching b_N through updates b_{k+1} requires N successful calls, whereas W sums N+1 costs from k=0 through N. An authoritative OMT source and a consistent definition of which calls W counts are required.

children.title: Large Unsatisfiable Cores
children.top_down_role: Optimization burdens associated with cores containing many soft constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Large Unsatisfiable Cores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines core size relative to the active soft-constraint population in a core-guided OMT iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be hard constraints and let \(S=\{s_1,\ldots,s_n\}\) be the active soft constraints. A set \(C\subseteq S\) is an unsatisfiable core when \(H\land\bigwedge_{s\in C}s\) is theory-unsatisfiable. For a prescribed scale threshold \(\alpha\in(0,1]\), the core is \(\alpha\)-large when \(|C|\geq\alpha n\). It is inclusion-minimal when every \(s\in C\) satisfies that \(H\land\bigwedge_{t\in C\setminus\{s\}}t\) is satisfiable. Largeness and minimality are independent: a large core need not be minimal, and a minimal core may still contain a linear fraction of all active soft constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unsatisfiable core is large when its cardinality is at least a fixed fraction of all active soft constraints; largeness does not imply minimality.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) and every member of \(S\) belong to the background theory language.
\(S\) is finite and \(n=|S|>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\text{ is }\alpha\text{-large}\iff C\subseteq S,\ H\land\bigwedge_{s\in C}s\text{ is unsatisfiable},\ |C|\geq\alpha n\).

notation.meaning: finite active set of soft constraints
unsatisfiable core drawn from the soft constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf and the core/minimality clauses are mathematically coherent. However, alpha-largeness is a record-specific quantitative convention rather than an established definition demonstrated by evidence, and no core-guided OMT source is cited. A source must support this convention or clearly motivate it as local terminology.

children.title: Overlapping Unsatisfiable Cores
children.top_down_role: Optimization burdens associated with repeated constraint membership across cores.

knowledge_statements.title: Overlapping Unsatisfiable Cores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines pairwise and aggregate overlap for cores generated during core-guided optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_1,
\ldots,C_m\) be unsatisfiable cores over a common finite soft-constraint set \(S\). Two distinct cores overlap when \(C_i\cap C_j\neq\varnothing\); their normalized overlap is the Jaccard coefficient \(J_{ij}=|C_i\cap C_j|/|C_i\cup C_j|\). For each \(s\in S\), define its core multiplicity by \(\mu(s)=|\{i:s\in C_i\}|\). The family has aggregate overlap precisely when some \(\mu(s)\geq2\), equivalently when \(\sum_{i=1}^{m}|C_i|>|\bigcup_{i=1}^{m}C_i|\). The excess incidence count \(R=\sum_i|C_i|-|\bigcup_i C_i|=\sum_{s\in S}\max\{\mu(s)-1,0\}\) measures repeated core membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cores overlap when they share soft constraints. Pairwise Jaccard coefficients and excess incidence count quantify local and aggregate repetition.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a finite soft-constraint set.
\(C_i\subseteq S\) is an unsatisfiable core for each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R>0\iff\exists s\in S:\mu(s)\geq2\iff\exists i\neq j:C_i\cap C_j\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Jaccard overlap of cores i and j
number of cores containing soft constraint s

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf, and the incidence identity is correct. The selected Jaccard and excess-incidence metrics lack cited support. Moreover, J_ij is undefined when C_i and C_j are both empty, which is possible if the hard constraints are already inconsistent unless nonempty cores or a denominator convention is imposed.

children.title: Core-Overlap Scalability
children.top_down_role: Resource effects produced by overlap among large core families.

knowledge_statements.title: Core-Overlap Scalability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies unavoidable incidence-processing work when a core-guided implementation scans each returned core independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) be returned unsatisfiable cores, let \(U=\bigcup_{i=1}^{m}C_i\), and let \(V=\sum_{i=1}^{m}|C_i|\). In an explicit-incidence model where processing a core reads every one of its members once, the total core-processing time is \(\Theta(V)\) and the stored incidence volume is \(\Theta(V)\). Writing \(\rho=V/|U|\) for \(U\neq\varnothing\), this becomes \(\Theta(\rho|U|)\). Hence repeated membership creates a multiplicative overhead \(\rho\) relative to one-pass processing of the distinct constraints; no implementation in this model can achieve \(o(V)\) time without avoiding or compressing incidence reads.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent scanning costs linear time in total core incidences. Overlap multiplies this cost by the average number of core occurrences per distinct constraint.
assumptions_latex: Every returned core is represented as an explicit list of its members.
The processing operation inspects each listed incidence at least once.
\(U\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T=\Theta(V)=\Theta(\rho|U|)\), where \(V=\sum_i|C_i|\) and \(\rho=V/|U|\geq1\).

notation.meaning: total number of listed core incidences

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A complexity bound is the correct role for this leaf, and Theta(V) time follows under the explicit mandatory-scan model. The simultaneous Theta(V) storage claim additionally requires retaining all explicit core lists, which the assumptions do not state unambiguously. No source supports the model or its relevance to core-guided OMT scalability.

knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Optimization-Theory Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines incompleteness of theory oracles used to answer bounded feasibility queries inside OMT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Q\) be a class of bounded optimization-theory queries and let an oracle return \(\mathsf{SAT}(x)\), \(\mathsf{UNSAT}(c)\), or \(\mathsf{UNKNOWN}\), where \(x\) is a verifiable model and \(c\) is a verifiable refutation certificate. The oracle is sound if its first two answers certify the corresponding truth values. It is complete on \(\mathcal Q\) if it terminates with one of those two conclusive answers for every \(q\in\mathcal Q\); otherwise it is incomplete. Thus incompleteness occurs when some query in \(\mathcal Q\) yields \(\mathsf{UNKNOWN}\) or nontermination, and an OMT procedure relying solely on that response cannot soundly infer feasibility, infeasibility, or optimality for the affected bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sound theory oracle is incomplete when some bounded query returns unknown or fails to terminate, preventing a conclusive OMT status from that response alone.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal Q\) is a specified class of theory queries.
Models and refutation certificates are independently checkable.
The oracle's conclusive answers are sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{incomplete on }\mathcal Q\iff\exists q\in\mathcal Q\text{ for which the oracle returns }\mathsf{UNKNOWN}\text{ or does not terminate}.\)

notation.meaning: conclusive satisfiable answer with model x
conclusive unsatisfiable answer with certificate c

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role is suitable, but the exact notion of completeness depends on a custom three-result, certificate-producing oracle interface. Standard SMT completeness does not inherently require every conclusive answer to carry the stated independently checkable certificate. An authoritative SMT/OMT source is needed to establish the intended oracle model and resulting failure boundary.
